ex.en: How did he come to break his leg?
ex.cn: 他怎么把腿弄断的？

ex.en: How do you come to be so late?
ex.cn: 你怎么这么晚？

senses.def: to have a particular position

ex.en: That comes a long way down my list of priorities.
ex.cn: 在我的优先事项中，那事远没那么紧要。

ex.en: His family comes first (= is the most important thing in his life).
ex.cn: 他把家庭放在首位。

ex.en: She came second (= received the second highest score) in the exam.
ex.cn: 她这次考试名列第二。

senses.def: used in many expressions to show that sth has reached a particular state
senses.chn: （用于许多词组）达到，进入（某种状态）

ex.en: At last winter came to an end.
ex.cn: 冬天终于结束了。

ex.en: He came to power in 2006.
ex.cn: 他于 2006 年上台执政。

ex.en: When will they come to a decision?
ex.cn: 他们何时会作出决定？

ex.en: The trees are coming into leaf.
ex.cn: 树开始长叶子了。

senses.def: to be available or to exist in a particular way

ex.en: This dress comes in black and red.
ex.cn: 这款连衣裙有黑、红两种颜色。

ex.en: New cars don't come cheap (= they are expensive).
ex.cn: 新汽车没有便宜的。

senses.def: to become

ex.en: The buttons had come undone.
ex.cn: 纽扣都松开了。

ex.en: The handle came loose.
ex.cn: 这把手松了。

ex.en: Everything will come right in the end.
ex.cn: 一切到最后都会好起来的。

ex.en: This design came to be known as the Oriental style.
ex.cn: 这种设计后来被称为东方风格。

senses.def: to reach a point where you realize, understand or believe sth
senses.chn: 达到（认识、理解或相信的程度）

ex.en: In time she came to love him.
ex.cn: 她终于爱上了他。

ex.en: She had come to see the problem in a new light.
ex.cn: 她开始从新的角度来看待这个问题。

ex.en: I've come to expect this kind of behaviour from him.
ex.cn: 对于他的这种举止我渐渐不感到意外了。

senses.def: to have an orgasm
to be very clever, stupid, etc.
used to ask sb to repeat sth
senses.chn: （要求重复）再说一遍，你说什么来着

ex.en: 'She's an entomologist.' 'Come again?' 'An entomologist—she studies insects.'
ex.cn: “她是昆虫学家。” “请再说一遍？” “昆虫学家，她是研究昆虫的。”

senses.def: to arrive and leave; to move freely

ex.en: They had a party next door—we heard people coming and going all night.
ex.cn: 他们在隔壁聚会，我们整夜都听见人来人往的声音。

senses.def: to be present for a short time and then go away

ex.en: The pain in my leg comes and goes.
ex.cn: 我的腿时而疼时而不疼。

senses.def: to be easy, natural, etc. for sb to do
senses.chn: （对某人而言）轻而易举（或生来就会等）

ex.en: Acting comes naturally to her.
ex.cn: 她天生就会表演。

senses.def: to suddenly feel ill/sick or faint
senses.chn: 突然感到昏眩（或眩晕、头晕等）

senses.def: to play the part of a particular type of person; to behave in a particular way
senses.chn: 扮演（某类人）；以（某种方式）行事

ex.en: Don't come the innocent with me.
ex.cn: 别跟我扮无辜。

senses.def: to be unsuccessful; to have no successful result

ex.en: How sad that all his hard work should come to nothing.
ex.cn: 他的所有辛勤劳动竟全部付诸东流，太让人伤心了。

ex.en: Her plans didn't come to anything.
ex.cn: 她的计划全落空了。

senses.def: used to introduce sth extra that is connected with what has just been said
senses.chn: （引出与刚提及的事物相关的事）说起…来，既然如此，假如那样的话

ex.en: I don't really trust him—nor his wife, come to that.
ex.cn: 我不太信任他。说起信任，我也不信任他的妻子。

senses.def: despite any problems or difficulties you may have
senses.chn: 不管出现什么问题；无论有什么困难；不管怎样

ex.en: He promised to support her come what may.
ex.cn: 他答应不管出现什么问题都支持她。

senses.def: used to say you do not understand how sth can happen and would like an explanation
senses.chn: （用以表示不理解情况是如何发生的，希望得到解释）怎么回事，怎么发生的，怎样解释

ex.en: 'I think you owe me some money.' 'How come?'
ex.cn: “你好像欠我钱。” “怎么会呢？”

ex.en: If she spent five years in Paris, how come her French is so bad?
ex.cn: 既然她在巴黎待了五年，她的法语怎么还会这样糟糕？

senses.def: to not be important or successful
senses.chn: 不重要；无关紧要；不成功

senses.def: in the future

ex.en: They may well regret the decision in years to come.
ex.cn: 他们过几年之后很可能会为这个决定而后悔。

ex.en: This will be a problem for some time to come (= for a period of time in the future).
ex.cn: 这将是未来一段时期里的一个问题。

senses.def: when it is a question of sth
senses.chn: 当涉及某事（或做某事）时

ex.en: When it comes to getting things done, he's useless.
ex.cn: 一涉及做事，他便不中用了。

senses.def: somebody's ideas, beliefs, personality, etc. that makes them say what they have said
senses.chn: （决定某人言论的）某人的全部背景

ex.en: I see where you're coming from (= I understand what you mean).
ex.cn: 我明白你究竟是什么意思。

senses.def: to happen

ex.en: Can you tell me how the accident came about?
ex.cn: 你能告诉我事故是怎样发生的吗？

senses.def: to be understood

ex.en: He spoke for a long time but his meaning didn't really come across.
ex.cn: 他讲了很久，但并没有人真正理解他的意思。

senses.def: to make a particular impression
senses.chn: 给人以…印象；使产生…印象

ex.en: She comes across well in interviews.
ex.cn: 她在面试中常给人留下很好的印象。

ex.en: He came over as a sympathetic person.
ex.cn: 他给人的印象是一个富有同情心的人。

senses.def: to meet or find sb/sth by chance

ex.en: I came across children sleeping under bridges.
ex.cn: 我偶然发现睡在桥下的孩子。

ex.en: She came across some old photographs in a drawer.
ex.cn: 她在抽屉里偶然发现了一些旧照片。

senses.def: to provide or supply sth when you need it

ex.en: I hoped she'd come across with some more information.
ex.cn: 我希望她能再提供更多的信息。

senses.def: to chase or follow sb
to arrive; to appear

ex.en: When the right opportunity comes along, she'll take it.
ex.cn: 适当的机会来临时，她会抓住的。

senses.def: to go somewhere with sb

ex.en: I'm glad you came along.
ex.cn: 有你跟我一起来，我很高兴。

senses.def: to improve or develop in the way that you want

ex.en: Your French has come along a lot recently.
ex.cn: 你的法语最近进步很大。

senses.def: used in orders to tell sb to hurry, or to try harder

ex.en: Come along! We're late.
ex.cn: 快点！我们迟到了。

ex.en: Come along! It's easy!
ex.cn: 再加把劲！这很容易！

senses.def: to break into pieces

ex.en: The book just came apart in my hands.
ex.cn: 这本书就在我手中散开了。

ex.en: My whole life had come apart at the seams.
ex.cn: 我的整个生活都崩溃了。

senses.def: to become conscious again

ex.en: Your mother hasn't yet come round from the anaesthetic.
ex.cn: 你的母亲麻醉后还没有苏醒过来。

senses.def: to happen again

ex.en: My birthday seems to come around quicker every year.
ex.cn: 我的生日似乎一年比一年来得快。

senses.def: to come to a place, especially sb's house, to visit for a short time
senses.chn: 短暂访问（尤指某人的家）

ex.en: Do come around and see us some time.
ex.cn: 务必抽空来看看我们。

senses.def: to change your mood or your opinion

ex.en: He'll never come round to our way of thinking.
ex.cn: 他绝不会改变观点与我们的思路一致。

senses.def: to move towards sb as though you are going to attack them

ex.en: She came at me with a knife.
ex.cn: 她拿着刀子向我扑过来。

ex.en: The noise came at us from all sides.
ex.cn: 噪音从四面八方向我们袭来。

senses.def: to think about a problem, question, etc. in a particular way

ex.en: We're getting nowhere—let's come at it from another angle.
ex.cn: 我们这样会毫无进展，还是换个角度考虑一下吧。

senses.def: to become separated from sth

ex.en: The plaster had started to come away from the wall.
ex.cn: 灰泥已开始从墙上剥落。

senses.def: to leave a place with a particular feeling or impression

ex.en: We came away with the impression that all was not well with their marriage.
ex.cn: 我们离开时有一种印象：他们的婚姻并不十分美满。

senses.def: to return

ex.en: You came back (= came home) very late last night.
ex.cn: 你昨晚回来得很晚。

ex.en: The colour was coming back to her cheeks.
ex.cn: 她的双颊又泛起了红晕。

ex.en: United came back from being two goals down to win 3–2.
ex.cn: 联队在先失两球的情况下将比分扳回，最终以 3:2 取胜。

ex.en: I waited a long time for him to return.
ex.cn: 我等他回来等了很长时间。

ex.en: Come back and visit again soon!
ex.cn: 请早点儿再回来探访！

ex.en: Do you ever want to go back to China?
ex.cn: 你想过回中国去吗？

senses.def: to become popular or successful again

ex.en: Long hair for men seems to be coming back in.
ex.cn: 男子留长发好像又在流行了。

senses.def: to reply to sb angrily or with force
senses.chn: 强有力地（或愤怒地）答复；反驳

ex.en: She came back at the speaker with some sharp questions.
ex.cn: 她用一些尖锐的提问来反驳讲话人。

senses.def: to return to sb's memory

ex.en: It's all coming back to me now.
ex.cn: 现在我全都回想起来了。

ex.en: Once you've been in France a few days, your French will soon come back.
ex.cn: 只要在法国待上几天，你的法语就会很快恢复起来。

senses.def: to return to a subject, an idea, etc.

ex.en: Let's come back to the point at issue.
ex.cn: 咱们还是回到问题的焦点吧。

ex.en: It all comes back to a question of money.
ex.cn: 一切又回到钱的问题上来了。

senses.def: to be presented to sb/sth for discussion or a decision
senses.chn: 被提交给…讨论（或作决定）

ex.en: The case comes before the court next week.
ex.cn: 这案件在下周庭审。

senses.def: to damage a relationship between two people

ex.en: I'd hate anything to come between us.
ex.cn: 我不喜欢任何有损我们之间关系的事情。

senses.def: to make a short visit to a place, in order to see sb

ex.en: She came by the house.
ex.cn: 她来家里看了一下。

senses.def: to manage to get sth

ex.en: Jobs are hard to come by these days.
ex.cn: 如今找工作很难。

senses.def: to receive sth

ex.en: How did you come by that scratch on your cheek?
ex.cn: 你脸颊上的抓伤是怎么来的？

senses.def: to break and fall to the ground

ex.en: The ceiling came down with a terrific crash.
ex.cn: 随着一声可怕的巨响，天花板塌了下来。

senses.def: to fall

ex.en: The rain came down in torrents.
ex.cn: 大雨滂沱。

senses.def: to land or fall from the sky

ex.en: We were forced to come down in a field.
ex.cn: 我们被迫降落在田野里。

senses.def: if a price, a temperature, a rate, etc. comes down, it gets lower

ex.en: The price of gas is coming down.
ex.cn: 煤气价格在下跌。

ex.en: Gas is coming down in price.
ex.cn: 煤气价格在下跌。

senses.def: to decide and say publicly that you support or oppose sb
senses.chn: 决定并宣布（支持或反对）

ex.en: The committee came down in support of his application.
ex.cn: 委员会决定并宣布支持他的申请。

senses.def: to reach as far down as a particular point
senses.chn: 下垂，向下延伸（到某一点）

ex.en: Her hair comes down to her waist.
ex.cn: 她的头发垂至腰部。

senses.def: to leave a university, especially Oxford or Cambridge, at the end of a term or after finishing your studies
senses.chn: （尤指在牛津或剑桥期末或学业结束后）离开大学，大学毕业

senses.def: to come from one place to another, usually from the north of a country to the south, or from a larger place to a smaller one
senses.chn: 从…到…（通常指从一国的北部到南部，或从大地方到小地方）

senses.def: to criticize sb severely or punish sb

ex.en: Don't come down too hard on her.
ex.cn: 不要太严厉地责备她。

ex.en: The courts are coming down heavily on young offenders.
ex.cn: 法庭对年轻罪犯实行严惩。

senses.def: to have come from a long time in the past

ex.en: The name has come down from the last century.
ex.cn: 这名称是从上个世纪流传下来的。

senses.def: to be able to be explained by a single important point

ex.en: What it comes down to is either I get more money or I leave.
ex.cn: 归结起来就是：不给我加薪，我就辞职。

senses.def: to get an illness that is not very serious

ex.en: I think I'm coming down with flu.
ex.cn: 我想我得了流感。

senses.def: to offer your help, services, etc.
senses.chn: 主动提供（帮助或服务等）

ex.en: Several people came forward with information.
ex.cn: 有几个人自动站出来提供了信息。

ex.en: Police have asked witnesses of the accident to come forward.
ex.cn: 警方呼吁事故的目击者出来提供线索。

senses.def: to have as your place of birth or the place where you live

ex.en: She comes from London.
ex.cn: 她是伦敦人。

ex.en: Where do you come from?
ex.cn: 你是什么地方的人？

senses.def: to start in a particular place or be produced from a particular thing

ex.en: Much of our butter comes from New Zealand.
ex.cn: 我们的黄油大多产自新西兰。

ex.en: This wool comes from goats, not sheep.
ex.cn: 这种羊毛是山羊毛，不是绵羊毛。

ex.en: This poem comes from his new book.
ex.cn: 这首诗出自他的新书。

ex.en: Where does her attitude come from?
ex.cn: 她的态度因何而起？

ex.en: Where's that smell coming from?
ex.cn: 那种气味是哪里来的？

ex.en: He comes from a family of actors.
ex.cn: 他出身于演员世家。

senses.def: when the tide comes in, it moves towards the land
to finish a race in a particular position

ex.en: My horse came in last.
ex.cn: 我的马跑了最后一名。

senses.def: to become fashionable

ex.en: Long hair for men came in in the sixties.
ex.cn: 男子留长发在 60 年代流行开来。

senses.def: to become available

ex.en: We're still waiting for copies of the book to come in.
ex.cn: 我们仍然在等这本书进货。

senses.def: to have a part in sth

ex.en: I understand the plan perfectly, but I can't see where I come in.
ex.cn: 我完全了解这项计划，可是不明白我能起什么作用。

senses.def: to arrive somewhere; to be received

ex.en: The train is coming in now.
ex.cn: 火车现正进站。

ex.en: News is coming in of a serious plane crash in France.
ex.cn: 刚收到的消息说法国发生了一起严重的飞机坠毁事故。

ex.en: She has over a thousand pounds a month coming in from her investments.
ex.cn: 她每月从自己的投资中得到超过一千英镑的收入。

senses.def: to take part in a discussion

ex.en: Would you like to come in at this point, Susan?
ex.cn: 苏珊，你愿意在此刻发表意见吗？

senses.def: to be introduced; to begin to be used
to receive sth, especially sth unpleasant

ex.en: The government's economic policies have come in for a lot of criticism.
ex.cn: 政府的经济政策遭到了很多批评。

senses.def: to become involved in sth

ex.en: If you want to come in on the deal, you need to decide now.
ex.cn: 如果你要做这笔交易，你得现在作出决定。

senses.def: to be left money by sb who has died

ex.en: She came into a fortune when her uncle died.
ex.cn: 她在叔叔去世后继承了一大笔财产。

senses.def: to be important in a particular situation

ex.en: I've worked very hard to pass this exam—luck doesn't come into it.
ex.cn: 我为通过这次考试下了很大的苦功，运气不是主要的。

senses.def: to be the result of sth

ex.en: I made a few enquiries, but nothing came of it in the end.
ex.cn: 我做过一些查询，但到头来却毫无结果。

ex.en: That comes of eating too much!
ex.cn: 那是吃得太多的结果！

senses.def: to be able to be removed

ex.en: Does this hood come off?
ex.cn: 这风帽能卸下来吗？

ex.en: That mark won't come off.
ex.cn: 那污点去不掉。

senses.def: to take place; to happen

ex.en: Did the trip to Rome ever come off?
ex.cn: 去罗马的事最后成了吗？

senses.def: to be successful; to have the intended effect or result
senses.chn: 成功；达到预期效果（或结果）

ex.en: They had wanted it to be a surprise but the plan didn't come off.
ex.cn: 他们本想一鸣惊人，然而计划却流产了。

senses.def: to be successful/not successful in a fight, contest, etc.

ex.en: I thought they came off very well in the debate.
ex.cn: 我认为他们在辩论中表现非常出色。

senses.def: to fall from sth

ex.en: to come off your bicycle/horse
ex.cn: 从自行车／马上跌下

senses.def: to become separated from sth

ex.en: When I tried to lift the jug, the handle came off in my hand.
ex.cn: 我刚想提起水壶，壶把子就掉在我的手中了。

ex.en: A button had come off my coat.
ex.cn: 我的外套掉了一颗纽扣。

senses.def: used to disagree with sb rudely
senses.chn: （粗鲁地表示不同意）别胡扯，别胡说，住口

ex.en: Come off it! We don't have a chance.
ex.cn: 别胡扯了！我们没机会。

senses.def: to stop taking medicine, a drug, alcohol, etc.

ex.en: I've tried to get him to come off the tranquillizers.
ex.cn: 我试图说服他停止服用镇静剂。

senses.def: to walk onto the stage
to join a team during a game

ex.en: Owen came on for Brown ten minutes before the end of the game.
ex.cn: 终场前十分钟，欧文上场替换了布朗。

senses.def: to improve or develop in the way you want

ex.en: The project is coming on fine.
ex.cn: 这项工程进展顺利。

senses.def: used in orders to tell sb to hurry or to try harder

ex.en: Come on! We don't have much time.
ex.cn: 快点！我们时间不多了。

ex.en: Come on! Try once more.
ex.cn: 加把劲！再试一次。

senses.def: used to show that you know what sb has said is not correct
senses.chn: （表示知道某人所说的话不正确）得了吧

ex.en: Oh, come on—you know that isn't true!
ex.cn: 咳，得了吧，你知道那不是真的！

senses.def: to begin

ex.en: I can feel a cold coming on.
ex.cn: 我觉得要感冒了。

ex.en: I think there's rain coming on.
ex.cn: 我看要下雨了。

ex.en: It came on to rain.
ex.cn: 天下起雨来了。

senses.def: to start

ex.en: What time does the news come on?
ex.cn: 新闻报道什么时候开始？

senses.def: to begin to operate

ex.en: Set the oven to come on at six.
ex.cn: 把烤箱设定在六点钟开始烘烤。

ex.en: When does the heating come on?
ex.cn: 什么时间来暖气？

senses.def: to meet or find sb/sth by chance
to behave in a way that shows sb that you want to have a sexual relationship with them
senses.chn: 勾引，勾搭（想与其发生性关系）

senses.def: to start talking about a subject

ex.en: I'd like to come on to that question later.
ex.cn: 我想稍后再讨论那个问题。

senses.def: when the sun, moon or stars come out, they appear

ex.en: The rain stopped and the sun came out.
ex.cn: 雨停后太阳出来了。

senses.def: to open

ex.en: The daffodils came out early this year.
ex.cn: 水仙花今年开得早。

senses.def: to be produced or published

ex.en: When is her new novel coming out?
ex.cn: 她的新小说何时出版？

senses.def: to become known

ex.en: The full story came out at the trial.
ex.cn: 案情始末在审判时真相大白。

ex.en: It came out that he'd been telling lies.
ex.cn: 后来才知道他一直在说谎。

senses.def: if a photograph comes out, it is a clear picture when it is developed and printed

ex.en: Some of the photos from our trip didn't come out.
ex.cn: 我们旅行的一些照片冲洗的效果不好。

senses.def: to be shown clearly

ex.en: Her best qualities come out in a crisis.
ex.cn: 她的优秀品质在危难之际显示了出来。

senses.def: when words come out, they are spoken

ex.en: I tried to say 'I love you,' but the words wouldn't come out.
ex.cn: 我想说 “我爱你”，但这话怎么也说不出口。

senses.def: to say publicly whether you agree or disagree with sth
senses.chn: 公开表明（同意或不同意）

ex.en: He came out against the plan.
ex.cn: 他公开表示反对这个计划。

ex.en: In her speech, the senator came out in favour of a change in the law.
ex.cn: 这位参议员在她的讲话中公开赞成修改法律。

senses.def: to stop work and go on strike
to no longer hide the fact that you are homosexual
senses.chn: 不再隐瞒自己是同性恋者的事实；公开表明自己是同性恋者；“出柜”

senses.def: to be formally introduced into society
to be removed from a place where it is fixed

ex.en: This nail won't come out.
ex.cn: 这颗钉子拔不出来。

senses.def: to be removed from sth by washing or cleaning

ex.en: These ink stains won't come out of my dress.
ex.cn: 我衣服上的这些墨水斑点洗不掉。

ex.en: Will the colour come out (= become faint or disappear) if I wash it?
ex.cn: 我若用水洗，它会掉色吗？

senses.def: to add up to a particular cost or sum

ex.en: The total bill comes out at £500.
ex.cn: 账单金额总计为 500 英镑。

senses.def: to become covered in spots, etc. on the skin

ex.en: Hot weather makes her come out in a rash.
ex.cn: 炎热的天气使她起了皮疹。

senses.def: to relax and become more confident and friendly with other people
senses.chn: 精神放松、更加自信和友好地与他人交往

ex.en: It was when she started drama classes that she really came out of herself.
ex.cn: 她是在开始学习戏剧课程时才真正不再害羞。

senses.def: to develop from sth

ex.en: The book came out of his experiences in India.
ex.cn: 这本书取材于他在印度的经历。

ex.en: Rock music came out of the blues.
ex.cn: 摇滚乐起源于布鲁斯音乐。

senses.def: to say sth, especially sth surprising or rude
senses.chn: 说出（尤指令人吃惊或粗鲁的话）

ex.en: He came out with a stream of abuse.
ex.cn: 他讲了一连串的脏话。

ex.en: She sometimes comes out with the most extraordinary remarks.
ex.cn: 她有时说起话来语惊四座。

senses.def: to suddenly feel sth

ex.en: to come over funny/dizzy/faint
ex.cn: 突然感到可笑／眩晕／昏眩

ex.en: I come over all shy whenever I see her.
ex.cn: 我每次看到她时都会突然感到很害羞。

senses.def: to come to a place, especially sb's house, to visit for a short time
to travel from one place to another, usually over a long distance

ex.en: Why don't you come over to England in the summer?
ex.cn: 你为何不在夏天来英格兰呢？

ex.en: Her grandparents came over from Ireland during the famine.
ex.cn: 她的祖父母是在饥荒时期从爱尔兰迁移过来的。

senses.def: to change from one side, opinion, etc. to another
to affect sb

ex.en: A fit of dizziness came over her.
ex.cn: 她感到一阵头晕目眩。

ex.en: I can't think what came over me (= I do not know what caused me to behave in that way).
ex.cn: 我不知道我是怎么了。

senses.def: to arrive by telephone, radio, etc. or through an official organization
senses.chn: （用电话、无线电等或由官方机构）传来

ex.en: A message is just coming through.
ex.cn: 刚有消息传来。

senses.def: to get better after a serious illness or to avoid serious injury
senses.chn: （重病后）康复；避免受严重伤害

ex.en: With such a weak heart she was lucky to come through the operation.
ex.cn: 她的心脏很弱，手术后能活下来真是幸运。

senses.def: to successfully do or complete sth that you have promised to do

ex.en: We were worried she wouldn't be able to handle it, but she came through in the end.
ex.cn: 我们担心她没有能力处理那件事，然而她最终说到做到了。

ex.en: The bank finally came through with the money.
ex.cn: 这家银行终于兑现了那笔钱。

senses.def: to return to your normal state
to enter your mind

ex.en: The idea came to me in the bath.
ex.cn: 我泡澡时想出了这个主意。

ex.en: It suddenly came to her that she had been wrong all along.
ex.cn: 她突然意识到她一开始就错了。

senses.def: to add up to sth

ex.en: The bill came to $30.
ex.cn: 账单金额总计为 30 美元。

ex.en: I never expected those few items to come to so much.
ex.cn: 我根本没想到就那么几件东西合计起来竟要花这么多钱。

senses.def: to reach a particular situation, especially a bad one
senses.chn: 达到（某状况，尤指坏的局面）

ex.en: The doctors will operate if necessary—but it may not come to that.
ex.cn: 必要时医生会施行手术，但也许还不至于此。

ex.en: Who'd have thought things would come to this (= become so bad)?
ex.cn: 谁会想到事情竟会变成这个样子？

senses.def: if two or more different people or things come together, they form a united group

ex.en: Three colleges have come together to create a new university.
ex.cn: 三所学院合并成了一所新的大学。

ex.en: Bits and pieces of things he'd read and heard were coming together, and he began to understand.
ex.cn: 他把读到和听到的零碎片段综合起来，便逐渐明白了。

senses.def: to be included in a particular group

ex.en: What heading does this come under?
ex.cn: 这该归入哪一个主题？

senses.def: to be a person that others are attacking or criticizing
senses.chn: 成为（攻击或批评的）目标

ex.en: The head teacher came under a lot of criticism from the parents.
ex.cn: 校长受到了家长的很多批评。

senses.def: to be controlled or influenced by sth

ex.en: All her students came under her spell.
ex.cn: 她所有的学生都被她迷住了。

senses.def: to appear above the soil

ex.en: The daffodils are just beginning to come up.
ex.cn: 那些水仙花刚开始破土发芽。

senses.def: to rise

ex.en: We watched the sun come up.
ex.cn: 我们观看了日出。

senses.def: to happen

ex.en: I'm afraid something urgent has come up.
ex.cn: 恐怕有紧急事情发生。

ex.en: We'll let you know if any vacancies come up.
ex.cn: 一有空缺，我们就会通知你。

senses.def: to be mentioned or discussed

ex.en: The subject came up in conversation.
ex.cn: 谈话中提到了这个话题。

ex.en: The question is bound to come up at the meeting.
ex.cn: 会上一定会讨论这个问题。

senses.def: to be going to happen very soon

ex.en: Her birthday is coming up soon.
ex.cn: 她的生日就快到了。

senses.def: to be dealt with by a court

ex.en: Her divorce case comes up next month.
ex.cn: 她的离婚案在下月审理。

senses.def: if your number, name, ticket, etc. comes up in a betting game, it is chosen and you win sth
senses.chn: （在博彩游戏中指号码、名字、奖券等）被抽中，中奖

senses.def: to arrive; to be ready soon

ex.en: 'Is lunch ready?' 'Coming up!'
ex.cn: “午餐准备好了吗？” “马上就好！”

senses.def: to arrive at a university, especially Oxford or Cambridge, at the beginning of a term or in order to begin your studies
senses.chn: （尤指在牛津或剑桥学期开学时）到校上学

senses.def: to come from one place to another, especially from the south of a country to the north or from a smaller place to a larger one
senses.chn: （从…）上到…（通常指从一国的南部到北部，或从小地方到大地方）

ex.en: Why don't you come up to Scotland for a few days?
ex.cn: 你为何不上苏格兰来住几天？

senses.def: to move towards sb, in order to talk to them

ex.en: He came up to me and asked me the way to the station.
ex.cn: 他走到我跟前打听去车站的路。

senses.def: to be faced with or opposed by sb/sth

ex.en: We expect to come up against a lot of opposition to the plan.
ex.cn: 我们预料这个计划会遭到很多人的反对。

senses.def: to be considered for a job, an important position, etc.

ex.en: She comes up for re-election next year.
ex.cn: 她明年将再度参加竞选。

senses.def: to be reaching the time when sth must be done

ex.en: His contract is coming up for renewal.
ex.cn: 他的合同快到续订期了。

senses.def: to reach as far as a particular point

ex.en: The water came up to my neck.
ex.cn: 水淹到了我的脖子。

senses.def: to reach an acceptable level or standard
senses.chn: 达到（认可的水平或标准）

ex.en: His performance didn't really come up to his usual high standard.
ex.cn: 他的表现没有真正达到他往常的高水平。

ex.en: Their trip to France didn't come up to expectations.
ex.cn: 他们的法国之行未尽如人意。

senses.def: to find or produce an answer, a sum of money, etc.
senses.chn: 找到（答案）；拿出（一笔钱等）

ex.en: She came up with a new idea for increasing sales.
ex.cn: 她想出了增加销售量的新主意。

ex.en: How soon can you come up with the money?
ex.cn: 你什么时候能拿出这笔钱？

senses.def: when the time mentioned comes

ex.en: They would have been married forty years come this June.
ex.cn: 到今年六月他们结婚就有四十年了。

senses.def: used when encouraging sb to be sensible or reasonable, or when showing slight disapproval
senses.chn: （鼓励某人要有理智或通情达理，或表示不太赞同）嗨，得啦，好啦

ex.en: Oh come now, things aren't as bad as all that.
ex.cn: 哦，好啦，情况并不是那么糟。

ex.en: Come, come, Miss Jones, you know perfectly well what I mean.
ex.cn: 得啦，得啦，琼斯小姐，你完全知道我的意思。

senses.def: semen
to fall over
to have a failure or near disaster

ex.en: We nearly came a cropper in the second half of the game.
ex.cn: 在比赛的下半场我们差一点就输掉了。

senses.def: to be understood

ex.en: He spoke for a long time but his meaning didn't really come across.
ex.cn: 他讲了很久，但并没有人真正理解他的意思。

senses.def: to make a particular impression
senses.chn: 给人以…印象；使产生…印象

ex.en: She comes across well in interviews.
ex.cn: 她在面试中常给人留下很好的印象。

ex.en: He came over as a sympathetic person.
ex.cn: 他给人的印象是一个富有同情心的人。

senses.def: to chase or follow sb
to fail or be defeated
to become interesting and exciting

ex.en: The game came alive in the second half.
ex.cn: 比赛在下半场变得有看头了。

senses.def: to become busy and full of activity

ex.en: The city starts to come alive after dark.
ex.cn: 这座城市天黑以后便热闹起来。

senses.def: to show interest in sth and become excited about it

ex.en: She came alive as she talked about her job.
ex.cn: 她一谈到她的工作精神就来了。

senses.def: to arrive; to appear

ex.en: When the right opportunity comes along, she'll take it.
ex.cn: 适当的机会来临时，她会抓住的。

senses.def: to go somewhere with sb

ex.en: I'm glad you came along.
ex.cn: 有你跟我一起来，我很高兴。

senses.def: to improve or develop in the way that you want

ex.en: Your French has come along a lot recently.
ex.cn: 你的法语最近进步很大。

senses.def: used in orders to tell sb to hurry, or to try harder

ex.en: Come along! We're late.
ex.cn: 快点！我们迟到了。

ex.en: Come along! It's easy!
ex.cn: 再加把劲！这很容易！

senses.def: to arrive and leave; to move freely

ex.en: They had a party next door—we heard people coming and going all night.
ex.cn: 他们在隔壁聚会，我们整夜都听见人来人往的声音。

senses.def: to be present for a short time and then go away

ex.en: The pain in my leg comes and goes.
ex.cn: 我的腿时而疼时而不疼。

senses.def: to break into pieces

ex.en: The book just came apart in my hands.
ex.cn: 这本书就在我手中散开了。

ex.en: My whole life had come apart at the seams.
ex.cn: 我的整个生活都崩溃了。

senses.def: to move towards sb as though you are going to attack them

ex.en: She came at me with a knife.
ex.cn: 她拿着刀子向我扑过来。

ex.en: The noise came at us from all sides.
ex.cn: 噪音从四面八方向我们袭来。

senses.def: to think about a problem, question, etc. in a particular way

ex.en: We're getting nowhere—let's come at it from another angle.
ex.cn: 我们这样会毫无进展，还是换个角度考虑一下吧。

senses.def: to leave a place with a particular feeling or impression

ex.en: We came away with the impression that all was not well with their marriage.
ex.cn: 我们离开时有一种印象：他们的婚姻并不十分美满。

senses.def: if a person in public life makes a comeback, they start doing sth again which they had stopped doing, or they become popular again

ex.en: an ageing pop star trying to stage a comeback
ex.cn: 试图重返歌坛的已经上了年纪的流行音乐歌星

senses.def: if a thing makes a comeback, it becomes popular and fashionable or successful again
senses.chn: 再度流行并变得时髦；再度获得成功

senses.def: a quick reply to a critical remark
senses.chn: （对批评迅速作出的）反驳，回应

senses.def: a way of holding sb responsible for sth wrong which has been done to you
senses.chn: 可因自身受到伤害而追究某人的责任

ex.en: You agreed to the contract, so now you have no comeback.
ex.cn: 你同意了这份合同，所以现在你不能追究他人的责任了。

senses.def: to return

ex.en: You came back (= came home) very late last night.
ex.cn: 你昨晚回来得很晚。

ex.en: The colour was coming back to her cheeks.
ex.cn: 她的双颊又泛起了红晕。

ex.en: United came back from being two goals down to win 3–2.
ex.cn: 联队在先失两球的情况下将比分扳回，最终以 3:2 取胜。

ex.en: I waited a long time for him to return.
ex.cn: 我等他回来等了很长时间。

ex.en: Come back and visit again soon!
ex.cn: 请早点儿再回来探访！

ex.en: Do you ever want to go back to China?
ex.cn: 你想过回中国去吗？

senses.def: to become popular or successful again

ex.en: Long hair for men seems to be coming back in.
ex.cn: 男子留长发好像又在流行了。

senses.def: to return to a subject, an idea, etc.

ex.en: Let's come back to the point at issue.
ex.cn: 咱们还是回到问题的焦点吧。

ex.en: It all comes back to a question of money.
ex.cn: 一切又回到钱的问题上来了。

senses.def: to damage a relationship between two people

ex.en: I'd hate anything to come between us.
ex.cn: 我不喜欢任何有损我们之间关系的事情。

senses.def: to manage to get sth

ex.en: Jobs are hard to come by these days.
ex.cn: 如今找工作很难。

senses.def: to receive sth

ex.en: How did you come by that scratch on your cheek?
ex.cn: 你脸颊上的抓伤是怎么来的？

senses.def: an entertainer who makes people laugh by telling jokes or funny stories
a female entertainer who makes people laugh by telling jokes or funny stories
senses.chn: 女滑稽演员；女喜剧演员

senses.def: to break and fall to the ground

ex.en: The ceiling came down with a terrific crash.
ex.cn: 随着一声可怕的巨响，天花板塌了下来。

senses.def: to fall

ex.en: The rain came down in torrents.
ex.cn: 大雨滂沱。

senses.def: to land or fall from the sky

ex.en: We were forced to come down in a field.
ex.cn: 我们被迫降落在田野里。

senses.def: if a price, a temperature, a rate, etc. comes down, it gets lower

ex.en: The price of gas is coming down.
ex.cn: 煤气价格在下跌。

ex.en: Gas is coming down in price.
ex.cn: 煤气价格在下跌。

senses.def: to decide and say publicly that you support or oppose sb
senses.chn: 决定并宣布（支持或反对）

ex.en: The committee came down in support of his application.
ex.cn: 委员会决定并宣布支持他的申请。

senses.def: to reach as far down as a particular point
senses.chn: 下垂，向下延伸（到某一点）

ex.en: Her hair comes down to her waist.
ex.cn: 她的头发垂至腰部。

senses.def: a situation in which a person is not as important as before, or does not get as much respect from other people
to criticize sb severely or punish sb

ex.en: Don't come down too hard on her.
ex.cn: 不要太严厉地责备她。

ex.en: The courts are coming down heavily on young offenders.
ex.cn: 法庭对年轻罪犯实行严惩。

senses.def: to happen; to become noticeable

ex.en: We're hearing a lot about new inventions coming down the pike.
ex.cn: 我们经常听说新发明不断问世。

senses.def: to be able to be explained by a single important point

ex.en: What it comes down to is either I get more money or I leave.
ex.cn: 归结起来就是：不给我加薪，我就辞职。

senses.def: to get an illness that is not very serious

ex.en: I think I'm coming down with flu.
ex.cn: 我想我得了流感。

senses.def: a play or film/movie that is intended to be funny, usually with a happy ending; plays and films/movies of this type

ex.en: a romantic comedy
ex.cn: 浪漫喜剧

ex.en: slapstick comedy
ex.cn: 打闹剧

senses.def: an amusing aspect of sth

ex.en: He didn't appreciate the comedy of the situation.
ex.cn: 他未领略到这种局面的滑稽可笑之处。

senses.def: an amusing play, film/movie, or book that shows the silly behaviour of a particular group of people
senses.chn: 风俗喜剧，风尚喜剧（讽刺某群体行为的戏剧、电影或书籍）

senses.def: to be considered more important than anything else
senses.chn: 首要；第一；首先要考虑的

ex.en: In any decision she makes, her family always comes first.
ex.cn: 她作任何决定都是家庭第一。

senses.def: to offer your help, services, etc.
senses.chn: 主动提供（帮助或服务等）

ex.en: Several people came forward with information.
ex.cn: 有几个人自动站出来提供了信息。

ex.en: Police have asked witnesses of the accident to come forward.
ex.cn: 警方呼吁事故的目击者出来提供线索。

senses.def: to start in a particular place or be produced from a particular thing

ex.en: Much of our butter comes from New Zealand.
ex.cn: 我们的黄油大多产自新西兰。

ex.en: This wool comes from goats, not sheep.
ex.cn: 这种羊毛是山羊毛，不是绵羊毛。

ex.en: This poem comes from his new book.
ex.cn: 这首诗出自他的新书。

ex.en: Where does her attitude come from?
ex.cn: 她的态度因何而起？

ex.en: Where's that smell coming from?
ex.cn: 那种气味是哪里来的？

ex.en: He comes from a family of actors.
ex.cn: 他出身于演员世家。

senses.def: appearing to be trying to attract sb sexually

ex.en: a come-hither look
ex.cn: 挑逗的眼神

senses.def: to become completely clear to sb, often in a way that is painful

ex.en: It suddenly came home to him that he was never going to see Julie again.
ex.cn: 他突然明白他再也见不到朱莉了。

senses.def: when the tide comes in, it moves towards the land
to finish a race in a particular position

ex.en: My horse came in last.
ex.cn: 我的马跑了最后一名。

senses.def: to become fashionable

ex.en: Long hair for men came in in the sixties.
ex.cn: 男子留长发在 60 年代流行开来。

senses.def: to become available

ex.en: We're still waiting for copies of the book to come in.
ex.cn: 我们仍然在等这本书进货。

senses.def: to have a part in sth

ex.en: I understand the plan perfectly, but I can't see where I come in.
ex.cn: 我完全了解这项计划，可是不明白我能起什么作用。

senses.def: to arrive somewhere; to be received

ex.en: The train is coming in now.
ex.cn: 火车现正进站。

ex.en: News is coming in of a serious plane crash in France.
ex.cn: 刚收到的消息说法国发生了一起严重的飞机坠毁事故。

ex.en: She has over a thousand pounds a month coming in from her investments.
ex.cn: 她每月从自己的投资中得到超过一千英镑的收入。

senses.def: to take part in a discussion

ex.en: Would you like to come in at this point, Susan?
ex.cn: 苏珊，你愿意在此刻发表意见吗？

senses.def: to be introduced; to begin to be used
to receive sth, especially sth unpleasant

ex.en: The government's economic policies have come in for a lot of criticism.
ex.cn: 政府的经济政策遭到了很多批评。

senses.def: to become accepted or included in a group, etc. after a period of being outside it
to be useful

ex.en: The extra money came in very handy.
ex.cn: 这笔额外的钱正好派上了用场。

ex.en: Don't throw that away—it might come in handy.
ex.cn: 别把它扔了，它或许有用。

senses.def: to come into use; to begin to apply

ex.en: New controls come into effect next month.
ex.cn: 下月开始实施新的管制措施。

senses.def: to start working; to start having an effect

ex.en: The new rules come into operation from next week.
ex.cn: 新规定从下周起实施。

senses.def: to become a matter for doubt and discussion
senses.chn: 成为怀疑（或讨论）的对象

senses.def: to be left money by sb who has died

ex.en: She came into a fortune when her uncle died.
ex.cn: 她在叔叔去世后继承了一大笔财产。

senses.def: to be important in a particular situation

ex.en: I've worked very hard to pass this exam—luck doesn't come into it.
ex.cn: 我为通过这次考试下了很大的苦功，运气不是主要的。

senses.def: to be born
pleasant to look at
when a person comes of age, they reach the age when they have an adult's legal rights and responsibilities
if sth comes of age, it reaches the stage of development at which people accept and value it
to be able to be removed

ex.en: Does this hood come off?
ex.cn: 这风帽能卸下来吗？

ex.en: That mark won't come off.
ex.cn: 那污点去不掉。

senses.def: to take place; to happen

ex.en: Did the trip to Rome ever come off?
ex.cn: 去罗马的事最后成了吗？

senses.def: to be successful; to have the intended effect or result
senses.chn: 成功；达到预期效果（或结果）

ex.en: They had wanted it to be a surprise but the plan didn't come off.
ex.cn: 他们本想一鸣惊人，然而计划却流产了。

senses.def: to be successful/not successful in a fight, contest, etc.

ex.en: I thought they came off very well in the debate.
ex.cn: 我认为他们在辩论中表现非常出色。

senses.def: used to disagree with sb rudely
senses.chn: （粗鲁地表示不同意）别胡扯，别胡说，住口

ex.en: Come off it! We don't have a chance.
ex.cn: 别胡扯了！我们没机会。

senses.def: to stop taking medicine, a drug, alcohol, etc.

ex.en: I've tried to get him to come off the tranquillizers.
ex.cn: 我试图说服他停止服用镇静剂。

senses.def: to lose a fight, competition, etc. or suffer more compared with others
to lose a fight, competition, etc. or suffer more compared with others
senses.chn: （在战斗、比赛等中）吃败仗，输得最惨

senses.def: to walk onto the stage
to join a team during a game

ex.en: Owen came on for Brown ten minutes before the end of the game.
ex.cn: 终场前十分钟，欧文上场替换了布朗。

senses.def: to improve or develop in the way you want

ex.en: The project is coming on fine.
ex.cn: 这项工程进展顺利。

senses.def: used in orders to tell sb to hurry or to try harder

ex.en: Come on! We don't have much time.
ex.cn: 快点！我们时间不多了。

ex.en: Come on! Try once more.
ex.cn: 加把劲！再试一次。

senses.def: used to show that you know what sb has said is not correct
senses.chn: （表示知道某人所说的话不正确）得了吧

ex.en: Oh, come on—you know that isn't true!
ex.cn: 咳，得了吧，你知道那不是真的！

senses.def: to begin

ex.en: I can feel a cold coming on.
ex.cn: 我觉得要感冒了。

ex.en: I think there's rain coming on.
ex.cn: 我看要下雨了。

ex.en: It came on to rain.
ex.cn: 天下起雨来了。

senses.def: to start

ex.en: What time does the news come on?
ex.cn: 新闻报道什么时候开始？

senses.def: to begin to operate

ex.en: Set the oven to come on at six.
ex.cn: 把烤箱设定在六点钟开始烘烤。

ex.en: When does the heating come on?
ex.cn: 什么时间来暖气？

senses.def: an object or action which is intended to attract sb or to persuade them to do sth

ex.en: She was definitely giving him the come-on (= trying to attract him sexually).
ex.cn: 她肯定是在勾引他。

senses.def: to make your feelings clear in an aggressive way, especially your sexual feelings towards sb
senses.chn: 言行过分；（尤指）露骨地调情

senses.def: to behave in a way that shows sb that you want to have a sexual relationship with them
senses.chn: 勾引，勾搭（想与其发生性关系）

senses.def: to start talking about a subject

ex.en: I'd like to come on to that question later.
ex.cn: 我想稍后再讨论那个问题。

senses.def: when the sun, moon or stars come out, they appear

ex.en: The rain stopped and the sun came out.
ex.cn: 雨停后太阳出来了。

senses.def: to open

ex.en: The daffodils came out early this year.
ex.cn: 水仙花今年开得早。

senses.def: to be produced or published

ex.en: When is her new novel coming out?
ex.cn: 她的新小说何时出版？

senses.def: to become known

ex.en: The full story came out at the trial.
ex.cn: 案情始末在审判时真相大白。

ex.en: It came out that he'd been telling lies.
ex.cn: 后来才知道他一直在说谎。

senses.def: if a photograph comes out, it is a clear picture when it is developed and printed

ex.en: Some of the photos from our trip didn't come out.
ex.cn: 我们旅行的一些照片冲洗的效果不好。

senses.def: to be shown clearly

ex.en: Her best qualities come out in a crisis.
ex.cn: 她的优秀品质在危难之际显示了出来。

senses.def: when words come out, they are spoken

ex.en: I tried to say 'I love you,' but the words wouldn't come out.
ex.cn: 我想说 “我爱你”，但这话怎么也说不出口。

senses.def: to say publicly whether you agree or disagree with sth
senses.chn: 公开表明（同意或不同意）

ex.en: He came out against the plan.
ex.cn: 他公开表示反对这个计划。

ex.en: In her speech, the senator came out in favour of a change in the law.
ex.cn: 这位参议员在她的讲话中公开赞成修改法律。

senses.def: to stop work and go on strike
to no longer hide the fact that you are homosexual
senses.chn: 不再隐瞒自己是同性恋者的事实；公开表明自己是同性恋者；“出柜”

senses.def: to be formally introduced into society
to add up to a particular cost or sum

ex.en: The total bill comes out at £500.
ex.cn: 账单金额总计为 500 英镑。

senses.def: to become covered in spots, etc. on the skin

ex.en: Hot weather makes her come out in a rash.
ex.cn: 炎热的天气使她起了皮疹。

senses.def: to develop from sth

ex.en: The book came out of his experiences in India.
ex.cn: 这本书取材于他在印度的经历。

ex.en: Rock music came out of the blues.
ex.cn: 摇滚乐起源于布鲁斯音乐。

senses.def: to admit sth openly that you kept secret before, especially because of shame or embarrassment
senses.chn: 公开承认秘密（尤指因耻辱或尴尬而一直保守着的秘密）；“出柜”

ex.en: Homosexuals in public life are now coming out of the closet.
ex.cn: 公众人物中的同性恋者如今逐渐公开自己的性取向。

senses.def: to relax and become more confident and friendly with other people
senses.chn: 精神放松、更加自信和友好地与他人交往

ex.en: It was when she started drama classes that she really came out of herself.
ex.cn: 她是在开始学习戏剧课程时才真正不再害羞。

senses.def: to become less shy and more confident when talking to other people
senses.chn: （和人交谈时）放大胆子，不缩手缩脚

senses.def: to win a contest or an argument
senses.chn: （在比赛或辩论中）名列前茅，先拔头筹

ex.en: In most boardroom disputes he tends to come out on top.
ex.cn: 在大多数董事会议的辩论中，他往往占据上风。

senses.def: to say sth, especially sth surprising or rude
senses.chn: 说出（尤指令人吃惊或粗鲁的话）

ex.en: He came out with a stream of abuse.
ex.cn: 他讲了一连串的脏话。

ex.en: She sometimes comes out with the most extraordinary remarks.
ex.cn: 她有时说起话来语惊四座。

senses.def: to suddenly feel sth

ex.en: to come over funny/dizzy/faint
ex.cn: 突然感到可笑／眩晕／昏眩

ex.en: I come over all shy whenever I see her.
ex.cn: 我每次看到她时都会突然感到很害羞。

senses.def: to affect sb

ex.en: A fit of dizziness came over her.
ex.cn: 她感到一阵头晕目眩。

ex.en: I can't think what came over me (= I do not know what caused me to behave in that way).
ex.cn: 我不知道我是怎么了。

senses.def: anyone who is interested in, or comes forward for, sth, especially a competition
senses.chn: （尤指对比赛）感兴趣的人，到场者，参加者

ex.en: The event is open to all comers.
ex.cn: 所有人均可参加这项比赛。

senses.def: a person who arrives somewhere
a person who is likely to be successful
to be pleased to do what sb wants
senses.chn: 赶紧做某人喜欢的事；急于应某人的要求

ex.en: She knew she had only to call and he would come running.
ex.cn: 她知道只要打个电话，他就会高高兴兴地照办。

senses.def: to have an accident; to get into trouble
that can be eaten
an item of food
a mass of ice and dust that moves around the sun and looks like a bright star with a tail
to arrive by telephone, radio, etc. or through an official organization
senses.chn: （用电话、无线电等或由官方机构）传来

ex.en: A message is just coming through.
ex.cn: 刚有消息传来。

senses.def: to stop completely
to go slower gradually and then stop completely

ex.en: Production ground to a halt during the strike.
ex.cn: 罢工期间生产渐渐陷入瘫痪。

senses.def: if you bring a situation to a head or if a situation comes to a head, you are forced to deal with it quickly because it suddenly becomes very bad
senses.chn: （使）事情达到紧要关头，需要当机立断

senses.def: to reach a sad or difficult state
senses.chn: 陷于不妙的（或困难的）境地；落到这步田地

senses.def: if two or more different people or things come together, they form a united group

ex.en: Three colleges have come together to create a new university.
ex.cn: 三所学院合并成了一所新的大学。

ex.en: Bits and pieces of things he'd read and heard were coming together, and he began to understand.
ex.cn: 他把读到和听到的零碎片段综合起来，便逐渐明白了。

senses.def: to end in total failure
senses.chn: 以彻底失败而告终；惨遭失败

senses.def: to be harmed in an accident

ex.en: Several pedestrians came to grief on the icy pavement.
ex.cn: 好几个人都在结了冰的人行道上摔伤了。

senses.def: to agree to obey sb and accept their orders
to come close to the person who has called it
to become more interesting, exciting or full of activity
senses.chn: 变得更有趣（或使人兴奋）；变得活跃

ex.en: The match finally came to life in the second half.
ex.cn: 比赛在下半场终于精彩起来。

senses.def: to start to act or move as if alive

ex.en: In my dream all my toys came to life.
ex.cn: 在我的梦里，玩具都活过来了。

senses.def: to become known to people
senses.chn: 为人所知；变得众所周知；暴露

ex.en: New evidence has recently come to light.
ex.cn: 新的证据最近已披露出来。

senses.def: to be unsuccessful; to have no successful result

ex.en: How sad that all his hard work should come to nothing.
ex.cn: 他的所有辛勤劳动竟全部付诸东流，太让人伤心了。

ex.en: Her plans didn't come to anything.
ex.cn: 她的计划全落空了。

senses.def: to happen
to stop moving

ex.en: The car crashed through the barrier and came to rest in a field.
ex.cn: 汽车闯过护栏，在一块田里停了下来。

ex.en: His eyes came to rest on Clara's face.
ex.cn: 他的目光停留在克拉拉的脸上。

senses.def: to enter your mind

ex.en: The idea came to me in the bath.
ex.cn: 我泡澡时想出了这个主意。

ex.en: It suddenly came to her that she had been wrong all along.
ex.cn: 她突然意识到她一开始就错了。

senses.def: to become known by sb
senses.chn: 被某人知道；被某人获悉

ex.en: It has come to our knowledge that you have been taking time off without permission.
ex.cn: 我们了解到你们时常未经允许就不上班。

senses.def: to add up to sth

ex.en: The bill came to $30.
ex.cn: 账单金额总计为 30 美元。

ex.en: I never expected those few items to come to so much.
ex.cn: 我根本没想到就那么几件东西合计起来竟要花这么多钱。

senses.def: to reach a particular situation, especially a bad one
senses.chn: 达到（某状况，尤指坏的局面）

ex.en: The doctors will operate if necessary—but it may not come to that.
ex.cn: 必要时医生会施行手术，但也许还不至于此。

ex.en: Who'd have thought things would come to this (= become so bad)?
ex.cn: 谁会想到事情竟会变成这个样子？

senses.def: to reach a sad or difficult state
senses.chn: 陷于不妙的（或困难的）境地；落到这步田地

senses.def: to accept sth unpleasant by learning to deal with it
senses.chn: 迁就顺从；接受（令人不快的事物）；适应（困难的处境）

ex.en: She is still coming to terms with her son's death.
ex.cn: 她还没有完全从儿子死亡的阴影中走出来。

senses.def: used to introduce sth extra that is connected with what has just been said
senses.chn: （引出与刚提及的事物相关的事）说起…来，既然如此，假如那样的话

ex.en: I don't really trust him—nor his wife, come to that.
ex.cn: 我不太信任他。说起信任，我也不信任他的妻子。

senses.def: to be/become important and noticed by people; to play an important part
senses.chn: 变得重要（或突出）；起重要作用

ex.en: The problem has come to the fore again in recent months.
ex.cn: 近几个月来这个问题又成为热点。

ex.en: She has always been to the fore at moments of crisis.
ex.cn: 在危急时刻她总是挺身而出。

senses.def: used when you suddenly remember sth or realize that it might be important
senses.chn: （用于突然想起某事或认识到其重要性）想起来了，的确

ex.en: Come to think of it, he did mention seeing you.
ex.cn: 想起来了，他确实提到看见过你。

senses.def: to return to your normal state
to become reality

ex.en: Winning the medal was like a dream come true.
ex.cn: 获得这枚奖牌好比梦想成真。

senses.def: to be included in a particular group

ex.en: What heading does this come under?
ex.cn: 这该归入哪一个主题？

senses.def: to be a person that others are attacking or criticizing
senses.chn: 成为（攻击或批评的）目标

ex.en: The head teacher came under a lot of criticism from the parents.
ex.cn: 校长受到了家长的很多批评。

senses.def: to be controlled or influenced by sth

ex.en: All her students came under her spell.
ex.cn: 她所有的学生都被她迷住了。

senses.def: to become very upset
if a plan, etc. comes unglued, it does not work successfully
to become separated from sth it was stuck or fastened to

ex.en: The flap of the envelope had come unstuck.
ex.cn: 信封的封口没粘牢，张开了。

senses.def: to fail completely, with bad results
to appear above the soil

ex.en: The daffodils are just beginning to come up.
ex.cn: 那些水仙花刚开始破土发芽。

senses.def: to rise

ex.en: We watched the sun come up.
ex.cn: 我们观看了日出。

senses.def: to happen

ex.en: I'm afraid something urgent has come up.
ex.cn: 恐怕有紧急事情发生。

ex.en: We'll let you know if any vacancies come up.
ex.cn: 一有空缺，我们就会通知你。

senses.def: to be mentioned or discussed

ex.en: The subject came up in conversation.
ex.cn: 谈话中提到了这个话题。

ex.en: The question is bound to come up at the meeting.
ex.cn: 会上一定会讨论这个问题。

senses.def: to be going to happen very soon

ex.en: Her birthday is coming up soon.
ex.cn: 她的生日就快到了。

senses.def: to be dealt with by a court

ex.en: Her divorce case comes up next month.
ex.cn: 她的离婚案在下月审理。

senses.def: if your number, name, ticket, etc. comes up in a betting game, it is chosen and you win sth
senses.chn: （在博彩游戏中指号码、名字、奖券等）被抽中，中奖

senses.def: to arrive; to be ready soon

ex.en: 'Is lunch ready?' 'Coming up!'
ex.cn: “午餐准备好了吗？” “马上就好！”

senses.def: to be considered for a job, an important position, etc.

ex.en: She comes up for re-election next year.
ex.cn: 她明年将再度参加竞选。

senses.def: to be reaching the time when sth must be done

ex.en: His contract is coming up for renewal.
ex.cn: 他的合同快到续订期了。

senses.def: a punishment for sth bad that you have done, that other people feel you really deserve

ex.en: I was glad to see that the bad guy got his comeuppance at the end of the movie.
ex.cn: 我很高兴看到那个坏蛋在电影的结尾受到了应有的惩罚。

senses.def: to reach as far as a particular point

ex.en: The water came up to my neck.
ex.cn: 水淹到了我的脖子。

senses.def: to reach an acceptable level or standard
senses.chn: 达到（认可的水平或标准）

ex.en: His performance didn't really come up to his usual high standard.
ex.cn: 他的表现没有真正达到他往常的高水平。

ex.en: Their trip to France didn't come up to expectations.
ex.cn: 他们的法国之行未尽如人意。

senses.def: to find or produce an answer, a sum of money, etc.
senses.chn: 找到（答案）；拿出（一笔钱等）

ex.en: She came up with a new idea for increasing sales.
ex.cn: 她想出了增加销售量的新主意。

ex.en: How soon can you come up with the money?
ex.cn: 你什么时候能拿出这笔钱？

senses.def: to do what you have promised to do or what people expect or want you to do

ex.en: We expected great things of the England team, but on the day they simply failed to deliver the goods.
ex.cn: 我们本指望英格兰队大获全胜，可那天他们真是有负众望。

senses.def: despite any problems or difficulties you may have
senses.chn: 不管出现什么问题；无论有什么困难；不管怎样

ex.en: He promised to support her come what may.
ex.cn: 他答应不管出现什么问题都支持她。

senses.def: to happen to you by chance, or when you were not expecting it
senses.chn: 意外落在…头上；偶尔发生在…身上

ex.en: He took whatever came his way.
ex.cn: 无论什么事落到他的头上，他都认了。

senses.def: a sweet/candy consisting of a nut, seed or fruit covered with sugar
the state of being physically relaxed and free from pain; the state of having a pleasant life, with everything that you need

ex.en: These tennis shoes are designed for comfort and performance.
ex.cn: 这些网球鞋的设计以舒适为本，打起球来发挥更出色。

ex.en: You can now watch the latest movies in the comfort of your own home.
ex.cn: 你现在可以在自己家舒舒服服地看最新电影。

ex.en: The hotel offers a high standard of comfort and service.
ex.cn: 这家旅馆提供高标准的舒适享受和优质服务。

ex.en: They had enough money to live in comfort in their old age.
ex.cn: 他们有足够的钱舒舒服服地安度晚年。

senses.def: a feeling of not suffering or worrying so much; a feeling of being less unhappy

ex.en: to take/draw comfort from sb's words
ex.cn: 从某人的话中得到安慰

ex.en: I tried to offer a few words of comfort.
ex.cn: 我试图说上几句安慰的话。

ex.en: The sound of gunfire was too close for comfort.
ex.cn: 炮火声太近，让人恐慌不安。

ex.en: If it's any comfort to you, I'm in the same situation.
ex.cn: 就当是一句安慰的话，我的情况也跟你一样。

ex.en: His words were of little comfort in the circumstances.
ex.cn: 在这种情况下，他的话起不了什么安慰作用。

ex.en: comfort food (= food that makes you feel better)
ex.cn: 安慰性食品

senses.def: a person or thing that helps you when you are suffering, worried or unhappy
senses.chn: 令人感到安慰的人（或事物）

ex.en: The children have been a great comfort to me through all of this.
ex.cn: 在我经历这一切的日子里，孩子们一直是我的莫大安慰。

ex.en: It's a comfort to know that she is safe.
ex.cn: 知道她安然无恙是令人宽慰的事。

senses.def: a thing that makes your life easier or more comfortable

ex.en: The hotel has all modern comforts/every modern comfort.
ex.cn: 这家旅馆拥有各种现代化的舒适设施。

ex.en: material comforts (= money and possessions)
ex.cn: 物质上的舒适条件（钱财）

senses.def: to make sb who is worried or unhappy feel better by being kind and sympathetic towards them

ex.en: The victim's widow was today being comforted by family and friends.
ex.cn: 受害人的遗孀今天正受到亲属和朋友的安慰。

ex.en: She comforted herself with the thought that it would soon be spring.
ex.cn: 她想到春天很快就要来临，以此来宽慰自己。

ex.en: It comforted her to feel his arms around her.
ex.cn: 感受到他的拥抱使她得到安慰。

senses.def: making you feel physically relaxed; pleasant to wear, sit on, etc.

ex.en: It's such a comfortable bed.
ex.cn: 这床真舒服。

ex.en: These new shoes are not very comfortable.
ex.cn: 这双新鞋穿起来不太舒服。

ex.en: a warm comfortable house
ex.cn: 温暖舒适的房子

senses.def: feeling physically relaxed in a pleasant way; warm enough, without pain, etc.
senses.chn: 愉快放松的；舒服的；安逸的

ex.en: Are you comfortable?
ex.cn: 你感觉舒服吗？

ex.en: She shifted into a more comfortable position on the chair.
ex.cn: 她在椅子上换了个更舒适的姿势。

ex.en: Please make yourself comfortable while I get some coffee.
ex.cn: 我去冲咖啡，您别拘束。

ex.en: The patient is comfortable (= not in pain) after his operation.
ex.cn: 病人手术后感觉良好。

senses.def: confident and not worried or afraid
senses.chn: 自信而无忧虑的；自在的

ex.en: He's more comfortable with computers than with people.
ex.cn: 比起与人相处，他和电脑打交道更能应付自如。

senses.def: having enough money to buy what you want without worrying about the cost

ex.en: They're not millionaires, but they're certainly very comfortable.
ex.cn: 他们不是百万富翁，但也很富裕。

ex.en: affluent Western countries
ex.cn: 富裕的西方国家

ex.en: It's good to see you looking so prosperous.
ex.cn: 看到你成功的样子真是令人高兴。

ex.en: His family is not very well off.
ex.cn: 他家境不太宽裕。

ex.en: They're not millionaires, but they're certainly very comfortable.
ex.cn: 他们不是百万富翁，但也很富裕。

senses.def: quite large; allowing you to win easily

ex.en: The party won with a comfortable majority.
ex.cn: 该政党以明显的多数票获胜。

ex.en: a comfortable 2–0 win
ex.cn: 以 2:0 轻取

senses.def: in a comfortable way

senses.chn: （尤指旧时苏联的）政治委员，政委

senses.def: a department of the army that is responsible for food supplies
a government department in the Soviet Union before 1946
senses.chn: （1946 年以前苏联的）人民委员部

senses.def: a shop/store that sells food, etc. in a military base, a prison, etc.
senses.chn: （军事基地、监狱等处出售食品等的）杂货商店

senses.def: a restaurant for people working in a large organization, especially a film studio
senses.chn: （大型机构，尤指电影制片厂的）员工餐厅

senses.def: an official group of people who have been given responsibility to control sth, or to find out about sth, usually for the government
senses.chn: （通常为政府管控或调查某事的）委员会

ex.en: the European Commission
ex.cn: 欧洲委员会

ex.en: The government has set up a commission of inquiry into the disturbances at the prison.
ex.cn: 政府成立了一个委员会来调查监狱骚乱事件。

ex.en: a commission on human rights
ex.cn: 人权委员会

senses.def: an amount of money that is paid to sb for selling goods and which increases with the amount of goods that are sold

ex.en: You get a 10% commission on everything you sell.
ex.cn: 你可从你售出的每件商品中获得 10% 的佣金。

ex.en: He earned £2 000 in commission last month.
ex.cn: 他上个月挣了 2 000 英镑的佣金。

ex.en: In this job you work on commission (= are paid according to the amount you sell).
ex.cn: 你做这份工作按销售额提成。

senses.def: an amount of money that is charged by a bank, etc. for providing a particular service

ex.en: 1% commission is charged for cashing traveller's cheques.
ex.cn: 兑现旅行支票收取 1% 的手续费。

senses.def: a formal request to sb to design or make a piece of work such as a building or a painting
senses.chn: （请某人作建筑设计或作一幅画等的）正式委托

senses.def: an officer's position in the armed forces
the act of doing sth wrong or illegal

ex.en: the commission of a crime
ex.cn: 犯罪

senses.def: available/not available to be used

ex.en: Several of the airline's planes are temporarily out of commission and undergoing safety checks.
ex.cn: 这家航空公司有几架飞机暂时不能使用，正在接受安全检查。

senses.def: to officially ask sb to write, make or create sth or to do a task for you
senses.chn: 正式委托（谱写、制作、创作或完成）

ex.en: She has been commissioned to write a new national anthem.
ex.cn: 她已受委托谱写新国歌。

ex.en: Publishers have commissioned a French translation of the book.
ex.cn: 出版商已委托人把这本书译成法语。

senses.def: to choose sb as an officer in one of the armed forces

ex.en: She was commissioned in 2014.
ex.cn: 她于 2014 年被任命为军官。

ex.en: He has just been commissioned (as a) pilot officer.
ex.cn: 他刚被任命为空军少尉。

senses.def: a person in uniform whose job is to stand at the entrance to a hotel, etc. and open the door for visitors, find them taxis, etc.
senses.chn: （在旅馆等门口为来宾开门、叫出租车等的）穿制服的看门人，门童

senses.def: an officer in the armed forces who has a higher rank, such as a captain or a general
a member of a commission (= an official group of people who are responsible for controlling sth or finding out about sth)

ex.en: the Church Commissioners (= the group of people responsible for controlling the financial affairs of the Church of England)
ex.cn: 英格兰国教会财政管理委员会委员

ex.en: European Commissioners
ex.cn: 欧洲委员会委员

senses.def: the head of a particular police force in some countries
the head of a government department in some countries

ex.en: the agriculture/health, etc. commissioner
ex.cn: 农业、卫生等厅长

ex.en: Commissioner Rhodes was unavailable for comment.
ex.cn: 罗兹局长无暇评论。

senses.def: (in the US) an official chosen by a sports association to control it
senses.chn: （美国体育协会的）总干事，主管人

ex.en: the baseball commissioner
ex.cn: 棒球协会总干事

senses.def: a lawyer who has official authority to be present when sb makes a formal promise that a written statement that they will use as evidence in court is true
senses.chn: 监誓官（得到正式任命在法庭上主持宣誓的律师）

senses.def: to do sth wrong or illegal

ex.en: to commit murder/adultery
ex.cn: 犯凶杀罪／通奸罪

ex.en: Most crimes are committed by young men.
ex.cn: 多数罪行都是年轻人犯下的。

ex.en: appalling crimes committed against innocent children
ex.cn: 对无辜儿童犯下的骇人听闻的罪行

senses.def: to kill yourself deliberately
to promise sincerely that you will definitely do sth, keep to an agreement or arrangement, etc.
senses.chn: 承诺，保证（做某事、遵守协议或遵从安排等）

ex.en: The President is committed to reforming health care.
ex.cn: 总统承诺要改革卫生保健制度。

ex.en: Borrowers should think carefully before committing themselves to taking out a loan.
ex.cn: 借款人应当慎重考虑之后再行借贷。

ex.en: Both sides committed themselves to settle the dispute peacefully.
ex.cn: 双方承诺和平解决争端。

senses.def: to give an opinion or make a decision openly so that it is then difficult to change it
senses.chn: （公开地）表达意见，作出决定（以致日后难以更改）

ex.en: You don't have to commit yourself now, just think about it.
ex.cn: 你不必现在表态，只需考虑一下这件事。

senses.def: to be completely loyal to one person, organization, etc. or give all your time and effort to your work, an activity, etc.
senses.chn: 忠于（某个人、机构等）；全心全意投入（工作、活动等）

ex.en: Why are so many men scared to commit?(= say they will be loyal to one person)
ex.cn: 为什么有这么多的男人害怕许诺忠诚于人？

senses.def: to spend money or time on sth/sb

ex.en: The council has committed large amounts of money to housing projects.
ex.cn: 市政会在住宅项目上投入了大量资金。

senses.def: to order sb to be sent to a hospital, prison, etc.
senses.chn: （下令）把（某人）送进（医院或监狱等）

ex.en: She was committed to a psychiatric hospital.
ex.cn: 她被送进了精神病院。

senses.def: to send sb for trial in court
to learn sth well enough to remember it exactly

ex.en: She committed the instructions to memory.
ex.cn: 她把指令记得很牢。

senses.def: to write sth down
a promise to do sth or to behave in a particular way; a promise to support sb/sth; the fact of committing yourself
senses.chn: 承诺；许诺；允诺承担；保证

ex.en: She doesn't want to make a big emotional commitment to Steve at the moment.
ex.cn: 她不想在此刻对史蒂夫在感情上作出重大的承诺。

ex.en: the government's commitment to public services
ex.cn: 政府对公共服务作出的承诺

ex.en: The company's commitment to providing quality at a reasonable price has been vital to its success.
ex.cn: 这家公司保证供货质优价廉的承诺对它的成功起了决定性的作用。

senses.def: the willingness to work hard and give your energy and time to a job or an activity
senses.chn: （对工作或活动的）献身，奉献，投入

ex.en: A career as an actor requires one hundred per cent commitment.
ex.cn: 干演员这一行需要百分之百的投入。

senses.def: a thing that you have promised or agreed to do, or that you have to do
senses.chn: 已承诺（或同意）的事；不得不做的事

ex.en: He's busy for the next month with filming commitments.
ex.cn: 他正忙于准备已经承诺下个月接拍的电影工作。

ex.en: Women very often have to juggle work with their family commitments.
ex.cn: 妇女经常要工作和家庭两头忙。

senses.def: agreeing to use money, time or people in order to achieve sth
senses.chn: 花费，使用（资金、时间、人力）

ex.en: the commitment of resources to education
ex.cn: 对教育的资源投入

ex.en: Achieving success at this level requires a commitment of time and energy.
ex.cn: 取得这种水平的成就需要花费时间和精力。

senses.def: the official process of sending sb to prison or to a mental hospital
senses.chn: 收监；拘押；送入（精神病院）

ex.en: He was released on bail pending committal proceedings.
ex.cn: 他交保获释正在候审。

senses.def: willing to work hard and give your time and energy to sth; believing strongly in sth
senses.chn: 尽心尽力的；坚信的；坚定的

ex.en: a committed member of the team
ex.cn: 忠于职守的队员

ex.en: They are committed socialists.
ex.cn: 他们是坚定的社会主义者。

senses.def: a group of people who are chosen, usually by a larger group, to make decisions or to deal with a particular subject

ex.en: She's on the management committee.
ex.cn: 她任管理委员会委员。

ex.en: The committee has/have decided to close the restaurant.
ex.cn: 委员会已决定关闭这家餐馆。

ex.en: a committee member/a member of the committee
ex.cn: 委员会的委员

ex.en: a committee meeting
ex.cn: 委员会的会议

senses.def: a piece of furniture that looks like a chair but has a toilet under the seat
a piece of furniture, especially an old or antique one, with drawers for storing things in
senses.chn: （尤指旧式或古董）有抽屉的柜橱，五斗橱

senses.def: having a lot of space
a product or a raw material that can be bought and sold

ex.en: rice, flour and other basic commodities
ex.cn: 稻米、面粉和其他基本商品

ex.en: a drop in commodity prices
ex.cn: 商品价格的下跌

ex.en: Crude oil is the world's most important commodity.
ex.cn: 原油是世界上最重要的商品。

ex.en: to create/develop/launch a new product
ex.cn: 创造／开发／推出新产品

ex.en: cotton/leather goods
ex.cn: 棉织／皮革商品

ex.en: electrical goods
ex.cn: 电器商品

senses.def: a thing that is useful or has a useful quality
senses.chn: 有用的东西；有使用价值的事物

ex.en: Water is a precious commodity that is often taken for granted in the West.
ex.cn: 水很宝贵，但在西方国家人们往往意识不到这一点。

senses.def: an officer of high rank in the navy

ex.en: Commodore John Barry
ex.cn: 约翰 · 巴里海军准将

senses.def: happening often; existing in large numbers or in many places

ex.en: Jackson is a common English name.
ex.cn: 杰克逊是常见的英语人名。

ex.en: Breast cancer is the most common form of cancer among women in this country.
ex.cn: 乳腺癌是这个国家妇女中最常见的一种癌症。

ex.en: Some birds which were once a common sight are now becoming rare.
ex.cn: 有些曾经随处可见的鸟类现在日益稀少。

ex.en: a common spelling mistake
ex.cn: 常犯的拼写错误

senses.def: shared by or belonging to two or more people or by the people in a group

ex.en: They share a common interest in photography.
ex.cn: 他们在摄影方面兴趣相投。

ex.en: basic features which are common to all human languages
ex.cn: 所有人类语言共有的基本特征

ex.en: We are working together for a common purpose.
ex.cn: 我们在为一个共同的目标一起工作。

ex.en: common ownership of the land
ex.cn: 土地的共同所有权

ex.en: This decision was taken for the common good (= the advantage of everyone).
ex.cn: 作出这个决定是为了共同的利益。

ex.en: It is, by common consent, Scotland's prettiest coast (= everyone agrees that it is).
ex.cn: 这是苏格兰公认的最美丽的海岸。

senses.def: ordinary; not unusual or special
senses.chn: 普通的；平常的；寻常的；平凡的

ex.en: the common garden frog
ex.cn: 园地里常见的青蛙

ex.en: Shakespeare's work was popular among the common people in his day.
ex.cn: 莎士比亚的作品在他那个年代很受平民百姓的欢迎。

ex.en: In most people's eyes she was nothing more than a common criminal.
ex.cn: 在多数人的眼里她只不过是个普通的罪犯。

ex.en: You'd think he'd have the common courtesy to apologize (= this would be the polite behaviour that people would expect).
ex.cn: 你还以为他会懂得起码的礼貌去道个歉呢。

ex.en: It's only common decency to let her know what's happening (= people would expect it).
ex.cn: 出于礼貌，该让她知道正在发生的事。

senses.def: typical of sb from a low social class and not having good manners

ex.en: She thought he was very common and uneducated.
ex.cn: 她认为他很粗俗且无教养。

senses.def: ordinary; with no special features
the ability of a powerful or famous person to talk to and understand ordinary people
senses.chn: （有权势者或名人的）平易近人的品质，亲民作风

senses.def: to be united with sb about sth that you both agree on, believe in or wish to achieve
senses.chn: 与某人联合起来，与某人合作（以达到共同的目的）

senses.def: to be sth that everyone knows, especially in a particular community or group
an area of open land in a town or village that anyone may use

ex.en: We went for a walk on the common.
ex.cn: 我们在公地上散步。

ex.en: Wimbledon Common
ex.cn: 温布尔登公地

senses.def: a large room where students can eat in a school, college, etc.
senses.chn: （学校、大学等的）学生公共食堂

ex.en: The commons is next to the gym.
ex.cn: 学生公共食堂在体育馆的旁边。

senses.def: to have the same interests, ideas, etc. as sb else

ex.en: Tim and I have nothing in common./I have nothing in common with Tim.
ex.cn: 我和蒂姆毫无共同之处。

senses.def: to have the same features, characteristics, etc.
senses.chn: 有相同的特征（或特点等）

ex.en: The two cultures have a lot in common.
ex.cn: 这两种文化具有许多相同之处。

senses.def: by everyone in a group

ex.en: They hold the property as tenants in common.
ex.cn: 作为共同租赁人，他们共同占用这份房地产。

senses.def: in the same way as sb/sth

ex.en: Britain, in common with many other industrialized countries, has experienced major changes over the last 100 years.
ex.cn: 与许多其他工业化国家一样，英国在过去 100 年里经历了重大的变化。

senses.def: a number that can be divided exactly by all the numbers below the line in a set of fractions
an idea, attitude or experience that is shared by all the members of a group
a person who does not come from a royal or noble family
the period since the birth of Christ when the Christian calendar starts counting years

ex.cn: 公元 1890 年

senses.def: opinions, interests and aims that you share with sb, although you may not agree with them about other things
senses.chn: （观点、利益和目标的）共同基础，共同点，一致点

ex.en: Despite our disagreements, we have been able to find some common ground.
ex.cn: 尽管我们存在分歧，但仍能找到一些共同点。

senses.def: a system in which each person owns their flat/apartment in a building but the building and shared areas are owned by everyone together
senses.chn: 公寓楼共有制度（住户共同拥有楼房及公用区域）

senses.def: land that belongs to or may be used by the local community
(in some countries) the part of the law that has been developed from customs and from decisions made by judges, not created by Parliament
senses.chn: （某些国家）普通法，习惯法，判例法

senses.def: a person that a woman or man has lived with for a long time and who is recognized (in some countries though not the UK) as a husband or wife, without a formal marriage ceremony
senses.chn: （未举行结婚仪式的）事实婚姻的男方，事实婚姻的女方

senses.def: a person that a woman or man has lived with for a long time and who is recognized (in some countries though not the UK) as a husband or wife, without a formal marriage ceremony
senses.chn: （未举行结婚仪式的）事实婚姻的男方，事实婚姻的女方

senses.def: usually; very often; by most people

ex.en: Christopher is commonly known as Kit.
ex.cn: 克里斯托弗通常被称为基特。

ex.en: commonly held opinions
ex.cn: 多数人持有的观点

ex.en: This is one of the most commonly used methods.
ex.cn: 这是最常采用的方法之一。

senses.def: a group of countries that have agreed on low taxes on goods traded between countries in the group, and higher fixed taxes on goods imported from countries outside the group
senses.chn: 共同市场（成员国之间实行低关税贸易，对从成员国之外的国家进口的商品规定较高关税）

senses.def: a former name of the European Union
senses.chn: 欧洲共同市场（欧洲联盟旧称）

senses.def: a word such as table, cat or sea, that refers to an object or a thing but is not the name of a particular person, place or thing
senses.chn: 普通名词（如 table、cat 或 sea）

senses.def: ordinary; with no special features
done very often, or existing in many places, and therefore not unusual

ex.en: Computers are now commonplace in primary classrooms.
ex.cn: 计算机如今在小学教室里很普遍。

senses.def: an event, etc. that happens very often and is not unusual
a remark, etc. that is not new or interesting
senses.chn: 平淡无奇的言语等；老生常谈

senses.def: (especially in the past) a book into which you copy parts of other books, poems, etc. and add your own comments
a room used by the teachers or students of a school, college, etc. when they are not teaching or studying
the ability to think about things in a practical way and make sensible decisions

ex.en: For goodness' sake, just use your common sense!
ex.cn: 我的老天，你也凭常识想想！

ex.en: a common-sense approach to a problem
ex.cn: 按常理解决问题的方法

senses.def: an organization consisting of the United Kingdom and other countries, including most of the countries that used to be part of the British Empire
senses.chn: 英联邦（由英国和其他大多数曾经隶属于大英帝国的国家组成）

ex.en: a member of the Commonwealth
ex.cn: 英联邦成员国

ex.en: Commonwealth countries
ex.cn: 英联邦国家

senses.def: used in the official names of, and to refer to, some states of the US (Kentucky, Massachusetts, Pennsylvania and Virginia)
senses.chn: （用于美国肯塔基、马萨诸塞、宾夕法尼亚和弗吉尼亚四州的正式名称中）州

ex.en: the Commonwealth of Virginia
ex.cn: 弗吉尼亚州

ex.en: The city and the Commonwealth have lost a great leader.
ex.cn: 这座城市和这个州失去了一位伟大的领袖。

senses.def: an independent country that is strongly connected to the US
senses.chn: （与美国联系紧密的）自治政区

ex.en: Puerto Rico remains a US commonwealth, not a state.
ex.cn: 波多黎各至今仍然是美国的一个自治政区，而不是一个州。

senses.def: used in the names of some groups of countries or states that have chosen to be politically linked with each other
senses.chn: （用于某些政治上相互有联系的国家集团的名称）联合体

ex.en: the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS)
ex.cn: 独立国家联合体（独联体）

senses.def: sudden noisy confusion or excitement

ex.en: I heard a commotion and went to see what was happening.
ex.cn: 我听到一阵喧闹，便去看看发生了什么事情。

ex.en: The crowd waiting outside was causing a commotion.
ex.cn: 在外面等待的人群眼看就要发生骚乱。

senses.def: shared by, or for the use of, a number of people, especially people who live together
senses.chn: （尤指居住在一起的人）共享的，共有的，共用的

ex.en: a communal kitchen/garden, etc.
ex.cn: 共用的厨房、花园等

ex.en: As a student he tried communal living for a few years.
ex.cn: 当学生时他尝试过几年集体生活。

senses.def: involving different groups of people in a community
senses.chn: （集体中）不同群体的，各团体的

ex.en: communal violence between religious groups
ex.cn: 不同教派之间的暴力冲突

senses.def: the fact of living together and sharing possessions and responsibilities
a strong sense of belonging to a particular, especially religious, community, which can lead to extreme behaviour or violence towards others
a group of people who live together and share responsibilities, possessions, etc.
senses.chn: （共同生活、分担责任、共享财产等的）群体，公社

ex.en: a 1970s hippy commune
ex.cn: 20 世纪 70 年代的嬉皮士群体

senses.def: the smallest division of local government in France and some other countries
senses.chn: （法国及其他一些国家的）最小的行政区

senses.def: to share your emotions and feelings with sb/sth without speaking
senses.chn: 与…默默分享情感（或沟通、交融）

ex.en: He spent much of this time communing with nature.
ex.cn: 他这个时期的许多时间都沉浸在大自然中。

senses.def: that sb can pass on to other people or communicate to sb else

ex.en: communicable diseases
ex.cn: 传染性疾病

senses.def: a person who receives Communion in a Christian church service
to exchange information, news, ideas, etc. with sb
senses.chn: （与某人）交流（信息或消息、意见等）；沟通

ex.en: We only communicate by email.
ex.cn: 我们只是互通电邮。

ex.en: They communicated in sign language.
ex.cn: 他们用手语沟通。

ex.en: Dolphins use sound to communicate with each other.
ex.cn: 海豚用声音相互沟通。

ex.en: to communicate information/a message to sb
ex.cn: 把情报／信息传递给某人

ex.en: We talked on the phone for over an hour.
ex.cn: 我们在电话里谈了一个多小时。

ex.en: Have you discussed the problem with anyone?
ex.cn: 你与谁商量过这个问题吗？

senses.def: to make your ideas, feelings, thoughts, etc. known to other people so that they understand them
senses.chn: 传达，传递（想法、感情、思想等）

ex.en: Candidates must be able to communicate effectively.
ex.cn: 候选人必须善于有效地表达自己。

ex.en: He was eager to communicate his ideas to the group.
ex.cn: 他急于把他的想法传达给小组。

ex.en: Her nervousness was communicating itself to the children.
ex.cn: 她紧张不安的情绪传递给了孩子们。

ex.en: They failed to communicate what was happening and why.
ex.cn: 他们没说清楚当时发生了什么以及起因是什么。

senses.def: to have a good relationship because you are able to understand and talk about your own and other people's thoughts, feelings, etc.

ex.en: The novel is about a family who can't communicate with each other.
ex.cn: 这部小说写的是一个成员间彼此无法沟通的家庭。

senses.def: to pass a disease from one person, animal, etc. to another

ex.en: The disease is communicated through dirty drinking water.
ex.cn: 这种疾病通过不干净的饮用水传播。

senses.def: if two rooms communicate, they are next to each other and you can get from one to the other

ex.en: a communicating door (= one that connects two rooms)
ex.cn: 连通门

senses.def: the activity or process of expressing ideas and feelings or of giving people information

ex.en: Speech is the fastest method of communication between people.
ex.cn: 说话是人与人之间最快捷的沟通方法。

ex.en: All channels of communication need to be kept open.
ex.cn: 所有沟通渠道都要保持畅通。

ex.en: Doctors do not always have good communication skills.
ex.cn: 医生不一定都具备良好的交际能力。

ex.en: non-verbal communication
ex.cn: 非言语交际

ex.en: We are in regular communication by email.
ex.cn: 我们定期通过电子邮件联系。

senses.def: methods of sending information, especially telephones, radio, computers, etc. or roads and railways

ex.en: communication systems/links/technology
ex.cn: 通信系统／线路／技术

ex.en: The new airport will improve communications between the islands.
ex.cn: 新机场将改善岛屿间的交通联系。

ex.en: Snow has prevented communication with the outside world for three days.
ex.cn: 大雪使得与外界的通信联系中断了三天。

senses.def: a message, letter or telephone call

ex.en: a communication from the leader of the party
ex.cn: 来自政党领袖的信息

senses.def: willing to talk and give information to other people

ex.en: I don't find him very communicative.
ex.cn: 我发觉他不太爱说话。

senses.def: connected with the ability to communicate in a language, especially a foreign language
senses.chn: 语言交际能力的（尤指用外语）

ex.en: communicative skills
ex.cn: 语言交际能力

senses.def: a person's ability to communicate information and ideas in a foreign language
a person who communicates sth to others

ex.en: an effective/skilled/successful communicator
ex.cn: 有效的／熟练的／成功的交际者

ex.en: a poor communicator
ex.cn: 不善于交流的人

ex.en: I looked around to see who the speaker was.
ex.cn: 我四下环顾看说话的是谁。

ex.en: a fluent Arabic speaker
ex.cn: 阿拉伯语讲得流利的人

ex.en: The ideal candidate will be an effective communicator.
ex.cn: 理想的候选人定要是善于沟通的人。

ex.en: Myra is a dear, but she's also a terrible gossip.
ex.cn: 迈拉是很可爱，但也是个讨厌的长舌妇。

senses.def: a ceremony in the Christian Church during which people eat bread and drink wine in memory of the last meal that Christ had with his disciples
senses.chn: （基督教教会的）圣餐仪式，领受圣体

ex.en: to go to Communion (= attend church for this celebration)
ex.cn: 去参加圣餐仪式

ex.en: to take/receive communion (= receive the bread and wine)
ex.cn: 领受圣餐

senses.def: the state of sharing or exchanging thoughts and feelings; the feeling of being part of sth

ex.en: poets living in communion with nature
ex.cn: 与大自然情感交融的诗人

senses.def: a group of people with the same religious beliefs

ex.en: the Anglican communion
ex.cn: 圣公会

senses.def: a political movement that believes in an economic system in which the state controls the means of producing everything on behalf of the people. It aims to create a society in which everyone is treated equally.
the system of government by a ruling Communist Party, such as in the former Soviet Union
a person who believes in or supports communism
senses.chn: 共产主义者；共产主义的支持者

senses.def: a member of a Communist Party
all the people who live in a particular area, country, etc. when talked about as a group

ex.en: The local community was shocked by the murders.
ex.cn: 当地社会对这些谋杀案感到震惊。

ex.en: health workers based in the community (= working with people in a local area)
ex.cn: 以社区为基地的保健工作人员

ex.en: the international community (= the countries of the world as a group)
ex.cn: 国际社会

ex.en: good community relations with the police
ex.cn: 社区与警方之间的良好关系

ex.en: community parks/libraries (= paid for by the local town/city)
ex.cn: 社区公园／图书馆

senses.def: a group of people who share the same religion, race, job, etc.

ex.en: the Polish community in London
ex.cn: 在伦敦的波兰侨民团体

ex.en: ethnic communities
ex.cn: 种族团体

ex.en: the farming community
ex.cn: 农业界

senses.def: the feeling of sharing things and belonging to a group in the place where you live

ex.en: There is a strong sense of community in this town.
ex.cn: 这个镇上有一种强烈的社区意识。

ex.en: community spirit
ex.cn: 团体精神

senses.def: a group of plants and animals growing or living in the same place or environment
medical and other care for people who need help over a long period, which allows them to live at home rather than in a hospital
senses.chn: 社区护理服务（让长期需要帮助者在家中接受医疗等）

senses.def: a place where people from the same area can meet for social events or sports or to take classes
(in Britain) a secondary school that is open to adults from the local community as well as to its own students
senses.chn: 社区中学（在英国除接收本校学生外亦向当地社区成人开放）

senses.def: (in the US) a college that is mainly for students from the local community and that offers programmes that are two years long, including programmes in practical skills
senses.chn: 社区学院（美国为社区成员提供两年制课程，包括职业技术训练）

senses.def: a method of teaching a foreign language that uses small groups and other ways of reducing students' anxiety
(in the UK) a decision, made in court, to give a punishment that involves helping people in the community, having treatment for an addiction, etc. instead of going to prison
senses.chn: （英国）社区服务令（须完成法院规定的社区服务工作或接受戒瘾治疗等，无须入狱）

ex.en: He was sentenced to a community order that involved psychological counselling.
ex.cn: 他被判社区服务，需要接受心理辅导。

senses.def: property that is considered to belong equally to a married couple
(in the UK) a punishment, given by a court, that involves helping people in the community, having treatment for an addiction, etc. instead of going to prison
senses.chn: （英国）社区刑罚，社区服务刑（须完成法院规定的社区服务工作或接受戒瘾治疗等，无须入狱）

ex.en: She was given a two-year community sentence for the assault on her neighbour.
ex.cn: 她因袭击邻居被判处两年社区刑。

senses.def: work helping people in the local community that sb does without being paid, either because they want to, or because they have been ordered to by a court as a punishment
senses.chn: 社区服务（自愿或因受法庭惩罚的无偿劳动）

senses.def: close enough or short enough to make travelling to work every day a possibility
senses.chn: 上下班方便的；（离工作地点）近的

senses.def: a commutable punishment can be made less severe
able to be changed
the act of making a punishment less severe

ex.en: a commutation of the death sentence to life imprisonment
ex.cn: 由死刑减为终身监禁

senses.def: the act of replacing one method of payment with another; a payment that is replaced with another
giving the same result whatever the order in which the quantities are shown
senses.chn: 交换的（排列次序不影响结果）

senses.def: a device that connects a motor to the electricity supply
a device for changing the direction in which electricity flows
to travel regularly by bus, train, car, etc. between your place of work and your home
senses.chn: （乘公共汽车、火车、汽车等）上下班往返，经常往返（于两地）

ex.en: She commutes from Oxford to London every day.
ex.cn: 她每天上下班往返于牛津与伦敦之间。

ex.en: He spent that year commuting between New York and Chicago.
ex.cn: 那年他穿梭来往于纽约与芝加哥之间。

ex.en: I live within commuting distance of Dublin.
ex.cn: 我住在离都柏林上下班可乘公交车往返的地方。

ex.en: People are prepared to commute long distances if they are desperate for work.
ex.cn: 亟需得到工作的人会愿意长途乘车往返上下班。

senses.def: to replace one punishment with another that is less severe
to exchange one form of payment, for sth else
the journey that a person makes when they commute to work

ex.en: a two-hour commute into downtown Washington
ex.cn: 去华盛顿中心区两小时的上下班路程

ex.en: I have only a short commute to work.
ex.cn: 我上班的路程很短。

senses.def: a person who travels into a city to work each day, usually from quite far away

ex.en: the commuter belt (= the area around a city where people live and from which they travel to work in the city)
ex.cn: 上班族居住地带

senses.def: (a person) from Comoros
senses.chn: 科摩罗人；科摩罗的；科摩罗人的

senses.def: a country consisting of a group of islands in the Indian Ocean
senses.chn: 科摩罗（印度洋的群岛国家）

senses.def: a complimentary ticket, meal, etc. (= one that you do not have to pay for)
smaller than is usual for things of the same kind

ex.en: a compact camera
ex.cn: 袖珍照相机

senses.def: using or filling only a small amount of space

ex.en: The kitchen was compact but well equipped.
ex.cn: 这间厨房虽然空间小但设备齐全。

senses.def: closely and firmly packed together

ex.en: a compact mass of earth
ex.cn: 一堆压得很结实的泥土

senses.def: small and strong

ex.en: He had a compact and muscular body.
ex.cn: 他个子矮小，身体健壮。

senses.def: a small car
a small flat box with a mirror, containing powder that women use on their faces
a formal agreement between two or more people or countries
to press sth together firmly

ex.en: a layer of compacted snow
ex.cn: 压紧的一层雪

senses.def: a friend or sb with whom you spend a lot of time
a person or an animal that travels with you or spends a lot of time with you

ex.en: travelling companions
ex.cn: 旅伴

ex.en: Fear was the hostages' constant companion.
ex.cn: 人质一直都感到恐惧不安。

senses.def: a person who has similar tastes, interests, etc. to your own and whose company you enjoy
senses.chn: （爱好、志趣等相投的）伙伴，同伴

ex.en: She was a charming dinner companion.
ex.cn: 与她同桌进餐使人感到十分高兴。

ex.en: His younger brother is not much of a companion for him.
ex.cn: 他的弟弟和他志趣不太相投。

ex.en: They're drinking companions (= they go out drinking together).
ex.cn: 他们是酒友。

senses.def: a person who shares in your work, pleasures, sadness, etc.

ex.en: We became companions in misfortune.
ex.cn: 我们成了患难之交。

senses.def: a person, usually a woman, employed to live with and help sb, especially sb old or ill/sick
senses.chn: 陪护（通常受雇照料老人或病人）

senses.def: one of a pair of things that go together or can be used together
senses.chn: 成对的物品之一；一副物品中的一个

ex.en: A companion volume is soon to be published.
ex.cn: 这卷书的姊妹篇即将问世。

senses.def: used in book titles to describe a book giving useful facts and information on a particular subject

ex.en: A Companion to French Literature
ex.cn: 《法国文学指南》

senses.def: friendly
senses.chn: 朋友般的；友好的；友善的

senses.def: the pleasant feeling that you have when you have a friendly relationship with sb and are not alone

ex.en: They meet at the club for companionship and advice.
ex.cn: 他们在俱乐部相会是为了联谊和寻求建议。

ex.en: She had only her cat for companionship.
ex.cn: 她只有猫儿做伴。

senses.def: a set of stairs on a ship
a business organization that makes money by producing or selling goods or services

ex.en: the largest computer company in the world
ex.cn: 全球最大的计算机公司

ex.en: the National Bus Company
ex.cn: 全国公共汽车公司

ex.en: She joined the company in 2009.
ex.cn: 她于 2009 年加入这家公司。

ex.en: Company profits were 5% lower than last year.
ex.cn: 公司的利润比去年降低了 5%。

senses.def: a group of people who work or perform together

ex.en: a theatre/dance, etc. company
ex.cn: 剧团、舞蹈团等

ex.en: the Royal Shakespeare Company
ex.cn: 皇家莎士比亚戏剧团

senses.def: the fact of being with sb else and not alone
