ex.en: I enjoy Jo's company (= I enjoy being with her).
ex.cn: 我喜欢和乔在一起。

ex.en: She enjoys her own company (= being by herself) when she is travelling.
ex.cn: 她喜爱独自旅行。

ex.en: The children are very good company (= pleasant to be with) at this age.
ex.cn: 和这个年龄的孩子在一起很开心。

ex.en: a pleasant evening in the company of friends
ex.cn: 与朋友一起度过的愉快夜晚

ex.en: He's coming with me for company.
ex.cn: 他要陪伴我一起来。

senses.def: guests in your house

ex.en: I didn't realize you had company.
ex.cn: 我不知道你有客人。

senses.def: a group of people together

ex.en: She told the assembled company what had happened.
ex.cn: 她把发生的事告诉了聚会的人。

ex.en: It is bad manners to whisper in company (= in a group of people).
ex.cn: 在众人面前窃窃私语是不礼貌的行为。

senses.def: a group of soldiers that is part of a battalion
the people that sb spends time with
senses.chn: 某人所交往的人；伙伴；与之为伍的人

ex.en: Judging by the company he kept, Mark must have been a wealthy man.
ex.cn: 根据马克所交往的人来判断，他一定是位富翁。

senses.def: to be friends with people that others disapprove of
together with or at the same time as sb/sth

ex.en: She arrived in company with the ship's captain.
ex.cn: 她与船长一起到达。

ex.en: The US dollar went through a difficult time, in company with the oil market.
ex.cn: 美元与石油市场同时经历了艰难时期。

senses.def: if you say that sb is in good company, you mean that they should not worry about a mistake, etc. because sb else, especially sb more important, has done the same thing
senses.chn: 无伤大雅（表示不必为错误等担忧，因为他人，尤其是更重要的人也犯过同样的错误）

senses.def: to stay with sb so that they are not alone

ex.en: I'll keep you company while you're waiting.
ex.cn: 你等待时我会陪伴你。

senses.def: used to suggest that it is better to be in a group of only two people than have a third person with you as well
to leave sb; to end a relationship with sb

ex.en: This is where we part company (= go in different directions).
ex.cn: 这就是我们分手的地方。

ex.en: The band have parted company with their manager.
ex.cn: 乐队与其经理人已散伙了。

ex.en: The band and their manager have parted company.
ex.cn: 乐队与其经理人已散伙了。

senses.def: to disagree with sb about sth

ex.en: Weber parted company with Marx on a number of important issues.
ex.cn: 韦伯与马克思在若干重大问题上意见有分歧。

senses.def: used after being rude or critical about sb to say that the people you are talking to are not included in the criticism
senses.chn: 在座诸位除外；与这里的各位无关

senses.def: a car which is provided by the company that you work for
similar to sb/sth else and able to be compared

ex.en: A comparable house in the south of the city would cost twice as much.
ex.cn: 一栋类似的房子位于城南就要贵一倍。

ex.en: The situation in the US is not directly comparable to that in the UK.
ex.cn: 美国的情况与英国的不能直接相比。

ex.en: Inflation is now at a rate comparable with that in other European countries.
ex.cn: 现在通货膨胀率已经和欧洲其他国家的差不多了。

senses.def: connected with studying things to find out how similar or different they are

ex.en: a comparative study of the educational systems of two countries
ex.cn: 两国教育制度的比较研究

ex.en: comparative linguistics
ex.cn: 比较语言学

senses.def: measured or judged by how similar or different it is to sth else

ex.en: Then he was living in comparative comfort (= compared with others or with his own life at a previous time).
ex.cn: 他那时生活比较舒适。

ex.en: The company is a comparative newcomer to the software market (= other companies have been in business much longer).
ex.cn: 就软件市场来说，这家公司相对而言就是新手了。

senses.def: relating to adjectives or adverbs that express more in amount, degree or quality, for example better, worse, slower and more difficult
senses.chn: （形容词或副词）比较级的（如 better、worse、slower 和 more difficult）

senses.def: the form of an adjective or adverb that expresses more in amount, degree or quality
senses.chn: （形容词或副词的）比较级形式

ex.en: 'Better' is the comparative of 'good' and 'more difficult' is the comparative of 'difficult'.
ex.cn: better 是 good 的比较级；more difficult 是 difficult 的比较级。

senses.def: as compared to sth/sb else

ex.en: The unit is comparatively easy to install and cheap to operate.
ex.cn: 这种设备比较容易安装而且用起来便宜。

ex.en: He died comparatively young (= at a younger age than most people die).
ex.cn: 他死时年纪并不大。

ex.en: comparatively few/low/rare/recent
ex.cn: 比较少／低／罕见；时间上相对较近的

senses.def: to examine people or things to see how they are similar and how they are different

ex.en: It is interesting to compare their situation and ours.
ex.cn: 把他们的状况与我们的相比很有意思。

ex.en: We compared the two reports carefully.
ex.cn: 我们仔细地比较了两个报告。

ex.en: We carefully compared the first report with the second.
ex.cn: 我们仔细比较了第一份报告和第二份报告。

ex.en: My own problems seem insignificant compared with other people's.
ex.cn: 与别人的问题相比，我自己的问题算不得什么。

ex.en: I've had some difficulties, but they were nothing compared to yours (= they were not nearly as bad as yours).
ex.cn: 我遇到了一些困难，但与你的困难比起来就算不上什么了。

ex.en: Standards in health care have improved enormously compared to 40 years ago.
ex.cn: 与 40 年前相比，卫生保健的水平得到了极大提高。

senses.def: to be similar to sb/sth else, either better or worse

ex.en: This school compares with the best in the country (= it is as good as them).
ex.cn: 这所学校可与全国最好的学校媲美。

ex.en: This house doesn't compare with our previous one (= it is not as good).
ex.cn: 这房子比不上我们以前的。

ex.en: Their prices compare favourably to those of their competitors. [transitive] ~ A to B to show or state that sb/sth is similar to sb/sth else
ex.cn: 表明…与…相似；将…比作

senses.def: if two or more people compare notes, they each say what they think about the same event, situation, etc.
it is impossible to say that one thing is better than another if the two are completely different
senses.chn: （因两样事物完全不同）不具可比性，不能相提并论

ex.en: They are both great but you can't compare apples and oranges.
ex.cn: 他们两个都很不错，但是不可相提并论。

senses.def: better than anything else of the same kind
the process of comparing two or more people or things

ex.en: Comparison with other oil-producing countries is extremely interesting.
ex.cn: 与其他石油生产国作一比较是很有意思的。

ex.en: I enclose the two plans for comparison.
ex.cn: 兹附上两份计划以供比较。

ex.en: The education system bears/stands no comparison with (= is not as good as) that in many Asian countries.
ex.cn: 这种教育制度比不上许多亚洲国家的教育制度。

senses.def: an occasion when two or more people or things are compared

ex.en: a comparison of the rail systems in Britain and France
ex.cn: 英国和法国铁路系统的比较

ex.en: a comparison of men's salaries with those of women
ex.cn: 男女薪酬的比较

ex.en: comparisons between Britain and the rest of Europe
ex.cn: 英国与欧洲其他国家之间的各种比较

ex.en: a comparison of the brain to a computer (= showing what is similar)
ex.cn: 将大脑比作计算机

ex.en: It is difficult to make a comparison with her previous book—they are completely different.
ex.cn: 这很难与她以前的书相比，两者是截然不同的。

ex.en: You can draw comparisons with the situation in Ireland (= say how the two situations are similar).
ex.cn: 这种情形可与爱尔兰的相比。

senses.def: used especially at the beginning of a sentence when the next thing that is mentioned is compared with sth in the previous sentence

ex.en: By comparison, expenditure on education increased last year.
ex.cn: 相比之下，去年教育经费增加了。

senses.def: when compared with sb/sth

ex.en: The second half of the game was dull by comparison with the first.
ex.cn: 与上半场相比，比赛的下半场有些沉闷。

ex.en: The tallest buildings in London are small in comparison with New York's skyscrapers.
ex.cn: 伦敦最高的建筑物与纽约的摩天大厦一比就相形见绌。

senses.def: used to emphasize the difference between two people or things that are being compared
senses.chn: （强调比较之下的差别）无法相比，根本不能相提并论

ex.en: In terms of price there's no comparison (= one thing is much more expensive than the other).
ex.cn: 在价格方面无法相比。

senses.def: to seem less important when compared with sth else

ex.en: Last year's riots pale in comparison with this latest outburst of violence.
ex.cn: 去年的骚乱与最近这次暴乱相比，可说是小巫见大巫。

senses.def: one of the separate sections which a coach/car on a train is divided into
senses.chn: （铁路客车车厢分隔成的）隔间

senses.def: one of the separate sections that sth such as a piece of furniture or equipment has for keeping things in
senses.chn: （家具或设备等的）分隔间，隔层

ex.en: The desk has a secret compartment.
ex.cn: 这书桌有一个秘密暗格。

ex.en: There is a handy storage compartment beneath the oven.
ex.cn: 在烤箱的下面有一个便利的橱柜。

senses.def: to divide sth into separate sections, especially so that one thing does not affect the other

ex.en: Life today is rigidly compartmentalized into work and leisure.
ex.cn: 当今的生活被严格划分为工作和休闲两部分。

senses.def: an instrument for finding direction, with a needle that always points to the north
senses.chn: 罗盘；罗经；指南针；罗盘仪

ex.en: a map and compass
ex.cn: 地图和指南针

ex.en: the points of the compass (= N, S, E, W, etc.)
ex.cn: 罗经方位点（东、南、西、北等）

senses.def: an instrument with two long thin parts joined together at the top, used for drawing circles and measuring distances on a map

ex.en: a pair of compasses
ex.cn: 一副圆规

senses.def: a range or an extent, especially of what can be achieved in a particular situation

ex.en: the compass of a singer's voice (= the range from the lowest to the highest note that he or she can sing)
ex.cn: 歌手的音域

senses.def: a strong feeling of sympathy for people who are suffering and a desire to help them

ex.en: to feel/show compassion
ex.cn: 感到／表示同情

senses.def: feeling or showing sympathy for people who are suffering
senses.chn: 有同情心的；表示怜悯的

ex.en: He was allowed to go home on compassionate grounds (= because he was suffering).
ex.cn: 他因为得到同情而获准回家。

senses.def: time that you are allowed to be away from work because sb in your family is ill/sick or has died
senses.chn: 恩恤休假；恩假（因家人生病或去世而准许的休假）

senses.def: the ability of people or things to live or exist together without problems
the ability of machines, especially computers, and computer programs to be used together
senses.chn: （尤指计算机及程序的）兼容性，相容性

senses.def: able to be used together

ex.en: The new system will be compatible with existing equipment.
ex.cn: 新的系统将与现有的设备相互兼容。

senses.def: able to exist or be used together without causing problems
senses.chn: 可共存的；可共用的；兼容的

ex.en: Are measures to protect the environment compatible with economic growth?
ex.cn: 保护环境的措施与经济的增长协调吗？

ex.en: compatible blood groups
ex.cn: 相容的血型

senses.def: if two people are compatible, they can have a good relationship because they have similar ideas, interests, etc.
senses.chn: （因思想、志趣等相投而）关系好的，和睦相处的

senses.def: a person who was born in, or is a citizen of, the same country as sb else

ex.en: He played against one of his compatriots in the semi-final.
ex.cn: 他在半决赛中与他的一位同胞选手对垒。

senses.def: to force sb to do sth; to make sth necessary

ex.en: The law can compel fathers to make regular payments for their children.
ex.cn: 这项法律可强制父亲定期支付子女的费用。

ex.en: I feel compelled to write and tell you how much I enjoyed your book.
ex.cn: 我觉得必须写信告诉你我是多么欣赏你的书。

ex.en: Last year ill health compelled his retirement.
ex.cn: 去年他因身体不好被迫退休了。

senses.def: to cause a particular reaction

ex.en: He spoke with an authority that compelled the attention of the whole crowd.
ex.cn: 他用权威的口气讲话，引起了整个人群的注意。

senses.def: that makes you pay attention to it because it is so interesting and exciting
senses.chn: 引人入胜的；扣人心弦的

ex.en: Her latest book makes compelling reading.
ex.cn: 她新出的书读起来扣人心弦。

ex.en: That's an interesting question, Daniel.
ex.cn: 那是个有趣的问题，丹尼尔。

ex.en: The exhibition tells the fascinating story of the steam age.
ex.cn: 展览讲述了蒸汽时代引人入胜的故事。

ex.en: Her latest book makes compelling reading.
ex.cn: 她新出的书读起来扣人心弦。

ex.en: Thank you for a most stimulating discussion.
ex.cn: 感谢你们妙趣横生的讨论。

ex.en: His books are always so gripping.
ex.cn: 他的书总是那么扣人心弦。

senses.def: so strong that you must do sth about it
senses.chn: 非常强烈的；不可抗拒的

ex.en: a compelling need/desire
ex.cn: 非常强烈的需要／欲望

senses.def: that makes you think it is true

ex.en: There is no compelling reason to believe him.
ex.cn: 没有令人信服的理由让人相信他。

ex.en: compelling evidence
ex.cn: 有说服力的证据

senses.def: containing all the necessary facts about sth

ex.en: a compendious description
ex.cn: 简要说明

senses.def: a collection of facts, drawings and photographs on a particular subject, especially in a book
senses.chn: （尤指书中某题材事实、图画及照片的）汇编，概要

senses.def: to provide sth good to balance or reduce the bad effects of damage, loss, etc.

ex.en: Nothing can compensate for the loss of a loved one.
ex.cn: 失去心爱的人是无法补偿的。

senses.def: to pay sb money because they have suffered some damage, loss, injury, etc.

ex.en: Her lawyers say she should be compensated for the suffering she had been caused.
ex.cn: 她的律师说她应该为所遭受的痛苦得到赔偿。

senses.def: something, especially money, that sb gives you because they have hurt you, or damaged sth that you own; the act of giving this to sb
senses.chn: 补偿（或赔偿）物；（尤指）赔偿金，补偿金；赔偿

ex.en: to claim/award/receive compensation
ex.cn: 要求／判给／得到赔偿金

ex.en: to pay compensation for injuries at work
ex.cn: 支付工伤赔偿金

ex.en: to receive £10 000 in compensation
ex.cn: 得到赔偿金 1 万英镑

senses.def: things that make a bad situation better
senses.chn: 使坏的情况变好的事物；（对不利局面的）补偿

ex.en: I wish I were young again, but getting older has its compensations.
ex.cn: 我要是能再次年轻就好了，但上了年纪也有上了年纪的好处。

senses.def: to try to be more successful or better than sb else who is trying to do the same as you

ex.en: Several companies are competing for the contract.
ex.cn: 为得到那项合同，几家公司正在竞争。

ex.en: We can't compete with them on price.
ex.cn: 我们在价格上无法与他们竞争。

ex.en: Young children will usually compete for their mother's attention.
ex.cn: 小孩子通常都会在母亲面前争宠。

ex.en: Small traders cannot compete in the face of cheap foreign imports.
ex.cn: 面对廉价的外国进口商品，经营规模小的商人无法与之抗衡。

ex.en: There are too many magazines competing to attract readers.
ex.cn: 竞相吸引读者的杂志太多了。

senses.def: to take part in a contest or game

ex.en: He's hoping to compete in the London marathon.
ex.cn: 他期盼着参加伦敦马拉松比赛。

senses.def: the ability to do sth well

ex.en: to gain a high level of competence in English
ex.cn: 获得高水平的英语能力

ex.en: professional/technical competence
ex.cn: 专业／技术能力

senses.def: the power that a court, an organization or a person has to deal with sth
senses.chn: （法庭、机构或人的）权限，管辖权

ex.en: The judge has to act within the competence of the court.
ex.cn: 法官必须在法庭的权限范围内行使权力。

ex.en: outside sb's area of competence
ex.cn: 超出某人的权限范围

senses.def: a skill that you need in a particular job or for a particular task

ex.en: The syllabus lists the knowledge and competences required at this level.
ex.cn: 教学大纲列出了这一级水平要求掌握的知识和技能。

senses.def: having enough skill or knowledge to do sth well or to the necessary standard
senses.chn: 足以胜任的；有能力的；称职的

ex.en: Make sure the firm is competent to carry out the work.
ex.cn: 要确保这家公司有能力完成这项工作。

ex.en: He's very competent in his work.
ex.cn: 他工作十分称职。

senses.def: of a good standard but not very good
having the power to decide sth

ex.en: The case was referred to a competent authority.
ex.cn: 事情已交给有关当局处理。

senses.def: a situation in which people or organizations compete with each other for sth that not everyone can have

ex.en: There is now intense competition between schools to attract students.
ex.cn: 现在学校之间为了招揽学生展开了激烈竞争。

ex.en: We are in competition with four other companies for the contract.
ex.cn: 我们在与其他四家公司竞争这项合同。

ex.en: We won the contract in the face of stiff competition.
ex.cn: 面对激烈的竞争，我们赢得了这项合同。

senses.def: an event in which people compete with each other to find out who is the best at sth

ex.en: a music/photo, etc. competition
ex.cn: 音乐、摄影等比赛

ex.en: to enter/win/lose a competition
ex.cn: 参加／赢得／输掉比赛

senses.def: the people who are competing against sb

ex.en: We'll be able to assess the competition at the conference.
ex.cn: 我们可以在会上对竞争对手进行估量。

senses.def: used to describe a situation in which people or organizations compete against each other

ex.en: competitive games/sports
ex.cn: 竞技性的比赛／体育运动

ex.en: Graduates have to fight for jobs in a highly competitive market.
ex.cn: 毕业生不得不在竞争激烈的市场上奋力争取工作。

senses.def: as good as or better than others
senses.chn: （与…）一样好的；（比…）更好的；有竞争力的

ex.en: a shop selling clothes at competitive prices (= as low as any other shop)
ex.cn: 在服装价格上有竞争力的商店

ex.en: We need to work harder to remain competitive with other companies.
ex.cn: 我们需要更加努力工作以便在与其他公司的竞争中不落下风。

ex.en: to gain a competitive advantage over rival companies
ex.cn: 占有超越对手公司的竞争优势

ex.en: a bottle of cheap perfume
ex.cn: 一瓶低价劣质香水

senses.def: trying very hard to be better than others
senses.chn: 努力竞争的；一心求胜的

ex.en: You have to be highly competitive to do well in sport these days.
ex.cn: 如今你必须有强烈的竞争意识才能在体育运动中取得好成绩。

senses.def: a person or an organization that competes against others, especially in business
senses.chn: （尤指商业方面的）竞争者，对手

ex.en: our main/major competitor
ex.cn: 我们主要的竞争对手

senses.def: a person who takes part in a competition

ex.en: Over 200 competitors entered the race.
ex.cn: 200 多名选手参加了赛跑。

senses.def: a collection of items, especially pieces of music or writing, taken from different places and put together

ex.en: Her latest album is a compilation of all her best singles.
ex.cn: 她的最新专辑收录了她所有的最佳单曲。

ex.en: a compilation album
ex.cn: 一张选辑

senses.def: the process of compiling sth

ex.en: the compilation of a dictionary
ex.cn: 词典的编纂

senses.def: to produce a book, list, report, etc. by bringing together different items, articles, songs, etc.
senses.chn: 编写（书、列表、报告等）；编纂

ex.en: We are trying to compile a list of suitable people for the job.
ex.cn: 我们在努力编制一份适合做这项工作的人员的名单。

ex.en: The album was compiled from live recordings from last year's tour.
ex.cn: 这张专辑由去年巡回演出的实况录音汇编而成。

senses.def: to translate instructions from one computer language into another so that a particular computer can understand them
a person who compiles sth
a program that translates instructions from one computer language into another for a computer to understand
a feeling of satisfaction with yourself or with a situation, so that you do not think any change is necessary; the state of being complacent

ex.en: Despite signs of an improvement in the economy, there is no room for complacency.
ex.cn: 尽管在经济方面有改善的迹象，但仍不容自满。

senses.def: too satisfied with yourself or with a situation, so that you do not feel that any change is necessary; showing or feeling complacency
senses.chn: 自满的；自鸣得意的；表现出自满的

ex.en: a dangerously complacent attitude to the increase in unemployment
ex.cn: 对失业增加抱满不在乎的危险态度

ex.en: We must not become complacent about progress.
ex.cn: 我们决不能因进步变得自满。

senses.def: to say that you are annoyed, unhappy or not satisfied about sb/sth

ex.en: I'm going to complain to the manager about this.
ex.cn: 我要就这件事向经理投诉。

ex.en: The defendant complained of intimidation during the investigation.
ex.cn: 被告申诉在调查期间受到了恐吓。

ex.en: She never complains, but she's obviously exhausted.
ex.cn: 她虽然从不抱怨，但显然已疲惫不堪。

ex.en: 'How are you?' 'Oh, I can't complain (= I'm all right).'
ex.cn: “你好吗？” “啊，没的抱怨的。”

ex.en: He complained bitterly that he had been unfairly treated.
ex.cn: 他愤懑地诉说他所受到的不公平待遇。

ex.en: 'It's not fair,' she complained.
ex.cn: “这不公平。” 她抱怨道。

senses.def: to say that you feel ill/sick or are suffering from a pain

ex.en: She left early, complaining of a headache.
ex.cn: 她说自己头疼，很早就离开了。

senses.def: to say that you feel ill/sick or are suffering from a pain

ex.en: She left early, complaining of a headache.
ex.cn: 她说自己头疼，很早就离开了。

senses.def: a reason for not being satisfied; a statement that sb makes saying that they are not satisfied
senses.chn: 不满的原因；抱怨；埋怨；投诉；控告

ex.en: The most common complaint is about poor service.
ex.cn: 最常见的投诉与服务差有关。

ex.en: We received a number of complaints from customers about the lack of parking facilities.
ex.cn: 我们收到了来自顾客的许多投诉，抱怨缺乏停车设施。

ex.en: I'd like to make a complaint about the noise.
ex.cn: 我要就噪音问题提出投诉。

ex.en: I believe you have a complaint against one of our nurses.
ex.cn: 我认为你对我们的一位护士有怨言。

ex.en: a complaint that he had been unfairly treated
ex.cn: 对他受到了不公正待遇的投诉

ex.en: a formal complaint
ex.cn: 正式控告

senses.def: the act of complaining

ex.en: I can see no grounds for complaint.
ex.cn: 我找不到抱怨的理由。

ex.en: a letter of complaint
ex.cn: 投诉信

ex.en: I'm afraid I'm not satisfied with this.
ex.cn: 恐怕我对此不太满意。

ex.en: I'm sorry. This isn't acceptable/good enough. We've been waiting half an hour.
ex.cn: 对不起，这是不可接受的。我们已经等半个小时了。

ex.en: I'd like to make a complaint. The radio I bought doesn't work.
ex.cn: 我要投诉。我买的收音机有故障。

ex.en: Excuse me—this isn't what I asked for. I'm having/I ordered the soup, not the salad.
ex.cn: 对不起，这不是我点的。我要的是汤，不是色拉。

senses.def: an illness, especially one that is not serious, and often one that affects a particular part of the body
senses.chn: （尤指不严重、常影响身体某部位的）疾病

ex.en: a skin complaint
ex.cn: 皮肤病

senses.def: ready to accept other people's actions and opinions and to do what other people want
with skin and a complexion of the type mentioned

ex.en: fair/dark complected
ex.cn: 肤色白皙／黝黑

senses.def: to add to sth in a way that improves it or makes it more attractive
senses.chn: 补充；补足；使完美；使更具吸引力

ex.en: The excellent menu is complemented by a good wine list.
ex.cn: 佳肴佐以美酒，堪称完美无缺。

ex.en: The team needs players who complement each other.
ex.cn: 球队需要能够相互取长补短的队员。

ex.en: She complimented me on my English.
ex.cn: 她夸奖我的英语好。

ex.en: The different flavours complement each other perfectly.
ex.cn: 不同的味道搭配在一起，可口极了。

ex.en: She made some very complimentary remarks about my English.
ex.cn: 她对我的英语赞赏有加。

ex.en: There was a complimentary basket of fruit in our room.
ex.cn: 我们房间里有一篮免费赠送的水果。

senses.def: a thing that adds new qualities to sth in a way that improves it or makes it more attractive
the complete number or quantity needed or allowed

ex.en: We've taken our full complement of trainees this year.
ex.cn: 我们今年接收的实习生已满员。

senses.def: a word or phrase, especially an adjective or a noun, that is used after linking verbs such as be and become, and describes the subject of the verb. In some descriptions of grammar it is used to refer to any word or phrase which is governed by a verb and usually comes after the verb in a sentence.

ex.en: In the sentences 'I'm angry' and 'He became a politician', 'angry' and 'politician' are complements.
ex.cn: 在句子 I'm angry 和 He became a politician 中，angry 和 politician 为补语。

senses.def: two people or things that are complementary are different but together form a useful or attractive combination of skills, qualities or physical features
senses.chn: 互补的；补充的；相互补足的

ex.en: The school's approach must be complementary to that of the parents.
ex.cn: 学校与家长的教育方法必须相辅相成。

ex.en: She complimented me on my English.
ex.cn: 她夸奖我的英语好。

ex.en: The different flavours complement each other perfectly.
ex.cn: 不同的味道搭配在一起，可口极了。

ex.en: She made some very complimentary remarks about my English.
ex.cn: 她对我的英语赞赏有加。

ex.en: There was a complimentary basket of fruit in our room.
ex.cn: 我们房间里有一篮免费赠送的水果。

ex.en: The team members have different but complementary skills.
ex.cn: 队员技术不同但能互补。

senses.def: either of two angles which together make 90°
a colour that, when mixed with another colour, gives black or white
senses.chn: 互补色，补色（与另外一种颜色混合成为黑色或白色的颜色）

senses.def: a colour that gives the greatest contrast when combined with a particular colour
senses.chn: 对比色（与某特定颜色形成最大色差的颜色）

ex.en: The designer has chosen the complementary colours blue and orange.
ex.cn: 设计师选取了蓝和橙黄两种对比色。

senses.def: medical treatment that is not part of the usual scientific treatment used in Western countries, for example acupuncture
senses.chn: 辅助性医疗（不属于西方国家通常采用的科学疗法，如针灸）

senses.def: the fact of complementing sth
the complements of a verb in a clause
a word or part of a word that shows a clause is being used as a complement
used when you are emphasizing sth, to mean 'to the greatest degree possible'

ex.en: We were in complete agreement.
ex.cn: 我们意见完全一致。

ex.en: a complete change
ex.cn: 彻底的变化

ex.en: in complete silence
ex.cn: 万籁俱寂

ex.en: a complete stranger
ex.cn: 素不相识的人

ex.en: It came as a complete surprise.
ex.cn: 这事来得十分意外。

ex.en: I felt a complete idiot.
ex.cn: 我觉得自己是个十足的笨蛋。

senses.def: including all the parts, etc. that are necessary; whole

ex.en: I've collected the complete set.
ex.cn: 我收集了全套。

ex.en: a complete guide to events in Oxford
ex.cn: 牛津活动盛事完全手册

ex.en: the complete works of Tolstoy
ex.cn: 托尔斯泰全集

ex.en: You will receive payment for each complete day that you work.
ex.cn: 你将按你每一整天的工作领取报酬。

senses.def: including sth as an extra part or feature
senses.chn: 包括，含有（额外部分或特征）

ex.en: The furniture comes complete with tools and instructions for assembly.
ex.cn: 这件家具备有组装工具和说明书。

ex.en: The book, complete with CD, costs £35.
ex.cn: 此书包括光盘，售价 35 英镑。

senses.def: finished

ex.en: Work on the office building will be complete at the end of the year.
ex.cn: 办公大楼工程将于年底竣工。

senses.def: to finish making or doing sth

ex.en: She's just completed a master's degree in Law.
ex.cn: 她刚读完法律硕士学位。

ex.en: The project should be completed within a year.
ex.cn: 这项工程必须在一年之内完成。

senses.def: to write all the information you are asked for on a form

ex.en: 2 000 shoppers completed our questionnaire.
ex.cn: 2 000 名顾客填写了我们的调查表。

senses.def: to make sth whole or perfect

ex.en: I only need one more card to complete the set.
ex.cn: 我只差一张卡片就配齐全套了。

senses.def: in every way possible

ex.en: completely different
ex.cn: 截然不同

ex.en: completely and utterly broke
ex.cn: 彻底破产

ex.en: I've completely forgotten her name.
ex.cn: 我完全把她的名字给忘了。

ex.en: The explosion completely destroyed the building.
ex.cn: 爆炸完全毁掉了那栋大楼。

senses.def: the act or process of finishing sth; the state of being finished and complete

ex.en: the completion of the new hospital building
ex.cn: 新医院大楼的竣工

ex.en: Satisfactory completion of the course does not ensure you a job.
ex.cn: 圆满完成课程并不能保证你能得到工作。

ex.en: The project is due for completion in the spring.
ex.cn: 这项工程预定在明年春季竣工。

ex.en: The road is nearing completion (= it is nearly finished).
ex.cn: 这条道路快要完工了。

ex.en: the date of completion/the completion date
ex.cn: 竣工日期

senses.def: the formal act of completing the sale of property, for example the sale of a house
senses.chn: （房地产等的）完成交易，完成交割

senses.def: made of many different things or parts that are connected; difficult to understand

ex.en: complex machinery
ex.cn: 结构复杂的机器

ex.en: the complex structure of the human brain
ex.cn: 错综复杂的人脑构造

ex.en: a complex argument/problem/subject
ex.cn: 复杂难懂的论证／问题／科目

senses.def: containing one main part (= the root of a word or main clause or of a sentence) and one or more other parts (called affixes or subordinate clauses)
senses.chn: 复合的（指词根加有词缀或主句含有从句）

senses.def: a group of buildings of a similar type together in one place

ex.en: a sports complex
ex.cn: 综合体育场

ex.en: an industrial complex (= a site with many factories)
ex.cn: 工业建筑群

ex.en: We have a buyer who would like to view the property.
ex.cn: 我们有一买主想看看这房产。

ex.en: The price of property has risen enormously.
ex.cn: 房地产的价格大幅上升了。

ex.en: The company is looking for larger premises.
ex.cn: 这家公司正在寻找更大的营业场所。

ex.en: a leisure complex
ex.cn: 休闲活动中心

senses.def: a group of things that are connected

ex.en: This is just one of a whole complex of issues.
ex.cn: 这仅仅是所有相关的问题之一。

senses.def: a mental state that is not normal
senses.chn: 不正常的精神状态；情结

ex.en: to suffer from a guilt complex
ex.cn: 蒙受负罪感之苦

senses.def: if sb has a complex about sth, they are worried about it in way that is not normal
the natural colour and condition of the skin on a person's face

ex.en: a pale/bad complexion
ex.cn: 苍白的／病态的脸色

senses.def: the general character of sth

ex.en: a move which changed the political complexion of the country
ex.cn: 改变国家政局的举措

senses.def: to change the way that a situation appears
the state of being formed of many parts; the state of being difficult to understand

ex.en: the increasing complexity of modern telecommunication systems
ex.cn: 日益复杂的现代电信系统

ex.en: I was astonished by the size and complexity of the problem.
ex.cn: 这个问题的复杂性和涉及面之广使我感到惊讶。

senses.def: the features of a problem or situation that are difficult to understand

ex.en: the complexities of the system
ex.cn: 这一系统的复杂之处

senses.def: a number containing both a real number and an imaginary number
the practice of obeying rules or requests made by people in authority

ex.en: procedures that must be followed to ensure full compliance with the law
ex.cn: 为确保严格遵守法律所必须遵行的程序

ex.en: Safety measures were carried out in compliance with paragraph 6 of the building regulations.
ex.cn: 遵照建筑规程的第 6 条实施了安全措施。

senses.def: too willing to agree with other people or to obey rules
senses.chn: 顺从的；百依百顺的；俯首帖耳的

ex.en: By then, Henry seemed less compliant with his wife's wishes than he had six months before.
ex.cn: 与六个月以前相比，亨利当时对他妻子的意愿似乎已不那么百依百顺了。

ex.en: We should not be producing compliant students who do not dare to criticize.
ex.cn: 我们不应当把学生培养成不敢批评的唯唯诺诺的人。

senses.def: in agreement with a set of rules
senses.chn: （与一系列规则）符合的，一致的

ex.en: This site is HTML compliant.
ex.cn: 这个网站支持 HTML 语言。

senses.def: to make sth more difficult to do, understand or deal with

ex.en: I do not wish to complicate the task more than is necessary.
ex.cn: 我不想使这项任务不必要地复杂化。

ex.en: To complicate matters further, there will be no transport available till 8 o'clock.
ex.cn: 使事情更难办的是 8 点钟之前不会有交通工具。

ex.en: The issue is complicated by the fact that a vital document is missing.
ex.cn: 一份重要文件的丢失使这个问题复杂化了。

senses.def: made of many different things or parts that are connected; difficult to understand

ex.en: a complicated system
ex.cn: 复杂的系统

ex.en: The instructions look very complicated.
ex.cn: 这说明书看起来很难懂。

ex.en: It's all very complicated—but I'll try and explain.
ex.cn: 尽管这一切都很难理解，但我会尽力解释。

senses.def: a thing that makes a situation more complicated or difficult
senses.chn: 使更复杂化（或更困难）的事物

ex.en: The bad weather added a further complication to our journey.
ex.cn: 恶劣的天气给我们的旅行增加了更多的困难。

senses.def: a new problem or illness that makes treatment of a previous one more complicated or difficult

ex.en: She developed complications after the surgery.
ex.cn: 她手术后出现了并发症。

senses.def: involved with other people in sth wrong or illegal
senses.chn: （与某人在某事上）同谋的，串通的

ex.en: Several officers were complicit in the cover-up.
ex.cn: 几名军官串通一气隐瞒真相。

senses.def: the act of taking part with another person in a crime

ex.en: to be guilty of complicity in the murder
ex.cn: 犯凶杀同谋罪

ex.en: evident complicity between the two brothers
ex.cn: 两兄弟间明显的串通一气

senses.def: a remark that expresses praise or admiration of sb

ex.en: to pay sb a compliment (= to praise them for sth)
ex.cn: 对某人表示赞扬

ex.en: 'You understand the problem because you're so much older.' 'I'll take that as a compliment!'
ex.cn: “您是能理解这个问题的，因为您年纪大那么多。” “就当你这是夸奖吧！”

ex.en: It's a great compliment to be asked to do the job.
ex.cn: 获聘请做这项工作是一项极大的荣誉。

ex.en: to return the compliment (= to treat sb in the same way as they have treated you)
ex.cn: 照样回敬

senses.def: polite words or good wishes, especially when used to express praise and admiration

ex.en: My compliments to the chef!
ex.cn: 请向厨师代为致意！

ex.en: Compliments of the season!(= for Christmas or the New Year)
ex.cn: 谨致节日的祝贺！（圣诞节或新年时的贺辞）

ex.en: Please accept these flowers with the compliments of (= as a gift from) the manager.
ex.cn: 请接受经理送的鲜花。

senses.def: to tell sb that you like or admire sth they have done, their appearance, etc.

ex.en: She complimented him on his excellent German.
ex.cn: 她夸奖他德语棒极了。

ex.en: She complimented me on my English.
ex.cn: 她夸奖我的英语好。

ex.en: The different flavours complement each other perfectly.
ex.cn: 不同的味道搭配在一起，可口极了。

ex.en: She made some very complimentary remarks about my English.
ex.cn: 她对我的英语赞赏有加。

ex.en: There was a complimentary basket of fruit in our room.
ex.cn: 我们房间里有一篮免费赠送的水果。

ex.en: The team members have different but complementary skills.
ex.cn: 队员技术不同但能互补。

senses.def: given free

ex.en: complimentary tickets for the show
ex.cn: 演出赠券

senses.def: expressing admiration, praise, etc.

ex.en: a complimentary remark
ex.cn: 赞美的言辞

ex.en: She was extremely complimentary about his work.
ex.cn: 她对他的工作给予了高度评价。

senses.def: a small piece of paper printed with the name of a company, that is sent out together with information, goods, etc.
senses.chn: （附在信息、货物等上印有公司名称的）赠礼便条，礼帖

senses.def: to obey a rule, an order, etc.

ex.en: They refused to comply with the UN resolution.
ex.cn: 他们拒绝遵守联合国的决议。

senses.def: money that is paid to a worker if he/she gets injured at work
one of several parts of which sth is made

ex.en: the components of a machine
ex.cn: 机器部件

ex.en: the car component industry
ex.cn: 汽车零部件制造业

ex.en: Key components of the government's plan are…
ex.cn: 政府计划的主要组成部分是…

ex.en: Trust is a vital component in any relationship.
ex.cn: 在任何关系中，信任都是一个至关重要的因素。

senses.def: the study of meaning by analysing the different parts of words
to behave in a particular way

ex.en: She always comports herself with great dignity.
ex.cn: 她的举止总是很端庄。

senses.def: the way in which sb/sth behaves

ex.en: She won admiration for her comportment during the trial.
ex.cn: 她在选拔赛中的表现得到了赞赏。

senses.def: to combine together to form a whole

ex.en: Ten men compose the committee.
ex.cn: 委员会由十人组成。

senses.def: to write music

ex.en: Mozart composed his last opera shortly before he died.
ex.cn: 莫扎特在创作出他最后一部歌剧后不久便去世了。

senses.def: to write a letter, etc. usually with a lot of care and thought

ex.en: She composed a letter of protest.
ex.cn: 她写了一封抗议信。

senses.def: to manage to control your feelings or expression

ex.en: Emma frowned, making an effort to compose herself.
ex.cn: 埃玛皱起了眉头，努力使自己镇定下来。

ex.en: I was so confused that I could hardly compose my thoughts.
ex.cn: 我心烦意乱难以镇定思绪。

senses.def: to be made or formed from several parts, things or people

ex.en: The committee is composed mainly of lawyers.
ex.cn: 委员会主要由律师组成。

ex.en: Their diet consists largely of vegetables.
ex.cn: 他们的日常饮食以蔬菜为主。

ex.en: The collection comprises 327 paintings.
ex.cn: 这组收藏有 327 幅画。

ex.en: Older people comprise a large proportion of those living in poverty.
ex.cn: 在那些生活贫困的人中，老年人占很大的比例。

ex.en: Women make up 56% of the student numbers.
ex.cn: 女生占学生人数的 56%。

ex.en: People under the age of 40 constitute the majority of the labour force. *
ex.cn: 40 岁以下的人占劳动力的大多数。

senses.def: calm and in control of your feelings

ex.en: She seemed outwardly composed.
ex.cn: 她表面上好像很镇静。

senses.def: a person who writes music, especially classical music
senses.chn: （尤指古典音乐的）创作者；作曲者；作曲家

senses.def: made of different parts or materials

ex.en: a composite picture (= one made from several pictures)
ex.cn: 合成照片

senses.def: something made by putting together different parts or materials
senses.chn: 合成物；混合物；复合材料

ex.en: The document was a composite of information from various sources.
ex.cn: 这份文件是不同来源信息的综合。

senses.def: a set of drawings of different features that can be put together to form the face of a person, especially sb wanted by the police, using descriptions given by people who saw the person; a picture made in this way
senses.chn: 容貌拼图（根据目击者描述拼制出人的面部画像，尤用于警方要捉拿的人）

senses.def: the different parts which sth is made of; the way in which the different parts are organized

ex.en: the chemical composition of the soil
ex.cn: 土壤的化学成分

ex.en: the composition of the board of directors
ex.cn: 董事会的组成

ex.en: the structure of the building/human body
ex.cn: 建筑物／人体结构

ex.en: the social structure of society
ex.cn: 社会的社会结构

ex.en: the grammatical structures of a language
ex.cn: 一种语言的语法结构

ex.en: a salary structure
ex.cn: 工资结构

senses.def: a piece of music or art, or a poem

ex.en: one of Beethoven's finest compositions
ex.cn: 贝多芬最优美的音乐作品之一

senses.def: the act of composing sth

ex.en: pieces performed in the order of their composition
ex.cn: 按作曲顺序表演的作品

senses.def: the art of writing music

ex.en: to study composition
ex.cn: 学习作曲艺术

senses.def: a short text that is written as a school exercise; a short essay
the arrangement of people or objects in a painting or photograph
a person who arranges text on a page before printing
having full control of your mind
senses.chn: 能完全控制神志；心智健全

senses.def: a mixture of decayed plants, food, etc. that can be added to soil to help plants grow

ex.en: potting compost (= a mixture of soil and compost that you can buy to grow new plants in)
ex.cn: 盆栽混合肥料

senses.def: to make sth into compost
to put compost on or in sth
a container in the garden where leaves, plants, etc. are put to make compost
senses.chn: （花园里的）堆肥桶；落叶垃圾桶

senses.def: a place in the garden where leaves, plants, etc. are piled, to make compost
senses.chn: （花园里的）堆肥处；园中落叶堆

senses.def: the state of being calm and in control of your feelings or behaviour

ex.en: to keep/lose/recover/regain your composure
ex.cn: 保持／失去／恢复镇静

senses.def: a cold dessert (= a sweet dish) made of fruit that has been cooked slowly with sugar
senses.chn: （加糖慢火煮过后冷却的）糖渍水果，蜜饯

senses.def: a thing consisting of two or more separate things combined together
a substance formed by a chemical reaction of two or more elements in fixed amounts relative to each other

ex.en: Common salt is a compound of sodium and chlorine.
ex.cn: 普通食盐是钠和氯的化合物。

senses.def: a noun, an adjective or a verb made of two or more words or parts of words, written as one or more words, or joined by a hyphen. Travel agent, dark-haired and bathroom are all compounds.
an area surrounded by a fence or wall in which a factory or other group of buildings stands
senses.chn: 有围栏（或围墙）的场地（内有工厂或其他建筑群）

ex.en: a prison compound
ex.cn: 监狱场地

senses.def: formed of two or more parts

ex.en: a compound adjective, such as fair-skinned
ex.cn: 复合形容词，如 fair-skinned

ex.en: A compound sentence contains two or more clauses.
ex.cn: 复合句包含两个或多个从句。

senses.def: to make sth bad become even worse by causing further damage or problems

ex.en: The problems were compounded by severe food shortages.
ex.cn: 严重的食物短缺使问题进一步恶化。

senses.def: to be formed from sth

ex.en: The DNA molecule is compounded from many smaller molecules.
ex.cn: 脱氧核糖核酸分子是由许多更小的分子组成的。

senses.def: to mix sth together

ex.en: liquid soaps compounded with disinfectant
ex.cn: 用消毒剂混合制成的皂液

senses.def: to pay or charge interest on an amount of money that includes any interest already earned or charged
an eye like that of most insects, made up of several parts that work separately
an injury in which a bone in the body is broken and part of the bone comes through the skin
interest that is paid both on the original amount of money saved and on the interest that has been added to it
to understand sth fully

ex.en: He stood staring at the dead body, unable to comprehend.
ex.cn: 他站在那里，盯着那具尸体，弄不明白是怎么回事。

ex.en: The infinite distances of space are too great for the human mind to comprehend.
ex.cn: 太空的广阔无垠是人类无法理解的。

ex.en: She could not comprehend how someone would risk people's lives in that way.
ex.cn: 她不明白怎么会有人竟拿人们的生命那样去冒险。

ex.en: He simply could not comprehend that she could be guilty.
ex.cn: 他就是搞不懂她怎么会有罪。

ex.en: I don't understand the instructions.
ex.cn: 我不懂这些指令的意思。

ex.en: Doctors still don't understand much about the disease.
ex.cn: 医生对这种疾病还了解不多。

senses.def: that can be understood by sb

ex.en: easily/readily comprehensible to the average reader
ex.cn: 一般读者容易懂的

senses.def: the ability to understand

ex.en: speech and comprehension
ex.cn: 说话能力和理解力

ex.en: His behaviour was completely beyond comprehension (= impossible to understand).
ex.cn: 他的举止完全令人费解。

ex.en: She had no comprehension of what was involved.
ex.cn: 她不明白所涉及的事情。

senses.def: an exercise that trains students to understand a language
senses.chn: （语言学习中的）理解练习（或训练）

ex.en: listening comprehension
ex.cn: 听力练习

ex.en: a reading comprehension
ex.cn: 阅读理解练习

senses.def: including all, or almost all, the items, details, facts, information, etc., that may be concerned
senses.chn: 全部的；所有的；（几乎）无所不包的；详尽的

ex.en: a comprehensive list of addresses
ex.cn: 详尽的地址目录

ex.en: a comprehensive study
ex.cn: 全面的研究

ex.en: comprehensive insurance (= covering all risks)
ex.cn: 综合保险

senses.def: designed for students of all abilities in the same school
senses.chn: 综合性的（接收各种资质的学生）

senses.def: (in Britain) a secondary school for young people of all levels of ability
senses.chn: （英国为各种资质的学生设立的）综合中学

senses.def: completely; thoroughly

ex.en: They were comprehensively beaten in the final.
ex.cn: 他们在决赛中一败涂地。

senses.def: to press or squeeze sth together or into a smaller space; to be pressed or squeezed in this way

ex.en: compressed air/gas
ex.cn: 压缩空气／气体

ex.en: Her lips compressed into a thin line.
ex.cn: 她的双唇抿成了一道缝。

senses.def: to reduce sth and fit it into a smaller space or amount of time

ex.en: The main arguments were compressed into one chapter.
ex.cn: 主要的论证被压缩为一个章节。

senses.def: to make computer files, etc. smaller so that they use less space on a disk, etc.
a cloth that is pressed onto a part of the body to stop the loss of blood, reduce pain, etc.
a machine that compresses air or other gases
to have sb/sth as parts or members

ex.en: The collection comprises 327 paintings.
ex.cn: 那一组收藏有 327 幅画。

ex.en: The committee is comprised of representatives from both the public and private sectors.
ex.cn: 委员会由政府和私人部门的双方代表组成。

senses.def: to be the parts or members that form sth
senses.chn: 是（某事物的）组成部分；组成；构成

ex.en: Older people comprise a large proportion of those living in poverty.
ex.cn: 在那些生活贫困的人中，老年人占有很大的比例。

ex.en: Their diet consists largely of vegetables.
ex.cn: 他们的日常饮食以蔬菜为主。

ex.en: The collection comprises 327 paintings.
ex.cn: 这组收藏有 327 幅画。

ex.en: Older people comprise a large proportion of those living in poverty.
ex.cn: 在那些生活贫困的人中，老年人占很大的比例。

ex.en: Women make up 56% of the student numbers.
ex.cn: 女生占学生人数的 56%。

ex.en: People under the age of 40 constitute the majority of the labour force. *
ex.cn: 40 岁以下的人占劳动力的大多数。

senses.def: an agreement made between two people or groups in which each side gives up some of the things they want so that both sides are happy at the end

ex.en: After lengthy talks the two sides finally reached a compromise.
ex.cn: 双方经过长期的商谈终于达成了妥协。

ex.en: In any relationship, you have to make compromises.
ex.cn: 在任何关系当中，人们都得作出让步。

ex.en: a compromise solution/agreement/candidate
ex.cn: 折中的解决方案／协议／候选人

senses.def: a solution to a problem in which two or more things cannot exist together as they are, in which each thing is reduced or changed slightly so that they can exist together

ex.en: This model represents the best compromise between price and quality.
ex.cn: 这种型号是平衡了价格和质量的最佳折中方案。

senses.def: the act of reaching a compromise

ex.en: Compromise is an inevitable part of life.
ex.cn: 妥协是生活不可避免的一部分。

ex.en: There is no prospect of compromise in sight.
ex.cn: 目前还没有和解的希望。

senses.def: to give up some of your demands after a disagreement with sb, in order to reach an agreement
senses.chn: （为达成协议而）妥协，折中，让步

ex.en: Neither side is prepared to compromise.
ex.cn: 双方都不愿意妥协。

ex.en: After much argument, the judges finally compromised on (= agreed to give the prize to) the 18-year old pianist.
ex.cn: 经过激烈争论，评委终于同意那个 18 岁的钢琴演奏者获奖。

ex.en: They were unwilling to compromise with the terrorists.
ex.cn: 他们不愿与恐怖分子妥协。

senses.def: to do sth that is against your principles or does not reach standards that you have set

ex.en: I refuse to compromise my principles.
ex.cn: 我拒绝在原则问题上妥协。

ex.en: We are not prepared to compromise on safety standards.
ex.cn: 我们不愿在安全标准问题上放松。

senses.def: to bring sb/sth/yourself into danger or under suspicion, especially by acting in a way that is not very sensible
senses.chn: （尤指因行为不很明智）使陷入危险，使受到怀疑

ex.en: She had already compromised herself by accepting his invitation.
ex.cn: 她接受了他的邀请，这件事已经使她的声誉受到了损害。

ex.en: Defeat at this stage would compromise their chances (= reduce their chances) of reaching the finals of the competition.
ex.cn: 在这个阶段的失败会减少他们进入决赛的机会。

senses.def: if sth is compromising, it shows or tells people sth that you want to keep secret, because it is wrong or embarrassing
senses.chn: 有失体面的；不宜泄露的

ex.en: compromising photos
ex.cn: 不宜公开的照片

ex.en: They were discovered together in a compromising situation.
ex.cn: 他们被人发现在一起，场面有伤风化。

senses.def: strong pressure that makes sb do sth that they do not want to do

ex.en: You are under no compulsion to pay immediately.
ex.cn: 没有人强迫你立刻付款。

ex.en: There are no compulsions on students to attend classes.
ex.cn: 没有强求学生上课。

senses.def: a strong desire to do sth, especially sth that is wrong, silly or dangerous
senses.chn: （尤指做不正确、愚蠢或危险事的）强烈欲望，冲动

ex.en: He felt a great compulsion to tell her everything.
ex.cn: 他感到一阵强烈的冲动，想要把一切都告诉她。

senses.def: that is difficult to stop or control

ex.en: compulsive eating/spending/gambling
ex.cn: 强迫性进食／消费；上瘾的赌博

senses.def: not being able to control their behaviour
senses.chn: 无法控制行为的；禁不住的

ex.en: a compulsive drinker/gambler/liar
ex.cn: 酗酒成性的酒徒；嗜赌成癖的赌徒；说谎成性的人

senses.def: that makes you pay attention to it because it is so interesting and exciting

ex.en: The programme made compulsive viewing.
ex.cn: 这节目引人入胜，收看起来欲罢不能。

senses.def: that must be done because of a law or a rule
senses.chn: （因法律或规则而）必须做的，强制的，强迫的

ex.en: It is compulsory for all motorcyclists to wear helmets.
ex.cn: 所有骑摩托车的人都必须戴头盔，这是强制性的。

ex.en: English is a compulsory subject at this level.
ex.cn: 英语在这一级别是必修科目。

ex.en: compulsory education/schooling
ex.cn: 义务教育

ex.en: compulsory redundancies
ex.cn: 强制裁员

senses.def: an occasion when sb is officially ordered to sell land or property to the government or other authority
senses.chn: （政府等对土地或财产的）强制征购，强制性购买

ex.en: a compulsory purchase order
ex.cn: 强制征购令

senses.def: a guilty feeling about doing sth

ex.en: She felt no compunction about leaving her job.
ex.cn: 她对自己的辞职一点儿也不感到懊悔。

ex.en: He had lied to her without compunction.
ex.cn: 他向她撒了谎却毫无愧疚。

ex.en: She has no compunctions about rejecting the plan.
ex.cn: 她对拒绝那个计划丝毫也不后悔。

senses.def: an act or the process of calculating sth

ex.en: All the statistical computations were performed by the new software system.
ex.cn: 所有的统计计算均由新的软件系统完成。

ex.en: an error in the computation
ex.cn: 计算错误

senses.def: using or connected with computers
senses.chn: 使用计算机的；与计算机有关的

ex.en: computational methods
ex.cn: 用计算机做的方法

ex.en: a computational approach
ex.cn: 通过计算机进行

senses.def: the study of language and speech using computers
senses.chn: 计算语言学（用计算机进行语言分析）

senses.def: to calculate sth

ex.en: The losses were computed at £5 million.
ex.cn: 损失估算为 500 万英镑。

senses.def: an electronic machine that can store, organize and find information, do calculations and control other machines

ex.en: a personal computer
ex.cn: 个人电脑

ex.en: Our sales information is processed by computer.
ex.cn: 我们的销售信息是用计算机处理的。

ex.en: a computer program
ex.cn: 计算机程序

ex.en: computer software/hardware/graphics
ex.cn: 计算机软件／硬件／制图

ex.en: a computer error
ex.cn: 计算机错误

ex.en: computer-aided design
ex.cn: 计算机辅助设计

senses.def: a game played on a computer
to provide a computer or computers to do the work of sth
senses.chn: 用计算机做；使计算机化；使电脑化

ex.en: The factory has been fully computerized.
ex.cn: 这家工厂已完全计算机化了。

senses.def: to store information on a computer
senses.chn: 用计算机存储，用电脑存储（信息）

ex.en: computerized databases
ex.cn: 计算机化数据库

ex.en: The firm has computerized its records.
ex.cn: 那家公司已把记录存入计算机。

senses.def: able to use computers well
senses.chn: 能熟练使用计算机的；会用电脑的

senses.def: the study of computers and how they can be used

ex.en: a degree in computer science
ex.cn: 计算机科学学位

senses.def: the fact of using computers
senses.chn: 计算；计算机技术；信息处理技术

ex.en: to work in computing
ex.cn: 从事信息处理

ex.en: to study computing
ex.cn: 从事数据处理研究

ex.en: educational/network/scientific computing
ex.cn: 教育／网络／科学信息处理技术

ex.en: computing power/services/skills/systems
ex.cn: 数据处理能力／服务／技术／系统

senses.def: a person who is a member of the same communist or socialist political party as the person speaking
senses.chn: （共产党或社会主义政党的）同志

senses.def: a friend or other person that you work with, especially as soldiers during a war
senses.chn: 朋友；同事；（尤指战争期间的）战友

ex.en: They were old army comrades.
ex.cn: 他们是部队的老战友。

senses.def: a trick; an act of cheating sb

ex.en: The so-called bargain was just a big con!
ex.cn: 这种所谓的减价优惠只不过是个大骗局！

ex.en: a con trick
ex.cn: 骗人的花招

ex.en: a con game
ex.cn: 骗局

ex.en: He's a real con artist (= a person who regularly cheats others).
ex.cn: 他真是个行骗老手。

senses.def: the advantages and disadvantages of sth
senses.chn: 事物的利与弊；支持与反对

ex.en: We weighed up the pros and cons.
ex.cn: 我们权衡了利弊得失。

senses.def: to trick sb, especially in order to get money from them or persuade them to do sth for you
senses.chn: （尤指为钱财或使人为自己做某事而）欺骗，哄骗，诈骗

ex.en: I was conned into buying a useless car.
ex.cn: 我上当受骗买了辆不能用的汽车。

ex.en: They had been conned out of £100 000.
ex.cn: 他们被骗走了 10 万英镑。

ex.en: He conned his way into the job using false references.
ex.cn: 他用假的推荐信骗取了那份工作。

ex.en: She is accused of attempting to cheat the taxman.
ex.cn: 她被指控企图蒙骗税务员。

ex.en: He cheated his way into the job.
ex.cn: 他骗取了这份工作。

ex.en: You're not allowed to look at the answers— that's cheating.
ex.cn: 你们不许看答案，那是作弊。

senses.def: a mental process that makes you want to do sth or decide to do sth
in a lively way, with energy
a series of things or events that are linked together
senses.chn: 一系列相关联的事物（或事件）

ex.en: a strange concatenation of events
ex.cn: 一连串奇怪的事

senses.def: curving in

ex.en: a concave lens/mirror
ex.cn: 凹透镜；凹镜

senses.def: the quality of being concave (= curving in)
a shape or place that curves in
to hide sb/sth

ex.en: The paintings were concealed beneath a thick layer of plaster.
ex.cn: 那些画被隐藏在厚厚的灰泥层下面。

ex.en: Tim could barely conceal his disappointment.
ex.cn: 蒂姆几乎掩饰不住自己的失望。

ex.en: She sat down to conceal the fact that she was trembling.
ex.cn: 她坐下来以不让人看出她在发抖。

ex.en: For a long time his death was concealed from her.
ex.cn: 他的死瞒了很长时间都没告诉她。

ex.en: He hid the letter in a drawer.
ex.cn: 他把信藏在抽屉里。

ex.en: She managed to hide her disappointment.
ex.cn: 她设法掩藏了自己的失望。

senses.def: a skin-coloured cream or powder used to cover spots or marks on the skin or dark circles under the eyes
the act of hiding sth; the state of being hidden

ex.en: the concealment of crime
ex.cn: 对罪行的隐瞒

ex.en: Many animals rely on concealment for protection.
ex.cn: 许多动物靠藏匿自己来自保。

senses.def: to admit that sth is true, logical, etc.
senses.chn: 承认（某事属实、合乎逻辑等）

ex.en: 'Not bad,' she conceded grudgingly.
ex.cn: “不错。” 她勉强承认道。

ex.en: He was forced to concede (that) there might be difficulties.
ex.cn: 他被迫承认可能会有困难。

ex.en: I had to concede the logic of this.
ex.cn: 我得承认这件事情有它的逻辑。

ex.en: He reluctantly conceded the point to me.
ex.cn: 他不情愿地向我承认了这一点。

ex.en: He reluctantly conceded me the point.
ex.cn: 他不情愿地向我承认了这一点。

ex.en: It must be conceded that different judges have different approaches to these cases.
ex.cn: 必须承认不同的法官会采用不同的方法来判定这些案件。

senses.def: to give sth away, especially unwillingly; to allow sb to have sth

ex.en: The President was obliged to concede power to the army.
ex.cn: 总统被迫把权力让给军队。

ex.en: England conceded a goal immediately after half-time.
ex.cn: 英格兰队在下半场一开始就被攻入一球。

ex.en: Women were only conceded full voting rights in the 1950s.
ex.cn: 妇女在 20 世纪 50 年代才被容许完全享有选举权。

senses.def: to admit that you have lost a game, an election, etc.

ex.en: After losing this decisive battle, the general was forced to concede.
ex.cn: 输掉了这场决定性的战役后，那位将军不得不承认失败。

ex.en: Injury forced Hicks to concede defeat.
ex.cn: 受伤后，希克斯被迫认输。

senses.def: too much pride in yourself and what you do
an artistic effect or device, especially one that is very clever or tries to be very clever but does not succeed
senses.chn: 别出心裁但不实用的效果；巧妙但不实用的东西

ex.en: The ill-advised conceit of the guardian angel dooms the film from the start.
ex.cn: 对守护天使的蹩脚设计弄巧成拙，从一开始就注定这部电影要失败。

senses.def: a clever expression in writing or speech that involves a comparison between two things
senses.chn: 巧妙的言辞；别出心裁的比喻

ex.en: The idea of the wind singing is a romantic conceit.
ex.cn: 风儿在唱歌这一巧妙的比喻很有浪漫色彩。

senses.def: having too much pride in yourself and what you do

ex.en: a very conceited person
ex.cn: 极其自命不凡的人

ex.en: It's very conceited of you to assume that your work is always the best.
ex.cn: 你认为你的工作总是最好的，真是太自大了。

senses.def: that you can imagine or believe

ex.en: It is conceivable that I'll see her tomorrow.
ex.cn: 我可能明天会见到她。

ex.en: a beautiful city with buildings of every conceivable age and style
ex.cn: 拥有各个时代和各种风格建筑物的美丽城市

senses.def: to form an idea, a plan, etc. in your mind; to imagine sth
senses.chn: 想出（主意、计划等）；想象；构想；设想

ex.en: He conceived the idea of transforming the old power station into an arts centre.
ex.cn: 他想出了把旧发电站改造为艺术中心的主意。

ex.en: God is often conceived of as male.
ex.cn: 上帝常常被想象为男性。

ex.en: I cannot conceive (= I do not believe) (that) he would wish to harm us.
ex.cn: 我无法想象他会存心伤害我们。

ex.en: I cannot conceive what it must be like.
ex.cn: 我想象不出它会是什么样子。

senses.def: when a woman conceives or conceives a child, she becomes pregnant

ex.en: She is unable to conceive.
ex.cn: 她不能怀孕。

ex.en: Their first child was conceived on their wedding night.
ex.cn: 他们的第一个小孩是在新婚之夜怀上的。

senses.def: to give all your attention to sth and not think about anything else

ex.en: I can't concentrate with all that noise going on.
ex.cn: 吵闹声不绝于耳，我无法集中精神。

ex.en: Nothing concentrates the mind better than the knowledge that you could die tomorrow (= it makes you think very clearly).
ex.cn: 没有什么比知道自己明天就可能会死去更能让人定下心来去思考种种问题的了。

ex.en: I decided to concentrate all my efforts on finding somewhere to live.
ex.cn: 我决定全力以赴找个住的地方。

senses.def: to bring sth together in one place

ex.en: Power is largely concentrated in the hands of a small elite.
ex.cn: 权力主要集中在少数精英人物的手里。

ex.en: We need to concentrate resources on the most run-down areas.
ex.cn: 我们需要把资源集中用于最衰败的地区。

ex.en: Fighting was concentrated around the towns to the north.
ex.cn: 战斗集中在北方诸城镇的周围进行。

senses.def: to increase the strength of a substance by reducing its volume, for example by boiling it
to spend more time doing one particular thing than others

ex.en: In this lecture I shall concentrate on the early years of Charles's reign.
ex.cn: 这一节课我将着重讲查理王朝的早期统治时期。

senses.def: a substance that is made stronger because water or other substances have been removed

ex.en: mineral concentrates found at the bottom of rivers
ex.cn: 在河底发现的精矿

ex.en: jams made with fruit juice concentrate
ex.cn: 用浓缩果汁做的果酱

senses.def: showing determination to do sth
senses.chn: 决心要做的；全力以赴的

ex.en: He made a concentrated effort to finish the work on time.
ex.cn: 他全力以赴以按时完成这项工作。

senses.def: made stronger because water or other substances have been removed

ex.en: concentrated orange juice
ex.cn: 浓缩橙汁

ex.en: a concentrated solution of salt in water
ex.cn: 浓缩盐水溶液

senses.def: if sth exists or happens in a concentrated way, there is a lot of it in one place or at one time

ex.en: concentrated gunfire
ex.cn: 密集的炮火

senses.def: to spend more time doing one particular thing than others

ex.en: In this lecture I shall concentrate on the early years of Charles's reign.
ex.cn: 这一节课我将着重讲查理王朝的早期统治时期。

senses.def: the ability to direct all your effort and attention on one thing, without thinking of other things

ex.en: This book requires a great deal of concentration.
ex.cn: 这本书需要全神贯注才能读懂。

ex.en: Tiredness affects your powers of concentration.
ex.cn: 疲劳影响注意力的集中。

senses.def: the process of people directing effort and attention on a particular thing

ex.en: a need for greater concentration on environmental issues
ex.cn: 更加关注环境问题的必要性

senses.def: a lot of sth in one place

ex.en: a concentration of industry in the north of the country
ex.cn: 该国北部的工业集中地

senses.def: the amount of a substance in a liquid or in another substance

ex.en: glucose concentrations in the blood
ex.cn: 血液中的葡萄糖含量

senses.def: a type of prison, often consisting of a number of buildings inside a fence, where political prisoners, etc. are kept in extremely bad conditions

ex.en: a Nazi concentration camp
ex.cn: 纳粹集中营

senses.def: having the same centre

ex.en: concentric rings
ex.cn: 同心环

senses.def: an idea or a principle that is connected with sth abstract

ex.en: the concept of social class
ex.cn: 社会等级的概念

ex.en: concepts such as 'civilization' and 'government'
ex.cn: 诸如 “文明” 和 “政府” 的概念

ex.en: He can't grasp the basic concepts of mathematics.
ex.cn: 他无法掌握数学的基本概念。

ex.en: the concept that everyone should have equality of opportunity
ex.cn: 人人应当机会均等的观念

senses.def: a collection of pieces of popular music, all having the same theme and recorded on one album (2)
senses.chn: （流行音乐）概念专辑，主题唱片（所有曲目为同一主题）

senses.def: the process of forming an idea or a plan

ex.en: The plan was brilliant in its conception but failed because of lack of money.
ex.cn: 尽管这计划构想绝妙，但终因资金不足而告流产。

senses.def: an understanding or a belief of what sth is or what sth should be
senses.chn: 理解（认为某事怎样或应该怎样）

ex.en: Marx's conception of social justice
ex.cn: 马克思对社会公平概念的理解

ex.en: He has no conception of how difficult life is if you're unemployed.
ex.cn: 他不懂得失业后生活会是怎样的艰难。

senses.def: the process of an egg being fertilized inside a woman's body so that she becomes pregnant

ex.en: the moment of conception
ex.cn: 受孕的一刻

senses.def: related to or based on ideas

ex.en: a conceptual framework within which children's needs are assessed
ex.cn: 对儿童需求进行评估的概念框架

ex.en: a conceptual model
ex.cn: 概念模式

senses.def: art in which the idea which the work of art represents is considered to be the most important thing about it
senses.chn: 概念艺术，观念艺术（将艺术品的思想作为精髓）

senses.def: the theory that general ideas such as 'beauty' and 'red' exist only as ideas in the mind
senses.chn: 概念论（认为 “美”、“红” 等笼统概念只存在于头脑中）

senses.def: to form an idea of sth in your mind
senses.chn: 构思；使形成观念；将…概念化（为…）

senses.def: to affect sb/sth; to involve sb/sth

ex.en: Don't interfere in what doesn't concern you.
ex.cn: 不要管与自己无关的事。

ex.en: The loss was a tragedy for all concerned (= all those affected by it).
ex.cn: 这损失对有关各方来说都是极大的不幸。

ex.en: Where our children's education is concerned, no compromise is acceptable.
ex.cn: 在事关我们的孩子的教育问题上，那是毫无妥协余地的。

ex.en: The individuals concerned have some explaining to do.
ex.cn: 涉及的每个人都要作出解释。

ex.en: To whom it may concern … (= used for example, at the beginning of a public notice or of a job reference about sb's character and ability)
ex.cn: 敬启者…（如用于公告或求职推荐信的开头）

ex.en: Everyone who was directly concerned in (= had some responsibility for) the incident has now resigned.
ex.cn: 所有与该事件有直接牵连的人现在均已辞职。

senses.def: to be about sth

ex.en: The story concerns the prince's efforts to rescue Pamina.
ex.cn: 这故事讲的是王子奋力解救帕米娜。

ex.en: The book is primarily concerned with Soviet-American relations during the Cold War.
ex.cn: 这部书主要讲的是冷战时期的苏美关系。

ex.en: This chapter concerns itself with the historical background.
ex.cn: 本章旨在讲述历史背景。

ex.en: One major difference between these computers concerns the way in which they store information.
ex.cn: 这些计算机彼此之间的一个主要差异涉及其存储信息的方式。

senses.def: to worry sb

ex.en: What concerns me is our lack of preparation for the change.
ex.cn: 让我担心的是我们对事态的变化缺乏准备。

ex.en: It concerns me that you no longer seem to care.
ex.cn: 你似乎不再在乎，这令我担忧。

senses.def: to take an interest in sth

ex.en: He didn't concern himself with the details.
ex.cn: 他对细节不感兴趣。

senses.def: to think it is important to do sth

ex.en: She was concerned to write about situations that everybody could identify with.
ex.cn: 她认为应该写大家都能产生共鸣的情境。

senses.def: used to give facts or an opinion about a particular aspect of sth
a feeling of worry, especially one that is shared by many people
senses.chn: （尤指许多人共同的）担心，忧虑

ex.en: There is growing concern about violence on television.
ex.cn: 人们对电视上充斥暴力内容的忧虑日益加重。

ex.en: In the meeting, voters raised concerns about health care.
ex.cn: 选民在会上提出了对卫生保健状况的担忧。

ex.en: She hasn't been seen for four days and there is concern for her safety.
ex.cn: 她已四天不见踪影，大家对她的安全很担心。

ex.en: The report expressed concern over continuing high unemployment.
ex.cn: 报告表达了对失业率居高不下的忧虑。

ex.en: There is widespread concern that new houses will be built on protected land.
ex.cn: 人们普遍对在保护区建新的房屋感到忧虑。

ex.en: Stress at work is a matter of concern to staff and management.
ex.cn: 工作压力是一件让员工和管理人员都关切的事。

senses.def: a desire to protect and help sb/sth

ex.en: parents' concern for their children
ex.cn: 父母对子女的关爱

senses.def: something that is important to a person, an organization, etc.

ex.en: What are your main concerns as a writer?
ex.cn: 作为一名作家，你主要关注的是哪些问题？

ex.en: The government's primary concern is to reduce crime.
ex.cn: 政府的头等大事是减少犯罪。

senses.def: something that is your responsibility or that you have a right to know about
senses.chn: （某人）负责的事，有权知道的事

ex.en: This matter is their concern.
ex.cn: 这件事由他们负责。

ex.en: How much money I make is none of your concern.
ex.cn: 我赚多少钱没有必要告诉你。

senses.def: a company or business

ex.en: a major publishing concern
ex.cn: 一家大出版公司

senses.def: a business or an activity that is making a profit and is expected to continue to do well
senses.chn: 生意兴隆的业务；发展中的事业

ex.en: He sold the cafe as a going concern.
ex.cn: 他把经营得正红火的咖啡馆卖掉了。

senses.def: worried and feeling concern about sth

ex.en: Concerned parents held a meeting.
ex.cn: 忧心忡忡的家长们开了一次会。

ex.en: The President is deeply concerned about this issue.
ex.cn: 总统对这个问题深感担忧。

ex.en: He didn't seem in the least concerned for her safety.
ex.cn: 对她的安全他似乎一点都不担心。

ex.en: She was concerned that she might miss the turning and get lost.
ex.cn: 她担心自己会错过转弯的地方而迷路。

senses.def: interested in sth
senses.chn: 感兴趣的；关切的；关注的

ex.en: They were more concerned with how the other women had dressed than with what the speaker was saying.
ex.cn: 他们对其他女人的衣着打扮比对演讲者的讲话更加感兴趣。

senses.def: used to give your personal opinion on sth

ex.en: As far as I am concerned, you can do what you like.
ex.cn: 就我而言，你想干什么就可以干什么。

senses.def: about sth; involving sb/sth

ex.en: He asked several questions concerning the future of the company.
ex.cn: 他问了几个有关公司前途的问题。

ex.en: All cases concerning children are dealt with in a special children's court.
ex.cn: 所有涉及儿童的案件均由儿童特别法庭审理。

senses.def: a public performance of music

ex.en: a concert of music by Bach
ex.cn: 巴赫作品音乐会

ex.en: a classical/rock/pop concert
ex.cn: 古典／摇滚／流行音乐会

ex.en: They're in concert at Wembley Arena.
ex.cn: 他们在温布利体育馆举行音乐会。

ex.en: a concert hall/pianist
ex.cn: 音乐厅；在音乐会上演奏的钢琴家

senses.def: working together with sb/sth
related to a piece of music which contains an important part for a solo singer or player and which is similar to a concerto in character
a large group of people who play wind instruments together, and who perform in a concert hall
done in a planned and determined way, especially by more than one person, government, country, etc.
senses.chn: 努力的；共同筹划决定的；同心协力的

ex.en: a concerted approach/attack/campaign
ex.cn: 商定的方法；联合攻击；协同运动

ex.en: She has begun to make a concerted effort to find a job.
ex.cn: 她开始尽全力寻找工作。

senses.def: a person who regularly goes to concerts, especially of classical music
senses.chn: 常去听音乐会的人（尤指古典音乐会）

senses.def: a piano of the largest size, used especially for concerts
senses.chn: 大型三角钢琴；音乐会大钢琴

senses.def: a musical instrument like a small accordion, that you hold in both hands. You press the ends together and pull them apart to produce sounds.
to fold up like a concertina
senses.chn: （像六角手风琴一样）折起，折叠

ex.en: The truck crashed into the tree and concertinaed.
ex.cn: 货车撞在树上撞扁了。

senses.def: the most important violin player in an orchestra
a piece of music for one or more solo instruments playing with an orchestra

ex.en: a piano concerto
ex.cn: 钢琴协奏曲

ex.en: a concerto for flute and harp
ex.cn: 长笛与竖琴协奏曲

senses.def: something that you allow or do, or allow sb to have, in order to end an argument or to make a situation less difficult

ex.en: The firm will be forced to make concessions if it wants to avoid a strike.
ex.cn: 要想避免罢工，公司将不得不作出一些让步。

ex.en: to win a concession from sb
ex.cn: 取得某人的让步

ex.en: a major/an important concession
ex.cn: 重大的让步

ex.en: She made no concession to his age; she expected him to work as hard as she did.
ex.cn: 她丝毫也不体谅他的年龄，要求他干得像她一样卖力。

senses.def: the act of giving sth or allowing sth; the act of conceding

ex.en: the concession of university status to some colleges
ex.cn: 对某些学院升为大学的许可

ex.en: McCain's concession speech (= when he admitted that he had lost the election)
ex.cn: 麦凯恩承认竞选失败的讲话

senses.def: a reduction in an amount of money that has to be paid; a ticket that is sold at a reduced price to a particular group of people
senses.chn: 减价；（对某类人的）减价票

ex.en: tax concessions
ex.cn: 税收减免

ex.en: Tickets are £3; there is a £1 concession for students.
ex.cn: 票价为 3 英镑，学生票减免 1 英镑。

ex.en: Adults £2.50, concessions £2, family £5.
ex.cn: 成人、优惠、家庭票价分别为 2.50 英镑、2 英镑、5 英镑。

senses.def: a right or an advantage that is given to a group of people, an organization, etc., especially by a government or an employer
senses.chn: （尤指由政府或雇主给予的）特许权，优惠

ex.en: The Bolivian government has granted logging concessions covering 22 million hectares.
ex.cn: 玻利维亚政府批准了在 2 200 万公顷土地上的伐木特许权。

senses.def: the right to sell sth in a particular place; the place where you sell it, sometimes an area which is part of a larger building or store
senses.chn: （在某地的）特许经营权；（有时为大型建筑物或商场中的）销售场地，摊位

ex.en: the burger concessions at the stadium
ex.cn: 体育场内的汉堡包小吃摊

senses.def: a person or a business that has been given a concession to sell sth
senses.chn: （销售）特许权获得者；特许经销商

senses.def: costing less money for people in particular situations; given as a concession (3)
senses.chn: （在某种情况下）花费少的；优惠的；减价的

ex.en: concessionary rates/fares/travel
ex.cn: 优惠费率／票价／旅行

senses.def: used at the beginning of a clause to say that the action of the main clause is in fact true or possible, despite the situation. 'Despite' and 'although' are concessive words.
the shell of a sea creature which is also called a conch
a conscientious objector
senses.chn: 出于道义原因而拒服兵役者

senses.def: a person, especially in France, who takes care of a building containing flats/apartments and checks people entering and leaving the building
senses.chn: （尤指法国公寓等处的）看门人，司阍

senses.def: a person in a hotel whose job is to help guests by giving them information, arranging theatre tickets, etc.
senses.chn: （旅馆中负责提供信息、订票等的）服务台职员

senses.def: to make sb less angry or more friendly, especially by being kind and pleasant or by giving them sth
senses.chn: （尤指通过和蔼友善或送给某物来）平息…的怒火，抚慰，安抚

senses.def: a person or an organization that tries to make angry people calm so that they can discuss or solve their problems successfully
senses.chn: 调解者；抚慰者；调解机构

senses.def: having the intention or effect of making angry people calm
senses.chn: 调解的；抚慰的；意在和解的；和解的

ex.en: a conciliatory approach/attitude/gesture/move
ex.cn: 调解的方法；和解的态度／姿态／行动

senses.def: giving only the information that is necessary and important, using few words

ex.en: a concise summary
ex.cn: 简明扼要的总结

ex.en: clear concise instructions
ex.cn: 言简意赅的说明

senses.def: shorter than the original book, on which it was based

ex.en: a concise dictionary
ex.cn: 简明词典

senses.def: a meeting to discuss sth in private; the people at this meeting
senses.chn: 秘密会议；秘密会议与会者

senses.def: to decide or believe sth as a result of what you have heard or seen

ex.en: What do you conclude from that?
ex.cn: 你从中得出了什么结论？

ex.en: The report concluded (that) the cheapest option was to close the laboratory.
ex.cn: 这份报告认为最省钱的做法是关闭实验室。

ex.en: He concluded from their remarks that they were not in favour of the plan.
ex.cn: 他从他们的话语中推断出他们不赞同此项计划。

ex.en: It was concluded that the level of change necessary would be low.
ex.cn: 结论是需要作出的变更程度很低。

ex.en: 'So it should be safe to continue,' he concluded.
ex.cn: “那么继续下去应该是安全的。” 他推断说。

ex.en: In conclusion, the study has provided useful insights into the issues relating to people's perception of crime.
ex.cn: 综上所述，本研究为人们对犯罪活动的认识问题提供了有益的见解。

senses.def: to come to an end; to bring sth to an end

ex.en: Let me make just a few concluding remarks.
ex.cn: 我来讲几句话作为结束语。

ex.en: The programme concluded with Stravinsky's 'Rite of Spring'.
ex.cn: 演出节目以斯特拉文斯基的《春之祭》结束。

ex.en: He concluded by wishing everyone a safe trip home.
ex.cn: 他讲话结束时祝愿大家回家一路平安。

ex.en: The commission concluded its investigation last month.
ex.cn: 委员会在上个月终止了调查。

ex.en: 'Anyway, she should be back soon,' he concluded.
ex.cn: “反正她快回来了。” 他最后说道。

senses.def: to arrange and settle an agreement with sb formally and finally

ex.en: They concluded a treaty with Turkey.
ex.cn: 他们同土耳其缔结了一项条约。

ex.en: A trade agreement was concluded between the two countries.
ex.cn: 两国之间签署了贸易协定。

senses.def: something that you decide when you have thought about all the information connected with the situation

ex.en: I've come to the conclusion that he's not the right person for the job.
ex.cn: 我断定他不适合做这项工作。

ex.en: It took the jury some time to reach the conclusion that she was guilty.
ex.cn: 陪审团花了很长时间才得出结论认为她有罪。

ex.en: New evidence might lead to the conclusion that we are wrong.
ex.cn: 根据新的证据可能会推断出我们是错的。

ex.en: We can safely draw some conclusions from our discussion.
ex.cn: 从讨论中我们可以有把握地得出一些结论。

senses.def: the end of sth such as a speech or a piece of writing

ex.en: The conclusion of the book was disappointing.
ex.cn: 这部书的结尾令人失望。

ex.en: In conclusion (= finally), I would like to thank…
ex.cn: 最后，我想感谢…

ex.en: If we took this argument to its logical conclusion …
ex.cn: 假如我们把这个论点归结到合乎其逻辑的结论…

ex.en: In conclusion, the study has provided useful insights into the issues relating to people's perception of crime.
ex.cn: 综上所述，本研究为人们对犯罪活动的认识问题提供了有益的见解。

ex.en: Based on this study, it can be concluded that the introduction of new street lighting did not reduce reported crime.
ex.cn: 基于这项研究可以得出这样的结论：增加街道照明设备并没有使犯罪案件报案数量减少。

ex.en: To sum up, no evidence can be found to support the view that improved street lighting reduces reported crime.
ex.cn: 总而言之，没有证据表明街道照明的改进能使犯罪案件报案数量减少。

senses.def: the formal and final arrangement of sth official

ex.en: the successful conclusion of a trade treaty
ex.cn: 贸易条约的成功签署

ex.en: I'm afraid time is running out/we're running out of time, so we'll have to make this the final question.
ex.cn: 恐怕时间不多了，所以这将是我们最后一个问题了。

ex.en: We've only got a couple of minutes left, so can we summarize what we've agreed?
ex.cn: 我们只剩下几分钟了，所以概括一下已经达成一致的意见好吗？

ex.en: I'd like to close the session with a few final remarks…
ex.cn: 我想最后说几句来结束这次会议…

ex.en: We'll have to leave it there, but thank you all very much for your input.
ex.cn: 我们就到这儿吧，非常感谢大家的参与。

ex.en: Well, that's all we have time for today, but we'll meet again on Tuesday.
ex.cn: 好了，我们今天没有时间了，但星期二我们将再次开会。

senses.def: to make a decision about sb/sth too quickly, before you know or have thought about all the facts

ex.en: There I go again—jumping to conclusions.
ex.cn: 我又犯老毛病了——匆忙草率地下结论。

senses.def: if you say that sth is a foregone conclusion, you mean that it is a result that is certain to happen
proving sth, and allowing no doubt or confusion
senses.chn: 结论性的；不容置疑的；确凿的

ex.en: conclusive evidence/proof/results
ex.cn: 确凿的证据；不容置疑的结果

senses.def: to make sth, especially food or drink, by mixing different things
senses.chn: 调制，调合，配制（尤指食物或饮料）

ex.en: The soup was concocted from up to a dozen different kinds of fish.
ex.cn: 这种汤是用多达十几种不同的鱼熬制而成的。

senses.def: to invent a story, an excuse, etc.
senses.chn: 虚构，杜撰，编造（故事、借口等）

ex.en: She concocted some elaborate story to explain her absence.
ex.cn: 她精心编造了解释她缺席的一些谎言。

senses.def: a strange or unusual mixture of things, especially drinks or medicines
senses.chn: （古怪或少见的）混合物，调合物，调配品（尤指饮料或药物）

ex.en: a concoction of cream and rum
ex.cn: 奶油和朗姆酒调制的怪味饮料

senses.def: happening at the same time as sth else, especially because one thing is related to or causes the other
senses.chn: （尤指相关联的或有因果关系的事）同时发生的，伴随的，相伴的

senses.def: a thing that happens at the same time as sth else
senses.chn: 同时发生的事；伴随（或相伴）的事物

senses.def: peace and agreement

ex.en: living in concord with neighbouring states
ex.cn: 与邻国和睦相处

senses.def: the fact of having the same number, gender or person
an alphabetical list of the words used in a book, etc. showing where and how often they are used
senses.chn: （书籍等中按字母顺序排列的）词语索引

ex.en: a Bible concordance
ex.cn: 《圣经》用语索引

senses.def: a list produced by a computer that shows all the examples of an individual word in a book, etc.
the state of being similar to sth or consistent with it

ex.en: There is reasonable concordance between the two sets of results.
ex.cn: 两组结果之间有着合理的一致。

senses.def: an agreement, especially between the Roman Catholic Church and the state
senses.chn: （尤指罗马教廷与各国政府订立的）政教协定，政教条约

senses.def: a large, open part of a public building, especially an airport or a train station
senses.chn: （尤指机场或火车站的）大厅，广场

ex.en: the station concourse
ex.cn: 车站大厅

senses.def: made of concrete

ex.en: a concrete floor
ex.cn: 混凝土地面

senses.def: based on facts, not on ideas or guesses
senses.chn: 确实的，具体的（而非想象或猜测的）

ex.en: concrete evidence/proposals/proof
ex.cn: 确凿的证据；具体的建议；确实的证明

ex.en: 'It's only a suspicion,' she said, 'nothing concrete.'
ex.cn: “那只是怀疑，” 她说，“没有任何确实的依据。”

ex.en: It is easier to think in concrete terms rather than in the abstract.
ex.cn: 结合具体的事物来思考要比抽象思考容易些。

senses.def: a concrete object is one that you can see and feel
building material that is made by mixing together cement, sand, small stones and water

ex.en: a slab of concrete
ex.cn: 混凝土板

senses.def: to cover sth with concrete

ex.en: The garden had been concreted over.
ex.cn: 花园里铺设了混凝土。

senses.def: a way of describing a city or an area that is unpleasant because it has many large modern buildings and no trees or parks
senses.chn: 混凝土丛林（指高楼林立、无树木无公园因而单调沉闷的现代化城市或地区）

senses.def: poetry in which the meaning or effect is communicated partly by using patterns of words or letters that are visible on the page
senses.chn: 实体诗歌（部分借助于字词或字母组合的视象方法表达）

senses.def: (especially in some societies in the past) a woman who lives with a man, often in addition to his wife or wives, but who is less important than they are
senses.chn: （尤指旧时某些社会里的）妾，姨太太，小老婆

senses.def: strong sexual desire
to agree

ex.en: Historians have concurred with each other in this view.
ex.cn: 历史学家在这个观点上已取得一致意见。

ex.en: The coroner concurred with this assessment.
ex.cn: 验尸官同意这个鉴定。

senses.def: agreement

ex.en: The doctor may seek the concurrence of a relative before carrying out the procedure.
ex.cn: 医生可能会征得亲属的同意后再施行此项手术。

senses.def: an example of two or more things happening at the same time

ex.en: an unfortunate concurrence of events
ex.cn: 几件事情不幸同时发生

senses.def: existing or happening at the same time

ex.en: He was imprisoned for two concurrent terms of 30 months and 18 months.
ex.cn: 他被判处 30 个月和 18 个月的监禁，合并执行。

senses.def: to hit sb on the head, making them become unconscious or confused for a short time
a temporary loss of consciousness caused by a blow to the head; the effects of a severe blow to the head such as confusion and temporary loss of physical and mental abilities

ex.en: He was taken to hospital with concussion.
ex.cn: 他因脑震荡被送进医院。

ex.en: He was taken to the hospital with a concussion.
ex.cn: 他因脑震荡被送进医院。

senses.def: to express very strong disapproval of sb/sth, usually for moral reasons
senses.chn: （通常因道义上的原因而）谴责，指责

ex.en: The government issued a statement condemning the killings.
ex.cn: 政府发表声明谴责这些凶杀事件。

ex.en: The editor of the newspaper was condemned as lacking integrity.
ex.cn: 这家报纸的主编被指责为缺乏操守。

senses.def: to say what sb's punishment will be
senses.chn: 宣判；判处（某人某种刑罚）

ex.en: He was condemned to death for murder and later hanged.
ex.cn: 他因谋杀罪被判处死刑后被绞死了。

ex.en: She was condemned to hang for killing her husband.
ex.cn: 她因杀害亲夫被处以绞刑。

senses.def: to force sb to accept a difficult or unpleasant situation
senses.chn: 迫使…接受困境（或不愉快的状况）

ex.en: He was condemned to a life of hardship.
ex.cn: 他不得不过苦日子。

ex.en: They were condemned to spend every holiday on a rainy campsite.
ex.cn: 他们得在阴雨连绵的野营地度过每一个假日，徒叹奈何。

senses.def: to say officially that sth is not safe enough to be used

ex.en: a condemned building
ex.cn: 一座已宣告不能居住的危楼

ex.en: The meat was condemned as unfit to eat.
ex.cn: 这种肉被宣告不宜食用。

senses.def: to show or suggest that sb is guilty of sth

ex.en: She is condemned out of her own mouth (= her own words show that she is guilty).
ex.cn: 她自己说的话显示她有罪责。

senses.def: an expression of very strong disapproval

ex.en: There was widespread condemnation of the invasion.
ex.cn: 那次侵略遭到了人们普遍的谴责。

senses.def: a prison cell where a person who is going to be punished by death is kept
drops of water that form on a cold surface when warm water vapour becomes cool
the process of a gas changing to a liquid
the process of making a book, etc. shorter by taking out anything that is not necessary
to change from a gas into a liquid; to make a gas change into a liquid

ex.en: Steam condenses into water when it cools.
ex.cn: 蒸汽冷却时凝结为水。

ex.en: The steam was condensed rapidly by injecting cold water into the cylinder.
ex.cn: 由于汽缸中注入了冷水，蒸汽迅速凝结了。

senses.def: if a liquid condenses or you condense it, it becomes thicker and stronger because it has lost some of its water

ex.en: Condense the soup by boiling it for several minutes.
ex.cn: 煮几分钟把汤熬浓。

senses.def: to put sth such as a piece of writing into fewer words; to put a lot of information into a small space

ex.en: The article was condensed into just two pages.
ex.cn: 这篇文章被简缩成仅两页。

ex.en: The author has condensed a great deal of material into just 100 pages.
ex.cn: 作者在短短 100 页中浓缩了大量信息。

senses.def: a type of thick sweet milk that is sold in cans
a device that cools gas in order to change it into a liquid
a device that receives or stores electricity, especially in a car engine
senses.chn: （尤指汽车发动机内的）电容器

senses.def: to do sth that you think it is below your social or professional position to do

ex.en: We had to wait almost an hour before he condescended to see us.
ex.cn: 我们等了几乎一小时他才屈尊大驾来见我们。

senses.def: to behave towards sb as though you are more important and more intelligent than they are

ex.en: When giving a talk, be careful not to condescend to your audience.
ex.cn: 发表讲话时，注意别对听众表现出高人一等的样子。

senses.def: behaving as though you are more important and more intelligent than other people
senses.chn: 表现出优越感的；居高临下的

ex.en: He has a condescending attitude towards women.
ex.cn: 他对女性总是居高临下。

senses.def: appropriate to the crime
a substance such as salt or pepper that is used to give flavour to food
a sauce, etc. that is used to give flavour to food, or that is eaten with food
the state that sth is in

ex.en: to be in bad/good/excellent condition
ex.cn: 处于糟糕的／良好的／极佳的状态

ex.en: a used car in perfect condition
ex.cn: 车况完好的旧车

ex.en: the present state of medical knowledge
ex.cn: 目前医学知识的状况

ex.en: We're worried about his mental state.
ex.cn: 我们担心他的精神状况。

ex.en: What a state this room is in(= very bad).
ex.cn: 这房间真糟糕。

ex.en: The car is in excellent condition.
ex.cn: 这辆汽车的车况好极了。

senses.def: the state of sb's health or how fit they are

ex.en: He is overweight and out of condition (= not physically fit).
ex.cn: 他体重超重，健康状况不佳。

ex.en: You are in no condition (= too ill/sick, etc.) to go anywhere.
ex.cn: 你的身体太差，哪儿都不宜去。

ex.en: The motorcyclist was in a critical condition in hospital last night.
ex.cn: 那位摩托车手昨晚在医院生命垂危。

senses.def: an illness or a medical problem that you have for a long time because it is not possible to cure it
senses.chn: （因不可能治愈而长期患有的）疾病

ex.en: a medical condition
ex.cn: 疾病

ex.en: He suffers from a serious heart condition.
ex.cn: 他患有严重的心脏病。

ex.en: He suffers from a rare blood disease.
ex.cn: 他患有一种罕见的血液病。

ex.en: She died after a long illness.
ex.cn: 她久病不愈而亡。

ex.en: a rare disorder of the liver
ex.cn: 一种罕见的肝病

ex.en: a throat infection
ex.cn: 喉部感染

senses.def: the circumstances or situation in which people live, work or do things
senses.chn: （居住、工作或做事情的）环境，境况，条件

ex.en: living/housing/working conditions
ex.cn: 生活／住房／工作条件

ex.en: changing economic conditions
ex.cn: 不断变化的经济状况

ex.en: neglected children living under the most appalling conditions
ex.cn: 生活在最恶劣环境下的无人关注的儿童

ex.en: a strike to improve pay and conditions
ex.cn: 要求提高工资和改善工作条件的罢工

ex.en: the present economic situation
ex.cn: 目前的经济形势

ex.en: The ship sank in mysterious circumstances.
ex.cn: 那艘船神秘地沉没了。

senses.def: the physical situation that affects how sth happens
senses.chn: （影响某事发生的）物质环境，状态，条件

ex.en: The plants grow best in cool, damp conditions.
ex.cn: 这种植物最适合在阴凉、潮湿的环境下生长。

ex.en: freezing/icy/humid, etc. conditions
ex.cn: 冰冻、结冰、潮湿等的气候条件

ex.en: Conditions are ideal (= the weather is very good) for sailing today.
ex.cn: 今天是乘帆船航海的理想天气。

ex.en: treacherous driving conditions
ex.cn: 危险的行车环境

senses.def: a rule or decision that you must agree to, sometimes forming part of a contract or an official agreement

ex.en: the terms and conditions of employment
ex.cn: 雇用的条款

ex.en: The offer is subject to certain conditions.
ex.cn: 此项优惠受制于某些条件。
