ex.en: They agreed to lend us the car on condition that (= only if) we returned it before the weekend.
ex.cn: 他们同意借车给我们，条件是周末以前归还。

ex.en: They will give us the money on one condition —that we pay it back within six months.
ex.cn: 他们给我们提供资金有一个条件，即我们在六个月以内偿还。

ex.en: They agreed under the condition that the matter be dealt with promptly.
ex.cn: 他们同意了，前提是要迅速处理这件事。

ex.en: Congress can impose strict conditions on the bank.
ex.cn: 国会可能会迫使这家银行接受苛刻的条件。

senses.def: a situation that must exist in order for sth else to happen

ex.en: a necessary condition for economic growth
ex.cn: 经济增长的必要条件

ex.en: A good training programme is one of the conditions for successful industry.
ex.cn: 良好的培训计划是企业成功的先决条件。

senses.def: the state of a particular group of people because of their situation in life, their problems, etc.

ex.en: He spoke angrily about the condition of the urban poor.
ex.cn: 他愤怒地谈论城市贫民的处境。

ex.en: Work is basic to the human condition (= the fact of being alive).
ex.cn: 劳动是人类生存的基本条件。

senses.def: not in any situation; never

ex.en: You must on no condition tell them what happened.
ex.cn: 你决不能告诉他们所发生的事。

senses.def: new or as good as new; in perfect condition
to train sb/sth to behave in a particular way or to become used to a particular situation

ex.en: the difference between inborn and conditioned reflexes (= reactions that are learned/not natural)
ex.cn: 先天反应与条件反射的差异

ex.en: Patients can become conditioned to particular forms of treatment.
ex.cn: 病人会习惯某些治疗方式。

ex.en: The rats had been conditioned to ring a bell when they wanted food.
ex.cn: 这些老鼠已经过训练，想吃食物时就会按铃。

senses.def: to have an important effect on sb/sth; to influence the way that sth happens
senses.chn: 对…具有重要影响；影响（某事发生的方式）

ex.en: Gender roles are often conditioned by cultural factors.
ex.cn: 文化因素常常对性别的角色有着重要的影响。

senses.def: to keep sth such as your hair or skin healthy
senses.chn: 保持（头发或皮肤等的）健康；养护

ex.en: a shampoo that cleans and conditions hair
ex.cn: 可清洁并养护头发的洗发剂

ex.en: a polish for conditioning leather
ex.cn: 皮革护理油

senses.def: depending on sth

ex.en: conditional approval/acceptance
ex.cn: 有条件的批准／接受

ex.en: Payment is conditional upon delivery of the goods (= if the goods are not delivered, the money will not be paid).
ex.cn: 货到方付款。

ex.en: He was found guilty and given a conditional discharge (= allowed to go free on particular conditions).
ex.cn: 他被判定有罪并被判处有条件的释放。

ex.en: a conditional offer (= that depends on particular conditions being met)
ex.cn: 有条件的要约

senses.def: expressing sth that must happen or be true if another thing is to happen or be true

ex.en: a conditional sentence/clause
ex.cn: 条件句／从句

senses.def: a sentence or clause that begins with if or unless and expresses a condition
senses.chn: 条件句，条件从句（由 if 或 unless 引导的）

senses.def: the form of a verb that expresses a conditional action, for example should in If I should die…
senses.chn: 动词的条件式（如 should 用在 If I should die...）

ex.en: the present/past/perfect conditional
ex.cn: 现在／过去／完成条件式

ex.en: the first/second/third conditional
ex.cn: 第一／第二／第三条件式

senses.def: a liquid that makes hair soft and shiny after washing

ex.en: shampoo and conditioner
ex.cn: 洗发剂与护发素

senses.def: a liquid, used after washing clothes, that makes them softer

ex.en: fabric conditioner
ex.cn: 织物柔顺剂

senses.def: the training or experience that an animal or a person has that makes them behave in a particular way in a particular situation

ex.en: Is personality the result of conditioning from parents and society, or are we born with it?
ex.cn: 个性是受父母和社会熏陶的结果，还是我们生而有之？

senses.def: sympathy that you feel for sb when a person in their family or that they know well has died; an expression of this sympathy

ex.en: to give/offer/express your condolences
ex.cn: 表示慰唁

ex.en: Our condolences go to his wife and family.
ex.cn: 向他的妻子和家人谨致吊慰之意。

ex.en: a letter of condolence
ex.cn: 吊唁信

senses.def: a thin rubber covering that a man wears over his penis during sex to stop a woman from becoming pregnant or to protect against disease
senses.chn: （男用）避孕套，保险套，安全套，阴茎套

senses.def: a thin rubber device that a woman wears inside her vagina during sex to prevent herself from becoming pregnant

an apartment building or group of houses in which each flat/apartment/house is owned by the person living in it but the shared areas are owned by everyone together; a flat/apartment/house in such a building or group of houses
senses.chn: 公寓（套房私有，其他地方属业主共有）；公寓的套房；公寓的单元

senses.def: to accept behaviour that is morally wrong or to treat it as if it were not serious

ex.en: Terrorism can never be condoned.
ex.cn: 决不能容忍恐怖主义。

senses.def: a large bird of the vulture family, that lives mainly in S America
senses.chn: 神鹰，大秃鹰（主要栖居在南美洲）

senses.def: making it easy, possible or likely for sth to happen
senses.chn: 使容易（或有可能）发生的

ex.en: Chairs in rows are not as conducive to discussion as chairs arranged in a circle.
ex.cn: 椅子成排摆放不如成圈摆放便于讨论。

senses.def: to organize and/or do a particular activity

ex.en: to conduct an experiment/an inquiry/a survey
ex.cn: 进行实验／询问／调查

ex.en: The negotiations have been conducted in a positive manner.
ex.cn: 已积极进行过谈判。

senses.def: to direct a group of people who are singing or playing music

ex.en: a concert by the London Philharmonic Orchestra, conducted by Marin Alsop
ex.cn: 由马林 · 阿尔索普指挥、伦敦爱乐乐团演出的音乐会

senses.def: to lead or guide sb through or around a place

ex.en: a conducted tour of Athens (= one with a guide, giving information about it)
ex.cn: 有导游陪同的雅典之行

ex.en: The guide conducted us around the ruins of the ancient city.
ex.cn: 导游带领我们游览了古城遗迹。

senses.def: to behave in a particular way

ex.en: He conducted himself far better than expected.
ex.cn: 他表现得比预料的要好得多。

senses.def: to allow heat or electricity to pass along or through it

ex.en: Copper conducts electricity well.
ex.cn: 铜的导电性能好。

senses.def: a person's behaviour in a particular place or in a particular situation
senses.chn: （人在某地或某种情况下的）行为，举止

ex.en: The sport has a strict code of conduct.
ex.cn: 这种体育运动有严格的行为规范。

senses.def: the way in which a business or an activity is organized and managed
senses.chn: 经营方式；管理方法；实施办法

ex.en: There was growing criticism of the government's conduct of the war.
ex.cn: 政府对战争的指挥方式受到越来越多的指责。

senses.def: the degree to which an object allows electricity or heat to pass through it
the process by which heat or electricity passes through a material
able to conduct electricity, heat, etc.
senses.chn: 导电（或热等）的；能传导（电、热等）的

senses.def: a treatment for people with cerebral palsy that was developed in Hungary and that involves special physical exercises and learning methods
senses.chn: 引导式教育（治疗脑瘫的方法，在匈牙利开发，包括特定的动作训练和学习方法）

senses.def: a person who stands in front of an orchestra, a group of singers etc., and directs their performance, especially sb who does this as a profession
senses.chn: （管弦乐队、合唱队等的）指挥；职业指挥

senses.def: a person who is in charge of a train and travels with it, but does not drive it
a person whose job is to collect money from passengers on a bus or train or check their tickets
senses.chn: （公共汽车）售票员；（火车）检票员

ex.en: a bus conductor
ex.cn: 公共汽车售票员

senses.def: a substance that allows electricity or heat to pass along it or through it
senses.chn: 导体（导电或导热等的物质）

ex.en: Wood is a poor conductor.
ex.cn: 木头是不良导体。

senses.def: a woman who collects money from passengers on a bus or checks their tickets
a pipe, channel or tube which liquid, gas or electrical wire can pass through
senses.chn: （液体、气体或电线的）管道，导管

senses.def: a person, an organization or a country that is used to pass things or information to other people or places
senses.chn: 中转人；中转机构；中转国

ex.en: The organization had acted as a conduit for money from the arms industry.
ex.cn: 那家机构充当了从军工业向他处中转资金的渠道。

senses.def: a solid or hollow object with a round flat base and sides that slope up to a point
a solid or hollow object that is shaped like a cone

ex.en: a paper cone full of popcorn
ex.cn: 装满爆玉米花的锥形纸筒

ex.en: the cone of a volcano
ex.cn: 火山锥

senses.def: a plastic object shaped like a cone and often red and white, or yellow, in colour, used on roads to show where vehicles are not allowed to go, for example while repairs are being done
senses.chn: 锥形交通标，锥形桶，路锥（常为红白色或红黄色的塑料锥形物，表示在维修道路等时禁止车辆通行）

senses.def: a piece of thin crisp biscuit shaped like a cone, which you can put ice cream in to eat it
the hard dry fruit of a pine or fir tree

ex.en: a pine cone
ex.cn: 松树球果

senses.def: to close a road or part of a road by putting a line of cones across it
senses.chn: 用锥形交通标关闭（道路或道路的一部分）

senses.def: an informal private discussion or conversation
a meeting or conference of the members of a profession or group

ex.en: the annual movie confab in Cannes
ex.cn: 在戛纳举行的电影年会

senses.def: a story that sb has invented in their mind; the act of inventing a story in your mind
a conversation; the activity of having a conversation
a cake or other sweet food that looks very attractive
a thing such as a building or piece of clothing, that is made in a skilful or complicated way
senses.chn: 精工制作的物品（如建筑物或衣物）

senses.def: a person or a business that makes or sells cakes and sweets/candy
senses.chn: （制作或销售糕饼和糖果的）甜食商，甜食业

senses.def: fine white powder made from sugar, that is mixed with water to make icing
sweets/candy, chocolate, etc.
a union of states, groups of people or political parties with the same aim
a person who helps sb, especially to do sth illegal or secret
a person who supported the Confederate States in the American Civil War
senses.chn: （美国内战期间）南部邦联的支持者

senses.def: belonging to a confederacy
connected with the Confederate States

ex.en: the Confederate flag
ex.cn: 南部邦联旗

senses.def: an organization consisting of countries, businesses, etc. that have joined together in order to help each other

ex.en: the Confederation of British Industry
ex.cn: 英国工业联合会

senses.def: (in Canada) the joining together of provinces and territories forming Canada, which began 1 July, 1867
senses.chn: 加拿大联邦（从 1867 年 7 月 1 日起由若干省和地区组成加拿大）

senses.def: to discuss sth with sb, in order to exchange opinions or get advice

ex.en: He wanted to confer with his colleagues before reaching a decision.
ex.cn: 他想与他的同事先商议一下再作出决定。

senses.def: to give sb an award, a university degree or a particular honour or right
senses.chn: 授予，颁发（奖项、学位、荣誉或权利）

ex.en: An honorary degree was conferred on him by Oxford University in 2009.
ex.cn: 牛津大学于 2009 年授予他荣誉学位。

senses.def: a large official meeting, usually lasting for a few days, at which people with the same work or interests come together to discuss their views
senses.chn: （通常持续几天的大型正式）会议，研讨会

ex.en: The hotel is used for exhibitions, conferences and social events.
ex.cn: 这家旅馆用于举行展览、大型会议和社交活动。

ex.en: a conference room/centre/hall
ex.cn: 会议室；会议中心；会议厅

ex.en: She is attending a three-day conference on AIDS education.
ex.cn: 她正在出席一个为期三天的有关艾滋病教育的会议。

ex.en: The conference will be held in Glasgow.
ex.cn: 会议将在格拉斯哥举行。

ex.en: delegates to the Labour Party's annual conference
ex.cn: 参加工党年会的代表

senses.def: a meeting at which people have formal discussions

ex.en: Ministers from all four countries involved will meet at the conference table this week.
ex.cn: 有关四国将各派部长于本周开会协商。

ex.en: He was in conference with his lawyers all day.
ex.cn: 他与他的律师们商讨了一整天。

senses.def: a group of sports teams that play against each other in a league

ex.en: Southeast Conference football champions
ex.cn: 东南部联盟的橄榄球联赛

senses.def: a telephone call in which three or more people take part
the activity of organizing or taking part in meetings, especially when people are in different places and use telephones, computers, or video to communicate
senses.chn: 召集（或参加）会议（尤指电话、网络或视频会议）

ex.en: video conferencing
ex.cn: 召开视频会议

senses.def: the action of giving sb an award, a university degree or a particular honour or right
senses.chn: （奖项、学位、荣誉或权利的）授予，颁发

senses.def: to admit, especially formally or to the police, that you have done sth wrong or illegal
senses.chn: 供认，坦白，承认（错误或罪行）

ex.en: After hours of questioning, the suspect confessed.
ex.cn: 经过数小时的审问后，嫌疑犯终于招供。

ex.en: She confessed to the murder.
ex.cn: 她供认犯了谋杀罪。

ex.en: He confessed that he had stolen the money.
ex.cn: 他承认他偷了那笔钱。

ex.en: We persuaded her to confess her crime.
ex.cn: 我们说服她坦白她的罪行。

senses.def: to admit sth that you feel ashamed or embarrassed about
senses.chn: 承认（自己感到羞愧或尴尬的事）

ex.en: She was reluctant to confess her ignorance.
ex.cn: 她不愿承认她的无知。

ex.en: I must confess to knowing nothing about computers.
ex.cn: 我得承认对电脑一窍不通。

ex.en: I confess (that) I know nothing about computers.
ex.cn: 我承认我对电脑一窍不通。

ex.en: 'I know nothing about them,' he confessed.
ex.cn: “我对他们一无所知。” 他承认道。

ex.en: I confess myself bewildered by their explanation.
ex.cn: 我承认他们的解释使我感到困惑。

ex.en: It was a stupid thing to do, I admit.
ex.cn: 我承认，那次干的是件蠢事。

senses.def: to tell God or a priest about the bad things you have done so that you can say that you are sorry and be forgiven
to hear sb confess their sins (= the bad things they have done)
senses.chn: 聆听（某人的）忏悔（或告罪、告解）

senses.def: a statement that a person makes, admitting that they are guilty of a crime; the act of making such a statement
senses.chn: 供词；供状；认罪；供认；坦白

ex.en: After hours of questioning by police, she made a full confession.
ex.cn: 经过警察数小时的审问，她供认了全部罪行。

senses.def: a statement admitting sth that you are ashamed or embarrassed about; the act of making such a statement
senses.chn: （对使自己羞愧或尴尬的事的）表白，承认

ex.en: I've a confession to make—I lied about my age.
ex.cn: 我有错要承认，我谎报了年龄。

senses.def: a private statement to a priest about the bad things that you have done

ex.en: to go to confession
ex.cn: 去告解

ex.en: to hear sb's confession
ex.cn: 听某人告解

senses.def: a statement of your religious beliefs, principles, etc.

ex.en: a confession of faith
ex.cn: 宗教信仰表白

senses.def: a private place in a church where a priest listens to people making confessions
senses.chn: （教堂内的）告解室，告解亭，忏悔室

senses.def: a Roman Catholic priest who listens to sb's confession (3)
small pieces of coloured paper that people often throw at weddings over people who have just been married, or (in the US) at other special events
senses.chn: （在婚礼或美国其他特殊活动中撒的）五彩纸屑

senses.def: a person that you trust and who you talk to about private or secret things

ex.en: a close/trusted confidant of the President
ex.cn: 总统的密友／亲信

senses.def: to tell sb secrets and personal information that you do not want other people to know

ex.en: She confided all her secrets to her best friend.
ex.cn: 她向她最要好的朋友倾吐了自己所有的秘密。

ex.en: He confided to me that he had applied for another job.
ex.cn: 他向我透露他已申请另一份工作。

ex.en: 'It was a lie,' he confided.
ex.cn: “这是谎言。” 他透露说。

senses.def: to tell sb secrets and personal information because you feel you can trust them
senses.chn: 向（认为可信赖的人）透露秘密（或隐私）

ex.en: It is important to have someone you can confide in.
ex.cn: 有一位心腹知己很重要。

senses.def: to tell sb secrets and personal information because you feel you can trust them
senses.chn: 向（认为可信赖的人）透露秘密（或隐私）

ex.en: It is important to have someone you can confide in.
ex.cn: 有一位心腹知己很重要。

senses.def: the feeling that you can trust, believe in and be sure about the abilities or good qualities of sb/sth

ex.en: The players all have confidence in their manager.
ex.cn: 队员都信赖他们的教练。

ex.en: A fall in unemployment will help to restore consumer confidence.
ex.cn: 失业人数的下降会有助于恢复消费者的信心。

ex.en: a lack of confidence in the government
ex.cn: 对政府缺乏信任

ex.en: The new contracts have undermined the confidence of employees.
ex.cn: 新的合同动摇了雇员们的信心。

ex.en: She has every confidence in her students' abilities.
ex.cn: 她完全相信她学生的能力。

senses.def: a belief in your own ability to do things and be successful

ex.en: He answered the questions with confidence.
ex.cn: 他自信地回答了那些问题。

ex.en: People often lose confidence when they are criticized.
ex.cn: 人受到批评时经常会失去信心。

ex.en: He gained confidence when he went to college.
ex.cn: 他上大学后增强了自信。

ex.en: She suffers from a lack of confidence.
ex.cn: 她深受缺乏自信心之苦。

ex.en: While girls lack confidence, boys often overestimate their abilities.
ex.cn: 女孩通常缺乏自信，而男孩则往往会高估自己的能力。

ex.en: I didn't have any confidence in myself at school.
ex.cn: 我在学校时对自己毫无信心。

senses.def: the feeling that you are certain about sth

ex.en: They could not say with confidence that he would be able to walk again after the accident.
ex.cn: 他们不能肯定他经过那场事故后还能行走。

ex.en: He expressed his confidence that they would win.
ex.cn: 他表示了自己的信心：他们必定取胜。

senses.def: a feeling of trust that sb will keep information private
senses.chn: （对某人会保守秘密的）信任，信赖

ex.en: Eva told me about their relationship in confidence.
ex.cn: 伊娃对我透露了他们俩的关系这个秘密。

ex.en: This is in the strictest confidence.
ex.cn: 这事切勿外传。

ex.en: It took a long time to gain her confidence (= make her feel she could trust me).
ex.cn: 我花了很长的时间才赢得她的信任。

senses.def: a secret that you tell sb

ex.en: The girls exchanged confidences.
ex.cn: 女孩子们相互吐露自己的心事。

ex.en: I could never forgive Mike for betraying a confidence.
ex.cn: 迈克泄露了秘密，我绝不会原谅他。

senses.def: to be trusted with sb's secrets
senses.chn: 受某人信任；是某人的心腹

ex.en: He is said to be very much in the President's confidence.
ex.cn: 据说他深受总统的信任。

senses.def: to tell sb secrets and personal information about yourself
senses.chn: 向某人吐露内心秘密（或隐私）

ex.en: She took me into her confidence and told me about the problems she was facing.
ex.cn: 她把我当成知己，把她面临的种种难题都向我和盘托出。

senses.def: a person who tricks others into giving him or her money, etc.
feeling sure about your own ability to do things and be successful

ex.en: She was in a relaxed, confident mood.
ex.cn: 她的心态从容而自信。

ex.en: The teacher wants the children to feel confident about asking questions when they don't understand.
ex.cn: 教师要孩子们遇到不懂的就大胆提问。

senses.def: feeling certain that sth will happen in the way that you want or expect
senses.chn: 肯定的；确信的；有把握的

ex.en: The team feels confident of winning.
ex.cn: 这个队觉得有把握取胜。

ex.en: I'm confident that you will get the job.
ex.cn: 我肯定你能得到那份工作。

ex.en: 'Is that John over there?' 'I'm not sure.'
ex.cn: “那边那个人是约翰吗？” “我说不准。”

ex.en: Are you sure about that?
ex.cn: 这事你肯定吗？

ex.en: England must win this game to be sure of qualifying.
ex.cn: 英格兰队必须拿下这场比赛才能确保获得资格。

ex.en: I'm quite sure (that) I left my bag here(= I have no doubt about it).
ex.cn: 我肯定是把包丢在这儿了。

senses.def: meant to be kept secret and not told to or shared with other people

ex.en: confidential information/documents
ex.cn: 机密情报／文件

ex.en: Your medical records are strictly confidential (= completely secret).
ex.cn: 你的病历是绝对保密的。

senses.def: showing that what you are saying is private or secret

ex.en: He spoke in a confidential tone, his voice low.
ex.cn: 他低声用隐秘的语气说话。

senses.def: trusted with private or secret information

ex.en: a confidential secretary
ex.cn: 机要秘书

senses.def: a situation in which you expect sb to keep information secret

ex.en: They signed a confidentiality agreement.
ex.cn: 他们签署了一份保守机密的协议。

ex.en: All letters will be treated with complete confidentiality.
ex.cn: 所有信件将按绝密处置。

senses.def: showing trust; showing that you want to tell sb a secret

ex.en: a confiding relationship
ex.cn: 可以推心置腹的关系

senses.def: an arrangement of the parts of sth or a group of things; the form or shape that this arrangement produces
senses.chn: 布局；结构；构造；格局；形状

senses.def: the equipment and programs that form a computer system and the way that these are set up to run
to arrange sth in a particular way, especially computer equipment; to make equipment or software work in the way that the user prefers
senses.chn: （按特定方式）安置；（尤指对计算机设备进行）配置；对（设备或软件进行）设定

senses.def: to keep sb/sth inside the limits of a particular activity, subject, area, etc.

ex.en: The work will not be confined to the Glasgow area.
ex.cn: 此项工作不会局限于格拉斯哥地区。

ex.en: I will confine myself to looking at the period from 1900 to 1916.
ex.cn: 我将把自己考察的范围限定在 1900 年至 1916 年这段时间以内。

senses.def: to keep a person or an animal in a small or closed space

ex.en: Keep the dog confined in a suitable travelling cage.
ex.cn: 把狗关进适于旅行的笼子里。

ex.en: Here the river is confined in a narrow channel.
ex.cn: 这条河在这里流入狭窄的河槽。

ex.en: The soldiers concerned were confined to barracks (= had to stay in the barracks, as a punishment).
ex.cn: 有关的士兵已受到禁闭在营房的处分。

senses.def: to have to stay in bed, in a wheelchair, etc.
senses.chn: 使离不开（或受困于床、轮椅等）

ex.en: She was confined to bed with the flu.
ex.cn: 她因患流感卧病在床。

ex.en: He was confined to a wheelchair after the accident.
ex.cn: 经过那场事故后他就离不开轮椅了。

senses.def: small and surrounded by walls or sides

ex.en: It is cruel to keep animals in confined spaces.
ex.cn: 把动物关在狭小的空间里是残忍的。

senses.def: the state of being forced to stay in a closed space, prison, etc., the act of putting sb there

ex.en: her confinement to a wheelchair
ex.cn: 半步离不开轮椅对她的束缚

ex.en: years of confinement as a political prisoner
ex.cn: 作为政治犯被监禁的岁月

senses.def: the time when a woman gives birth to a baby

ex.en: the expected date of confinement
ex.cn: 预产期

ex.en: a hospital/home confinement
ex.cn: 在医院／家中分娩

senses.def: limits or borders

ex.en: It is beyond the confines of human knowledge.
ex.cn: 这超出了人类的知识范围。

ex.en: the confines of family life
ex.cn: 家庭生活的范围

senses.def: to state or show that sth is definitely true or correct, especially by providing evidence
senses.chn: （尤指提供证据来）证实，证明，确认

ex.en: Rumours of job losses were later confirmed.
ex.cn: 裁员的传言后来得到了证实。

ex.en: His guilty expression confirmed my suspicions.
ex.cn: 他内疚的表情证实了我的猜疑。

ex.en: Please write to confirm your reservation (= say that it is definite).
ex.cn: 预订后请来函确认。

ex.en: Has everyone confirmed (that) they're coming?
ex.cn: 他们是不是每个人都确定了一定会来？

ex.en: Can you confirm what happened?
ex.cn: 你能证实一下发生了什么事吗？

ex.en: It has been confirmed that the meeting will take place next week.
ex.cn: 已经确定会议将于下个星期举行。

senses.def: to make sb feel or believe sth even more strongly

ex.en: The walk in the mountains confirmed his fear of heights.
ex.cn: 在山里步行使他更加确信自己有恐高症。

senses.def: to make a position, an agreement, etc. more definite or official; to establish sb/sth firmly
senses.chn: 批准（职位、协议等）；确认；认可

ex.en: After a six-month probationary period, her position was confirmed.
ex.cn: 经过六个月的试用期后，她获准正式担任该职。

ex.en: He was confirmed as captain for the rest of the season.
ex.cn: 他被正式任命在这个赛季剩下的时间内担任队长。

ex.en: I'm very happy to confirm you in your post.
ex.cn: 我很高兴确认你担任此职位。

senses.def: to make sb a full member of the Christian Church

ex.en: She was baptized when she was a month old and confirmed when she was thirteen.
ex.cn: 她出生一个月时受洗礼，十三岁时受坚信礼。

senses.def: a statement, letter, etc. that shows that sth is true, correct or definite

ex.en: I'm still waiting for confirmation of the test results.
ex.cn: 我仍在等待考试结果的通知书。

senses.def: a ceremony at which a person becomes a full member of the Christian Church
a Jewish ceremony similar to a bar mitzvah or bat mitzvah but usually for young people over the age of 16
senses.chn: 坚振礼（通常为 16 岁以上犹太年轻人举行的仪式）

senses.def: having a particular habit or way of life and not likely to change

ex.en: a confirmed bachelor (= a man who is not likely to get married, often used in newspapers to refer to a homosexual man)
ex.cn: 抱定独身主义的男子（报章常用以指同性恋者）

senses.def: to officially take sth away from sb, especially as a punishment

ex.en: Their land was confiscated after the war.
ex.cn: 他们的土地在战后被没收。

ex.en: The teacher threatened to confiscate their phones if they kept using them in class.
ex.cn: 老师警告说，如果他们上课时继续使用手机就予以没收。

senses.def: a very large fire that destroys a lot of land or buildings
to put two or more things together to make one new thing
a situation in which people, groups or countries are involved in a serious disagreement or argument

ex.en: a conflict between two cultures
ex.cn: 两种文化的冲突

ex.en: The violence was the result of political and ethnic conflicts.
ex.cn: 那次暴动是政治与种族冲突的结果。

ex.en: She found herself in conflict with her parents over her future career.
ex.cn: 她发现自己在将来择业的问题上与父母存在着分歧。

ex.en: John often comes into conflict with his boss.
ex.cn: 约翰经常和他的老板发生争执。

ex.en: The government has done nothing to resolve the conflict over nurses' pay.
ex.cn: 政府未采取任何措施来解决护士工资问题引发的冲突。

senses.def: a violent situation or period of fighting between two countries

ex.en: armed/military conflict
ex.cn: 武装／军事冲突

senses.def: a situation in which there are opposing ideas, opinions, feelings or wishes; a situation in which it is difficult to choose

ex.en: The story tells of a classic conflict between love and duty.
ex.cn: 这故事讲的是典型的爱情与责任之间的矛盾。

ex.en: Her diary was a record of her inner conflict.
ex.cn: 她的日记记录了她内心的矛盾。

ex.en: Many of these ideas appear to be in conflict with each other.
ex.cn: 这些观念中有许多看上去似乎相互矛盾。

senses.def: a situation in which sb has two jobs, aims, roles, etc. and cannot treat both of them equally and fairly at the same time

ex.en: There was a conflict of interest between his business dealings and his political activities.
ex.cn: 他的商务交往与政治活动之间出现利益冲突。

senses.def: if two ideas, beliefs, stories, etc. conflict, it is not possible for them to exist together or for them both to be true
senses.chn: （两种思想、信仰、说法等）冲突，抵触

ex.en: conflicting emotions/interests/loyalties
ex.cn: 相互矛盾的感情／利益／忠诚

ex.en: These results conflict with earlier findings.
ex.cn: 这些结果与早期的发现相矛盾。

ex.en: Reports conflicted on how much of the aid was reaching the famine victims.
ex.cn: 对于究竟有多少援助到了饥民手里，相关报告的说法彼此矛盾。

senses.def: a diamond that has not been shaped by cutting and that is sold illegally to provide money for an armed conflict
senses.chn: 冲突钻石，血钻（未经打磨，用于非法交易，为武装冲突提供资金）

ex.en: The organization is trying to combat trade in conflict diamonds in the war zone.
ex.cn: 该组织正全力打击交战区的血钻石交易。

senses.def: confused about what to do or choose because you have strong but opposing feelings
senses.chn: 因心理冲突而不知所措的

senses.def: the place where two rivers flow together and become one
senses.chn: （河流的）汇合处，汇流处，交汇处

senses.def: the fact of two or more things becoming one

ex.en: a confluence of social factors
ex.cn: 多种社会因素的汇集

senses.def: to behave and think in the same way as most other people in a group or society
senses.chn: 顺从，顺应（大多数人或社会）；随潮流

ex.en: There is considerable pressure on teenagers to conform.
ex.cn: 青少年被大力要求守规矩。

ex.en: He refused to conform to the local customs.
ex.cn: 他拒绝遵从当地的风俗习惯。

senses.def: to obey a rule, law, etc.
senses.chn: 遵守，遵从，服从（规则、法律等）

ex.en: The building does not conform with safety regulations.
ex.cn: 这座建筑物不符合安全条例。

senses.def: to agree with or match sth

ex.en: It did not conform to the usual stereotype of an industrial city.
ex.cn: 这和工业城市那种千篇一律的格局不一样。

senses.def: similar in form or nature to sth; in agreement with sth

ex.en: What happens in cases where common law is not conformable to the constitution?
ex.cn: 普通法与宪法相抵牾时该怎么办？

senses.def: the fact of following the rules or standards of sth

ex.en: You need to ensure conformance to strict quality guidelines.
ex.cn: 你得保证遵守严格的质量基准。

senses.def: the way in which sth is formed; the structure of sth, especially an animal
senses.chn: 构造；结构；形态；（尤指动物的）身体构造

senses.def: a person who behaves and thinks in the same way as most other people and who does not want to be different
senses.chn: 顺从者；随波逐流者；循规蹈矩的人

senses.def: behaviour or actions that follow the accepted rules of society
following the rules of sth; conforming to sth
senses.chn: 遵循（规则）；与…相符合（或一致）

ex.en: regulations that are in conformity with European law
ex.cn: 符合欧洲法律的条例

senses.def: to confuse and surprise sb

ex.en: The sudden rise in share prices has confounded economists.
ex.cn: 股价的突然上涨使经济学家大惑不解。

senses.def: to prove sb/sth wrong

ex.en: to confound expectations
ex.cn: 证明期望有误

ex.en: She confounded her critics and proved she could do the job.
ex.cn: 她驳倒了批评者的看法，证明自己能够胜任那项工作。

senses.def: to defeat an enemy
used to show that you are angry about sth/with sb
used when describing sth to show that you are annoyed
senses.chn: （表示某事令人厌烦）讨厌的，该死的

senses.def: a group of people who join together especially for a religious purpose or to help other people
senses.chn: （尤指宗教、慈善事业的）团体，协会

senses.def: to appear and need to be dealt with by sb

ex.en: the economic problems confronting the country
ex.cn: 这个国家所面临的经济问题

ex.en: The government found itself confronted by massive opposition.
ex.cn: 政府发现自己遭到了强烈的反对。

senses.def: to deal with a problem or difficult situation

ex.en: She knew that she had to confront her fears.
ex.cn: 她心里明白自己必须克服恐惧心理。

senses.def: to face sb so that they cannot avoid seeing and hearing you, especially in an unfriendly or dangerous situation

ex.en: This was the first time he had confronted an armed robber.
ex.cn: 这是他第一次面对一个武装劫匪。

senses.def: to make sb face or deal with an unpleasant or difficult person or situation
senses.chn: 使面对，使面临，使对付（令人不快或难处的人、场合）

ex.en: He confronted her with a choice between her career or their relationship.
ex.cn: 他要她在事业和他们两人关系之间作出抉择。

senses.def: to have sth in front of you that you have to deal with or react to

ex.en: Most people when confronted with a horse will pat it.
ex.cn: 大多数人遇见马时都会轻轻地拍拍它。

senses.def: a situation in which there is an angry disagreement between people or groups who have different opinions

ex.en: She wanted to avoid another confrontation with her father.
ex.cn: 她想避免和父亲再次发生冲突。

ex.en: confrontation between employers and unions
ex.cn: 资方与工会之间的对峙

senses.def: tending to deal with people in an aggressive way that is likely to cause arguments, rather than discussing things with them
based on or believing the teachings of the Chinese philosopher Confucius
senses.chn: 儒家的；儒学的；孔子学说的

senses.def: if two things are confusable, it is easy to confuse them

ex.en: 'Historic' and 'historical' are easily confusable.
ex.cn: historic 和 historical 容易搞混。

ex.en: The various types of owl are easily confusable with one another.
ex.cn: 各种猫头鹰之间很容易弄混。

senses.def: to make sb unable to think clearly or understand sth

ex.en: They confused me with conflicting accounts of what happened.
ex.cn: 他们对发生的事所作的陈述自相矛盾，使我迷惑不解。

senses.def: to think wrongly that sb/sth is sb/sth else

ex.en: People often confuse me and my twin sister.
ex.cn: 人们常常把我和我的孪生妹妹搞错。

ex.en: Be careful not to confuse quantity with quality.
ex.cn: 注意不要把数量与质量混淆了。

senses.def: to make a subject more difficult to understand

ex.en: His comments only served to confuse the issue further.
ex.cn: 他的评论只是把问题弄得更加复杂。

senses.def: unable to think clearly or to understand what is happening or what sb is saying

ex.en: People are confused about all the different labels on food these days.
ex.cn: 人们如今被那些五花八门的食物标签搞得稀里糊涂。

ex.en: He was depressed and in a confused state of mind.
ex.cn: 他意志消沉，脑子里乱成一团。

ex.en: I'm confused—say all that again.
ex.cn: 我被搞糊涂了，把那件事从头到尾再说一遍吧。

senses.def: not clear or easy to understand
senses.chn: 不清楚的；混乱的；难懂的

ex.en: The children gave a confused account of what had happened.
ex.cn: 孩子们把发生的事叙述得颠三倒四。

senses.def: difficult to understand; not clear

ex.en: The instructions on the box are very confusing.
ex.cn: 盒子上的使用说明令人费解。

ex.en: a very confusing experience
ex.cn: 让人莫名其妙的经历

senses.def: a state of not being certain about what is happening, what you should do, what sth means, etc.

ex.en: There is some confusion about what the correct procedure should be.
ex.cn: 对于应该采取什么正确步骤，还是有些不明确。

ex.en: a confusion as to what to do next
ex.cn: 不清楚下一步该怎么办

senses.def: the fact of making a mistake about who sb is or what sth is

ex.en: To avoid confusion, please write the children's names clearly on all their school clothes.
ex.cn: 为避免搞错，请在孩子所有的校服上写清楚他们各自的姓名。

ex.en: confusion between letters of the alphabet like 'o' or 'a'
ex.cn: 像 o 或 a 这类字母之间的易于混淆

senses.def: a feeling of embarrassment when you do not understand sth and are not sure what to do in a situation

ex.en: He looked at me in confusion and did not answer the question.
ex.cn: 他困窘地看着我，没有回答问题。

senses.def: a confused situation in which people do not know what action to take
senses.chn: （让人不知所措的）混乱局面，乱成一团

ex.en: Fighting had broken out and all was chaos and confusion.
ex.cn: 战斗爆发了，一切都陷入了混乱不堪的状态。

ex.en: Her unexpected arrival threw us into total confusion.
ex.cn: 她的突然到来使得我们不知所措，乱成一团。

senses.def: to prove a person or an argument to be wrong
a fast dance in which the dancers follow a leader in a long winding line, with each person holding on to the person in front; a piece of music for this dance
a tall narrow drum that you play with your hands
senses.chn: 康茄鼓（用手击打的狭长鼓）

senses.def: to become thick or solid

ex.en: congealed blood
ex.cn: 凝固了的血

ex.en: The cold remains of supper had congealed on the plate.
ex.cn: 晚餐剩下的冷饭菜已经凝结在盘子上了。

ex.en: The bitterness and tears had congealed into hatred.
ex.cn: 愤懑与眼泪凝结成了仇恨。

senses.def: pleasant to spend time with because their interests and character are similar to your own
senses.chn: 意气相投的；志趣相投的；合得来的

ex.en: a congenial colleague
ex.cn: 意气相投的同事

senses.def: pleasant because it suits your character

ex.en: a congenial working environment
ex.cn: 宜人的工作环境

senses.def: suitable for sth

ex.en: a situation that was congenial to the expression of nationalist opinions
ex.cn: 适于表达民族主义者意见的场合

senses.def: existing since or before birth

ex.en: congenital abnormalities
ex.cn: 先天畸形

senses.def: existing as part of a person's character and not likely to change

ex.en: a congenital inability to tell the truth
ex.cn: 生就不会说实话

senses.def: born with a particular illness

ex.en: a congenital liar (= one who will not change)
ex.cn: 生性好说谎的人

senses.def: a large eel (= a long thin fish) that lives in the sea
crowded; full of traffic
senses.chn: 拥挤的；挤满的；（交通）堵塞的

ex.en: congested city streets
ex.cn: 交通拥塞的城市街道

ex.en: Many of Europe's airports are heavily congested.
ex.cn: 欧洲许多机场都十分拥挤。

senses.def: blocked with blood or mucus
the state of being crowded and full of traffic

ex.en: traffic congestion and pollution
ex.cn: 交通拥塞和污染

senses.def: the state of part of the body being blocked with blood or mucus

ex.en: congestion of the lungs
ex.cn: 肺淤血

ex.en: medicine to relieve nasal congestion
ex.cn: 治疗鼻塞的药

senses.def: an amount of money that people have to pay for driving their cars into the centre of some cities as a way of stopping the city centre from becoming too full of traffic
senses.chn: 交通拥塞费，进城费（为缓解市中心塞车状况而收取）

senses.def: a large company formed by joining together different firms

ex.en: a media conglomerate
ex.cn: 大众传媒联合体

senses.def: a number of things or parts that are put together to form a whole
a type of rock made of small stones held together by dried clay
a mixture of different things that are found all together

ex.en: a conglomeration of buildings of different sizes and styles
ex.cn: 大小和风格各异的建筑楼群

senses.def: the process of forming a conglomerate or the state of being a conglomerate
a country in central Africa
(a person) from Congo or from the Democratic Republic of the Congo
senses.chn: 刚果人；刚果的；刚果人的

senses.def: to tell sb that you are pleased about their success or achievements

ex.en: I congratulated them all on their results.
ex.cn: 我为他们取得的成就向他们所有人表示祝贺。

ex.en: The authors are to be congratulated on producing such a clear and authoritative work.
ex.cn: 向创作出这样一部具有权威性又清晰易懂的作品的作者们祝贺。

ex.en: Congratulations on your engagement! I hope you'll be very happy.
ex.cn: 恭喜你们订婚！祝你们幸福美满。

ex.en: Well done for passing your driving test.(BrE)
ex.cn: 你通过了驾驶执照考试，很不错！

ex.en: Good job on passing your exams.(NAmE)
ex.cn: 你考试及格了，真棒！

ex.en: I hear you did very well in your exams/you've got a new job/you've had a baby— congratulations!(BrE)
ex.cn: 听说你考得非常好／找到了新工作／喜得贵子——恭喜恭喜！

senses.def: to feel pleased and proud because you have achieved sth or been successful at sth
senses.chn: （为成就或成功）感到自豪，引以为豪

ex.en: You can congratulate yourself on having done an excellent job.
ex.cn: 你应该为你出色的工作感到自豪。

senses.def: a message congratulating sb (= saying that you are happy about their good luck or success)

ex.en: to offer/send your congratulations to sb
ex.cn: 向某人致以祝贺

senses.def: used when you want to congratulate sb

ex.en: 'We're getting married!' 'Congratulations!'
ex.cn: “我们要结婚了！” “恭喜恭喜！”

ex.en: Congratulations on your exam results!
ex.cn: 祝贺你考出了好成绩！

senses.def: the act of congratulating sb

ex.en: a letter of congratulation
ex.cn: 贺信

senses.def: expressing congratulations

ex.en: a congratulatory message
ex.cn: 贺辞

senses.def: to come together in a group

ex.en: Young people often congregate in the main square in the evenings.
ex.cn: 年轻人傍晚时经常聚集在大广场上。

senses.def: a group of people who are gathered together in a church to worship God, not including the priest and choir

ex.en: The congregation stood to sing the hymn.
ex.cn: 会众站起来唱圣歌。

senses.def: a group of people who regularly attend a particular place of worship
senses.chn: （定期去特定地方做礼拜的）会众

senses.def: a type of Christianity in which the congregation of each church is responsible for its own affairs
senses.chn: 公理制，公理主义（主张各地方教会独立行事）

senses.def: a large formal meeting or series of meetings where representatives from different groups discuss ideas, make decisions, etc.

ex.en: an international congress of trades unions
ex.cn: 工会国际代表大会

senses.def: (in the US and some other countries) the name of the group of people who are elected to make laws, in the US consisting of the Senate and the House of Representatives
senses.chn: （美国及其他一些国家的）国会，议会

ex.en: Congress will vote on the proposals tomorrow.
ex.cn: 国会明天将对提案进行投票表决。

senses.def: used in the names of political parties in some countries
senses.chn: （用于某些国家的政党名称）国民大会

ex.en: the African National Congress
ex.cn: 非洲人国民大会

senses.def: related to or belonging to a congress or the Congress in the US
senses.chn: 立法机构的；代表大会的；（美国）国会的

ex.en: a congressional committee/bill
ex.cn: 代表委员会；国会议案

ex.en: the midterm Congressional elections
ex.cn: 国会的中期选举

senses.def: a member of Congress in the US, especially the House of Representatives
senses.chn: （尤指美国众议院的）国会议员；众议员

senses.def: a member of Congress in the US, especially the House of Representatives
senses.chn: （尤指美国众议院的）国会议员；众议员

senses.def: having the same size and shape

ex.en: congruent triangles
ex.cn: 全等三角形

senses.def: suitable for sth; appropriate in a particular situation
senses.chn: 适合的；适当的；恰当的；相称的

senses.def: of or related to a cone
shaped like a cone
senses.chn: 锥形的；圆锥形的；圆锥的

senses.def: a shape formed when a flat surface meets a cone with a round base
any tree that produces hard dry fruit called cones. Most conifers are evergreen (= have leaves that stay on the tree all year).
an opinion or idea that is not based on definite knowledge and is formed by guessing

ex.en: The truth of his conjecture was confirmed by the newspaper report.
ex.cn: 新闻报道证明了他的推测果然不假。

senses.def: the forming of an opinion or idea that is not based on definite knowledge

ex.en: What was going through the killer's mind is a matter for conjecture.
ex.cn: 凶手当时心里是怎样想的，这个问题只能由人们去推测了。

senses.def: to form an opinion about sth even though you do not have much information on it

ex.en: We can only conjecture about what was in the killer's mind.
ex.cn: 我们只能猜测当时凶手心里想的是什么。

ex.en: We can only conjecture what was in the killer's mind.
ex.cn: 我们只能猜测当时凶手心里想的是什么。

ex.en: He conjectured that the population might double in ten years.
ex.cn: 他推测人口在十年后可能会增加一倍。

ex.en: She conjectured the existence of a completely new species.
ex.cn: 她推测有一个全新物种存在。

ex.en: The remains are conjectured to be thousands of years old.
ex.cn: 据推测，这些古迹有几千年的历史。

senses.def: to join together; to join two or more things together
one of two people who are born with their bodies joined together in some way, sometimes sharing the same organs
combining all or both the people or things involved
connected with marriage and the sexual relationship between a husband and wife

ex.en: conjugal love
ex.cn: 夫妻间的恩爱

senses.def: the rights that a husband and wife each has in a marriage, especially the right to have sex with their partner
to give the different forms of a verb, as they vary according to number, person, tense, etc.
senses.chn: （根据数、人称、时态等）列举动词的变化形式

senses.def: to have different forms, showing number, person, tense, etc.
senses.chn: （表示数、人称、时态等）有词形变化形式

ex.en: How does this verb conjugate?
ex.cn: 这个动词有哪些词形变化？

senses.def: the way in which a verb conjugates

ex.en: a verb with an irregular conjugation
ex.cn: 不规则动词

senses.def: a group of verbs that conjugate in the same way
senses.chn: 词形变化相同的一类动词

ex.en: Latin verbs of the second conjugation
ex.cn: 属于第二种词形变化的拉丁语动词

senses.def: a word that joins words, phrases or sentences, for example 'and', 'but', 'or'
a combination of events, etc., that causes a particular result
senses.chn: （引起某种结果的事物等的）结合，同时发生

ex.en: The conjunction of low inflation and low unemployment came as a very pleasant surprise.
ex.cn: 低通货膨胀与低失业的同时出现是一大惊喜。

senses.def: the fact of stars, planets, etc. passing close together as seen from the earth
together with

ex.en: The police are working in conjunction with tax officers on the investigation.
ex.cn: 警方正和税务官员协同进行调查。

ex.en: The system is designed to be used in conjunction with a word processing program.
ex.cn: 本系统是为与文字处理程序配合使用而设计的。

senses.def: an infectious eye disease that causes pain and swelling in part of the eye
to do clever tricks such as making things seem to appear or disappear as if by magic
senses.chn: 变魔术；变戏法；使…变戏法般地出现（或消失）

ex.en: Her grandfather taught her to conjure.
ex.cn: 她的祖父教她变魔术。

ex.en: He could conjure coins from behind people's ears.
ex.cn: 他可以从人们的耳朵后面变出硬币来。

ex.en: Miyazaki is still a name to conjure with among anime fans.
ex.cn: 宫崎骏在日本动漫迷中仍是一个大名鼎鼎的名字。

ex.en: He comes from Tighnabruaich—now there's a name to conjure with!
ex.cn: 他来自 Tighnabruaich，这个名字真够拗口的！

senses.def: to make sth appear as a picture in your mind

ex.en: That smell always conjures up memories of holidays in France.
ex.cn: 那种气味总是勾起对法国度假那段日子的回忆。

senses.def: to make sb/sth appear by using special magic words
to create sth or make sth appear in a surprising or unexpected way
senses.chn: 令人惊讶地创造出；使意外地出现

ex.en: He conjured a delicious meal out of a few leftovers.
ex.cn: 他居然用几样吃剩的东西做出了可口的一餐。

senses.def: entertainment in the form of magic tricks, especially ones which seem to make things appear or disappear

ex.en: a conjuring trick
ex.cn: 魔术

senses.def: a person who performs conjuring tricks
to hit sb hard on their head
to stop working

ex.en: The car conked out halfway up the hill.
ex.cn: 汽车在上坡时半途抛锚了。

senses.def: to go to sleep
a person's nose
the smooth shiny brown nut of the horse chestnut tree
a children's game played with conkers on strings, in which two players take turns to try to hit and break each other's conker
senses.chn: 康克戏（儿童游戏，双方用系在绳上的七叶果轮流互击，以击破对方的七叶果）

senses.def: to stop working

ex.en: The car conked out halfway up the hill.
ex.cn: 汽车在上坡时半途抛锚了。

senses.def: to go to sleep
a man who tricks others into giving him money, etc.
to join together two or more things; to be joined together

ex.en: The towns are connected by train and bus services.
ex.cn: 这些城镇由火车和公共汽车连接起来。

ex.en: The canal was built to connect Sheffield with the Humber estuary.
ex.cn: 修建这条运河是为了将设菲尔德和亨伯河河口连接起来。

ex.en: a connecting door (= one that connects two rooms)
ex.cn: 连通两间房的门

ex.en: The rooms on this floor connect.
ex.cn: 这层楼的房间是相通的。

senses.def: to join sth to the main supply of electricity, gas, water, etc. or to another piece of equipment

ex.en: First connect the printer to the computer.
ex.cn: 首先把打印机与计算机接通。

ex.en: We're waiting for the telephone to be connected.
ex.cn: 我们等待着接通电话。

senses.def: to join a computer or a mobile device to the Internet or to a computer network
senses.chn: （使计算机或移动设备）连接（到互联网或计算机网络）

ex.en: Click 'Continue' to connect to the Internet.
ex.cn: 点击 Continue 连接到互联网。

senses.def: to notice or make a link between people, things, events, etc.
senses.chn: 注意到…有关联；把…联系起来

ex.en: There was nothing to connect him with the crime.
ex.cn: 他与那起犯罪毫无关联。

ex.en: I was surprised to hear them mentioned together: I had never connected them before.
ex.cn: 听到有人把他们牵扯在一起让我很吃惊；我以前从未把他们联起来想过。

senses.def: to arrive just before another one leaves so that passengers can change from one to the other

ex.en: His flight to Amsterdam connects with an afternoon flight to New York.
ex.cn: 他飞往阿姆斯特丹的班机与下午飞往纽约的一趟航班相衔接。

ex.en: There's a connecting flight at noon.
ex.cn: 中午有一趟相衔接的航班。

senses.def: to join telephone lines so that people can speak to each other

ex.en: Hold on please, I'm trying to connect you.
ex.cn: 请别挂电话，我在尽力给您接通。

senses.def: to form a good relationship with sb so that you like and understand each other

ex.en: They met a couple of times but they didn't really connect.
ex.cn: 尽管他们见了几次面，但仍未真正建立起良好的关系。

senses.def: to hit sb/sth

ex.en: The blow connected and she felt a surge of pain.
ex.cn: 她遭到沉重的一击，感到一阵疼痛。

senses.def: to join sth to a supply of electricity, gas, etc. or to another piece of equipment; to be joined in this way
senses.chn: 将…（与电源、煤气、设备等）连接起来，接通

ex.en: She connected up the two computers.
ex.cn: 她把两台计算机连接起来。

senses.def: (of two or more things or people) having a link between them
senses.chn: （两个或以上的事物或人）有联系的，相关的

ex.en: market prices and other connected matters
ex.cn: 市场价格及其他相关事宜

ex.en: They are connected by marriage.
ex.cn: 他们是姻亲。

ex.en: jobs connected with the environment
ex.cn: 与环境有关的工作

ex.en: The two issues are closely connected.
ex.cn: 这两个问题紧密相关。

senses.def: a feeling that you have a link with sb/sth or are part of a group

ex.en: the benefits of helping students feel a sense of connectedness to their school
ex.cn: 帮助学生感到自己是学校一分子的益处

senses.def: a small US state forming part of New England. It was one of the 13 original states. The capital city is Hartford and its largest city is Bridgeport.
senses.chn: 康涅狄格（美国小州，位于新英格兰地区，是最初的 13 个州之一。首府哈特福德，最大城市布里奇波特）

senses.def: something that connects two facts, ideas, etc.
senses.chn: （两种事实、想法等的）联系，关联

ex.en: Scientists have established a connection between cholesterol levels and heart disease.
ex.cn: 科学家已证实胆固醇含量与心脏病之间有关联。

ex.en: a direct/close/strong connection with sth
ex.cn: 与某事有直接的／密切的／牢固的联系

ex.en: How did you make the connection (= realize that there was a connection between two facts that did not seem to be related)?
ex.cn: 你怎么看出来有这种关系的？

senses.def: the act of connecting or the state of being connected

ex.en: Connection to the gas supply was delayed for three days.
ex.cn: 接通煤气延迟了三天。

ex.en: I'm having problems with my Internet connection.
ex.cn: 我的互联网连接有问题。

senses.def: a point, especially in an electrical system, where two parts connect
senses.chn: 连接点；（尤指电力系统的）接头

ex.en: A faulty connection caused the machine to stop.
ex.cn: 线路接错导致机器停止运转。

senses.def: a train, bus or plane at a station or an airport that a passenger can take soon after getting off another in order to continue their journey

ex.en: We arrived in good time for the connection to Paris.
ex.cn: 我们到达后有充分的时间接上去巴黎的联运。

senses.def: a means of travelling to another place

ex.en: There are good bus and train connections between the resort and major cities.
ex.cn: 在度假胜地与主要城市之间有着便利的公共汽车和火车运输。

senses.def: a person or an organization that you know and that can help or advise you in your social or professional life
senses.chn: 有社交或业务关系的人（或机构）

ex.en: One of my business connections gave them my name.
ex.cn: 我生意上的一个关系户向他们提供了我的名字。

senses.def: people who are your relatives, but not members of your close family

ex.en: She is British but also has German connections.
ex.cn: 她是英国人，但也有德国亲戚。

senses.def: for reasons connected with sb/sth

ex.en: A man has been arrested in connection with the murder of the teenager.
ex.cn: 一名男子因与该谋杀少年案有关而被捕。

ex.en: I am writing to you in connection with your recent job application.
ex.cn: 我写此信与你最近求职一事有关。

senses.def: for reasons connected with sth recently mentioned
that connects things

ex.en: connective tissue
ex.cn: 结缔组织

senses.def: a word that connects two parts of a sentence

ex.en: Don't overuse a causal connective like 'because'.
ex.cn: 不要过多地使用像 because 这样表示原因的连接词。

senses.def: the state of being connected or the degree to which two things are connected

ex.en: ISDN connectivity allows computers to communicate over a network.
ex.cn: 综合业务数字网连接实现了计算机网络通信。

senses.def: a thing that links two or more things together

ex.en: a cable connector
ex.cn: 电缆连接器

senses.def: a raised structure on a submarine containing the periscope
a sudden attack of anger or fear

ex.en: He had a conniption when he heard the news.
ex.cn: 他听到消息后大发雷霆。

senses.def: help in doing sth wrong; the failure to stop sth wrong from happening

ex.en: The crime was committed with the connivance of a police officer.
ex.cn: 这项罪行是在警察的纵容下发生的。

senses.def: to seem to allow sth wrong to happen

ex.en: She knew that if she said nothing she would be conniving in an injustice.
ex.cn: 她知道她如果什么也不说就是在纵容不公正的行为。

senses.def: to work together with sb to do sth wrong or illegal
senses.chn: 共谋；狼狈为奸；同流合污

ex.en: The government was accused of having connived with the security forces to permit murder.
ex.cn: 政府被指控与安全部队狼狈为奸放任谋杀。

senses.def: behaving in a way that secretly hurts others or deliberately fails to prevent others from being hurt
senses.chn: 暗算他人的；故意纵容的

senses.def: an expert on matters involving the judgement of beauty, quality or skill in art, food or music

ex.en: a connoisseur of Italian painting
ex.cn: 意大利绘画鉴赏家

ex.en: a wine connoisseur
ex.cn: 葡萄酒鉴定家

senses.def: an idea suggested by a word in addition to its main meaning

ex.en: The word 'professional' has connotations of skill and excellence.
ex.cn: professional 这个词隐含着技艺和专长的意思。

ex.en: negative connotations
ex.cn: 贬义

senses.def: to suggest a feeling, an idea, etc. as well as the main meaning
related to marriage, or the relationship between husband and wife
to take control of a country or city and its people by force

ex.en: The Normans conquered England in 1066.
ex.cn: 诺曼人于 1066 年征服了英格兰。

ex.en: conquered peoples/races/territories
ex.cn: 被征服的民族／种族；被占领的领土

senses.def: to defeat sb, especially in a competition, race, etc.
senses.chn: （尤指比赛、赛跑等中）击败，战胜

ex.en: The world champion conquered yet another challenger last night.
ex.cn: 昨晚这位世界冠军又战胜了一名挑战者。

senses.def: to succeed in dealing with or controlling sth

ex.en: The only way to conquer a fear is to face it.
ex.cn: 克服恐惧的唯一方法是正视恐惧。

ex.en: Mont Blanc was conquered (= successfully climbed) in 1786.
ex.cn: 勃朗峰于 1786 年被征服。

senses.def: to become very popular or successful in a place
senses.chn: 在（某地）很受欢迎；在（某地）成功

ex.en: The band is now setting out to conquer the world.
ex.cn: 这支乐队现在要出发去征服世界。

senses.def: a person who conquers

ex.en: William the Conqueror (= King William I of England)
ex.cn: 征服者威廉（英国国王威廉一世）

senses.def: the act of taking control of a country, city, etc. by force

ex.en: the Norman Conquest (= of England in 1066)
ex.cn: 诺曼征服（即 1066 年诺曼人征服英格兰）

senses.def: an area of land taken by force

ex.en: the Spanish conquests in South America
ex.cn: 西班牙人在南美洲的占领地

senses.def: a person that sb has persuaded to love them or to have sex with them

ex.en: I'm just one of his many conquests.
ex.cn: 我仅仅是他的众多俘虏之一。

senses.def: the act of gaining control over sth that is difficult or dangerous

ex.en: the conquest of inflation
ex.cn: 对通货膨胀的控制

senses.def: one of the Spanish people who took control of Mexico and Peru by force in the 16th century
senses.chn: （16 世纪侵占墨西哥和秘鲁的）西班牙征服者

senses.def: relationship by birth in the same family
the part of your mind that tells you whether your actions are right or wrong

ex.en: to have a clear/guilty conscience (= to feel that you have done right/wrong)
ex.cn: 问心无愧／有愧

ex.en: This is a matter of individual conscience (= everyone must make their own judgement about it).
ex.cn: 这关系到个人的良知。

ex.en: He won't let it trouble his conscience.
ex.cn: 他不会让这件事搞得自己良心不安的。

senses.def: a guilty feeling about sth you have done or failed to do

ex.en: She was seized by a sudden pang of conscience.
ex.cn: 她突然感到一阵内疚。

ex.en: I have a terrible conscience about it.
ex.cn: 我对此事深感愧疚。

senses.def: the fact of behaving in a way that you feel is right even though this may cause problems

ex.en: freedom of conscience (= the freedom to do what you believe to be right)
ex.cn: 凭良心行事的自由

ex.en: Emilia is the voice of conscience in the play.
ex.cn: 埃米莉亚在这出戏中是良知的代言人。

senses.def: believing your actions to be fair
senses.chn: （认为行为）公正地，公平地，凭良心

ex.en: We cannot in all conscience refuse to help.
ex.cn: 凭良心我们不能拒绝去帮助别人。

senses.def: making you feel guilty for doing or failing to do sth

ex.en: I'll write and apologize. I've had it on my conscience for weeks.
ex.cn: 我要写信赔礼道歉。几个星期以来我都为此而良心不安。

senses.def: to make you feel guilty about sth; to feel guilty about sth
senses.chn: 唤醒良心；受到良心谴责

ex.en: Her conscience pricked her as she lied to her sister.
ex.cn: 她对姐姐撒谎时良心上感到很不安。

senses.def: feeling guilty about sth you have done or failed to do
senses.chn: 内疚的；不安的；受良心责备的

senses.def: taking care to do things carefully and correctly
senses.chn: 勤勉认真的；一丝不苟的

ex.en: a conscientious student/teacher/worker
ex.cn: 勤勉认真的学生；一丝不苟的老师；认真负责的工人

senses.def: a person who refuses to serve in the armed forces for moral reasons
senses.chn: 出于道义原因而拒服兵役者

senses.def: to make sb/yourself aware of important social or political issues
senses.chn: 使意识到（重大社会或政治问题）；使觉悟

ex.en: People need to be conscientized about their rights.
ex.cn: 需要让人们明白自己的权利。

senses.def: aware of sth; noticing sth

ex.en: She's very conscious of the problems involved.
ex.cn: 她完全意识到了所涉及的问题。

ex.en: He became acutely conscious of having failed his parents.
ex.cn: 他深深感到自己辜负了父母的期望。

ex.en: I was vaguely conscious that I was being watched.
ex.cn: 我隐隐约约地觉察到有人在监视我。

senses.def: able to use your senses and mental powers to understand what is happening
senses.chn: 神志清醒的；有知觉的；有意识的

ex.en: A patient who is not fully conscious should never be left alone.
ex.cn: 神志并非完全清醒的病人必须时刻有人照料。

senses.def: deliberate or controlled

ex.en: to make a conscious decision
ex.cn: 作出慎重的决定

ex.en: I made a conscious effort to get there on time.
ex.cn: 我刻意约束自己准时到达那里。

ex.en: a conscious act of cruelty
ex.cn: 蓄意的残暴行径

senses.def: being particularly interested in sth

ex.en: environmentally conscious
ex.cn: 有环保意识的

ex.en: They have become increasingly health-conscious.
ex.cn: 他们的健康意识越来越强。

senses.def: the state of being able to use your senses and mental powers to understand what is happening

ex.en: I can't remember any more—I must have lost consciousness.
ex.cn: 我什么都想不起来了，我当时一定是失去了知觉。

ex.en: She did not regain consciousness and died the next day.
ex.cn: 她再也没有苏醒过来，第二天便去世了。

senses.def: the state of being aware of sth

ex.en: his consciousness of the challenge facing him
ex.cn: 他对所面临的挑战的清醒意识

ex.en: class-consciousness (= consciousness of different classes in society)
ex.cn: 阶级意识

senses.def: the ideas and opinions of a person or group

ex.en: her newly developed political consciousness
ex.cn: 她最近形成的政治观念

senses.def: the process of making people aware of important social and political issues
senses.chn: （社会或政治）觉悟提高，意识加强

senses.def: to make sb join the armed forces

ex.en: He was conscripted into the army in 1939.
ex.cn: 他于 1939 年应征入伍。

senses.def: a person who has been conscripted to join the armed forces

ex.en: young army conscripts
ex.cn: 年轻的应征士兵

ex.en: conscript soldiers/armies
ex.cn: 应征入伍的士兵；由应征入伍者组成的部队

senses.def: the practice of ordering people by law to serve in the armed forces
to state officially in a religious ceremony that sth is holy and can be used for religious purposes

ex.en: The church was consecrated in 1853.
ex.cn: 这座教堂于 1853 年祝圣。

ex.en: consecrated ground
ex.cn: 经祝圣的地方

senses.def: to make bread and wine into the body and blood of Christ
to state officially in a religious ceremony that sb is now a priest, etc.

ex.en: He was consecrated (as) bishop last year.
ex.cn: 他于去年被祝圣为主教。

senses.def: to give sth/sb/yourself to a special purpose, especially a religious one
following one after another in a series, without interruption

ex.en: She was absent for nine consecutive days.
ex.cn: 她一连缺席了九天。

ex.en: He is beginning his fourth consecutive term of office.
ex.cn: 他开始了第四届任期。

senses.def: which people in general agree with

ex.en: a consensual approach
ex.cn: 一致赞成的方法

senses.def: which the people taking part have agreed to

ex.en: consensual sex
ex.cn: 两厢情愿的性行为

senses.def: an opinion that all members of a group agree with

ex.en: She is skilled at achieving consensus on sensitive issues.
ex.cn: 她擅长就敏感问题进行斡旋，从而达成共识。

ex.en: There is a growing consensus of opinion on this issue.
ex.cn: 对这个问题的看法日趋一致。

ex.en: an attempt to reach a consensus
ex.cn: 达成共识的尝试

ex.en: There is a general consensus among teachers about the need for greater security in schools.
ex.cn: 教师们对必须加强学校的安全工作有普遍的共识。

ex.en: There seems to be a consensus that the plan should be rejected.
ex.cn: 看来人们一致同意放弃这一计划。

senses.def: permission to do sth, especially given by sb in authority

ex.en: Children under 16 cannot give consent to medical treatment.
ex.cn: 16 岁以下的儿童不得自行同意接受治疗。

ex.en: The written consent of a parent is required.
ex.cn: 要求有家长的书面同意。

ex.en: to refuse/withhold your consent
ex.cn: 拒不同意

ex.en: He is charged with taking a car without the owner's consent.
ex.cn: 他因未征得车主的同意自行开走车而受到指控。

senses.def: agreement about sth

ex.en: She was chosen as leader by common consent (= everyone agreed to the choice).
ex.cn: 大家一致同意选她为领导人。

ex.en: By mutual consent they didn't go out (= they both agreed not to).
ex.cn: 他俩一致同意不出门了。

senses.def: an official document giving permission for sth
to agree to sth or give your permission for sth

ex.en: When she told them what she intended they readily consented.
ex.cn: 她告诉他们她的打算时，他们欣然同意。

ex.en: He reluctantly consented to his daughter's marriage.
ex.cn: 他勉强同意了女儿的婚事。

ex.en: She finally consented to answer our questions.
ex.cn: 她最终同意回答我们的问题。

ex.en: He agreed to let me go early.
ex.cn: 他容许我早走。

ex.en: They accepted the court's decision.
ex.cn: 他们接受法院的判决。

ex.en: The committee unanimously approved the plan.
ex.cn: 委员会一致通过了计划。

senses.def: a person who is considered old enough, by law, to decide whether they should agree to have sex; a person who has agreed to have sex
senses.chn: 到达法定性成熟年龄的已成年人；同意发生性行为的已成年人

senses.def: a result of sth that has happened

ex.en: This decision could have serious consequences for the industry.
ex.cn: 这项决定可能对该行业造成严重后果。

ex.en: Two hundred people lost their jobs as a direct consequence of the merger.
ex.cn: 合并一事直接导致二百人失去了工作。

ex.en: He drove too fast with tragic consequences.
ex.cn: 他开车太快，结果酿成惨剧。

ex.en: to suffer/face/take the consequences of your actions
ex.cn: 自食其果；面对／承担自己行为的后果

ex.en: She died as a result of her injuries.
ex.cn: 她因伤死亡。

ex.en: This book is the result of 25 years of research.
ex.cn: 这本书是 25 年研究的结晶。

senses.def: importance

ex.en: Don't worry. It's of no consequence.
ex.cn: 别担心，这无关紧要。

senses.def: as a result of sth

ex.en: The child was born deformed in consequence of an injury to the mother.
ex.cn: 由于母亲受过伤，这小孩生下来是畸形的。

senses.def: happening as a result of sth
senses.chn: 随之发生的；作为结果的

ex.en: the lowering of taxes and the consequent increase in spending
ex.cn: 税收降低与随之引起的消费增长

ex.en: the responsibilities consequent upon the arrival of a new child
ex.cn: 新生儿出世后随之而来的职责

senses.def: happening as a result or an effect of sth
senses.chn: 随之而来的；相应发生的；作为结果的

ex.en: retirement and the consequential reduction in income
ex.cn: 退休与随之而来的收入减少

senses.def: important; that will have important results
senses.chn: 重要的；将产生重大结果的

ex.en: The report discusses a number of consequential matters that are yet to be decided.
ex.cn: 这份报告讨论了许多有待决定的重大问题。

senses.def: as a result; therefore

ex.en: This poses a threat to agriculture and the food chain, and consequently to human health.
ex.cn: 这会对农业和食物链造成威胁，因而危及人的健康。

ex.en: One consequence of changes in diet over recent years has been a dramatic increase in cases of childhood obesity.
ex.cn: 近年来饮食变化带来的一个结果是儿童肥胖人数急剧上升。

ex.en: Many parents today do not have time to cook healthy meals for their children. Consequently / As a consequence, many children grow up eating too much junk food.
ex.cn: 现在许多家长没有时间给孩子做健康的饭菜，结果造成许多孩子在成长过程中吃过多的垃圾食品。

ex.en: Many children spend their free time watching TV instead of playing outside. As a result, more and more of them are becoming overweight.
ex.cn: 许多孩子把他们的闲暇时间都花在看电视上，而不是进行户外活动，从而导致越来越多的孩子变得肥胖。

ex.en: Last year junk food was banned in schools. The effect of this has been to create a black market in the playground, with pupils bringing sweets from home to sell to other pupils.
ex.cn: 去年学校禁售垃圾食品，结果是学校操场上出现了垃圾食品的黑市交易，有的学生把从家里带来的甜食卖给其他学生。

senses.def: a group of officials who control the use of a port, a river, an area of land, etc.
senses.chn: （港口、河流、地区等的）管理机构

ex.en: the Thames Conservancy
ex.cn: 泰晤士河管理委员会

ex.en: Texas Nature Conservancy
ex.cn: 得克萨斯州自然资源管理委员会

senses.def: the protection of the natural environment

ex.en: nature conservancy
ex.cn: 自然环境的保护

senses.def: the protection of the natural environment

ex.en: to be interested in wildlife conservation
ex.cn: 对野生动物保护感兴趣

senses.def: the official protection of buildings that have historical or artistic importance
senses.chn: （官方对历史或艺术建筑的）保护；文物保护

senses.def: the act of preventing sth from being lost, wasted, damaged or destroyed
senses.chn: 防止流失（或浪费、损害、毁坏）；保持；保护

ex.en: to encourage the conservation of water/fuel
ex.cn: 鼓励节约用水／燃料

ex.en: energy conservation
ex.cn: 能源的节约

senses.def: (in the UK) an area where the natural environment or the buildings are protected by law from being damaged or changed
senses.chn: （英国自然环境或建筑物的）保护区

senses.def: a person who takes an active part in the protection of the environment

ex.en: a meeting of local conservationists
ex.cn: 当地自然环境保护主义者的会议

senses.def: the tendency to resist great or sudden change

ex.en: the innate conservatism of older people
ex.cn: 老年人固有的保守性

senses.def: the political belief that society should change as little as possible

ex.en: an examination of the political theories of conservatism and liberalism
ex.cn: 对保守主义和自由主义政治理论的审视

senses.def: the principles of the Conservative Party in British politics
opposed to great or sudden social change; showing that you prefer traditional styles and values

ex.en: the conservative views of his parents
ex.cn: 他父母的保守观念

ex.en: Her style of dress was never conservative.
ex.cn: 她的服装式样一点儿也不保守。

senses.def: connected with the British Conservative Party

ex.en: Conservative members/supporters
ex.cn: 保守党的党员／支持者

senses.def: lower than what is probably the real amount or number
senses.chn: 低于实际数量的；保守的

ex.en: At a conservative estimate, he'll be earning £50 000.
ex.cn: 按照保守的估计，他会赚到 5 万英镑。

senses.def: a member or supporter of the British Conservative Party
senses.chn: （英国）保守党党员，保守党支持者

senses.def: a conservative person
a school or college at which people are trained in music and theatre
senses.chn: 音乐（或戏剧）专科学校（或学院）

senses.def: a person who is responsible for repairing and preserving works of art, buildings and other things of cultural interest
senses.chn: 文物修复员；文物保护员

senses.def: a room with glass walls and a glass roof that is built on the side of a house. Conservatories are used for sitting in to enjoy the sun, and to protect plants from cold weather.
senses.chn: （靠房屋一侧用玻璃建造的）温室，暖房

senses.def: a school or college at which people are trained in music and theatre
senses.chn: 音乐（或戏剧）专科学校（或学院）

senses.def: to use as little of sth as possible so that it lasts a long time

ex.en: Help to conserve energy by insulating your home.
ex.cn: 对房屋做隔热处理来帮助节约能源。

senses.def: to protect sth and prevent it from being changed or destroyed

ex.en: new laws to conserve wildlife in the area
ex.cn: 保护该地区野生动物的新法令

senses.def: jam containing large or whole pieces of fruit
senses.chn: （含有大块或整块水果的）果酱，蜜饯

senses.def: to think about sth carefully, especially in order to make a decision
senses.chn: （尤指为作出决定而）仔细考虑，细想

ex.en: I'd like some time to consider.
ex.cn: 我希望有些时间考虑一下。

ex.en: She considered her options.
ex.cn: 她仔细考虑了自己的各种选择。

ex.en: a carefully considered response
ex.cn: 经过仔细考虑的回复

ex.en: The company is being actively considered as a potential partner (= it is thought possible that it could become one).
ex.cn: 这家公司正在被积极考虑为可能的合作伙伴。

ex.en: We're considering buying a new car.
ex.cn: 我们在考虑买一辆新车。

ex.en: We need to consider how the law might be reformed.
ex.cn: 我们得斟酌法律应如何修订。

senses.def: to think of sb/sth in a particular way

ex.en: He considers himself an expert on the subject.
ex.cn: 他认为自己是这门学科的专家。

ex.en: This award is considered (to be) a great honour.
ex.cn: 这项奖被视为极大的荣誉。

ex.en: These workers are considered (as) a high-risk group.
ex.cn: 这些工人被视为高风险人群。

ex.en: Consider yourself lucky you weren't fired.
ex.cn: 你没被解雇，算是万幸。

ex.en: Who do you consider (to be) responsible for the accident?
ex.cn: 你认为谁对这起事故负有责任？

ex.en: He's generally considered to have the finest tenor voice in the country.
ex.cn: 普遍认为他是全国最佳男高音歌手。

senses.def: to think about sth, especially the feelings of other people, and be influenced by it when making a decision, etc.

ex.en: You should consider other people before you act.
ex.cn: 你在行动之前应当考虑到别人。

senses.def: to look carefully at sb/sth

ex.en: He stood there, considering the painting.
ex.cn: 他站在那里，凝视着那幅画。

senses.def: thinking carefully about all the facts, especially the problems or difficulties, of a situation
senses.chn: 从各方面看来；考虑到所有情况；总而言之

ex.en: She's had a lot of problems since her husband died but she seems quite cheerful, all things considered.
ex.cn: 自从丈夫死后，她面临很多困难，但总的来说她看上去情绪还是挺乐观的。

senses.def: your opinion that is the result of careful thought
senses.chn: 成熟的意见；经过深思熟虑的意见

senses.def: great in amount, size, importance, etc.

ex.en: The project wasted a considerable amount of time and money.
ex.cn: 那项工程耗费了相当多的时间和资金。

ex.en: Damage to the building was considerable.
ex.cn: 对这栋建筑物的损坏相当严重。

senses.def: much; a lot

ex.en: The need for sleep varies considerably from person to person.
ex.cn: 不同的人对睡眠的需要差异相当大。

senses.def: always thinking of other people's wishes and feelings; careful not to hurt or upset others
senses.chn: 考虑周到的；为（他人）着想的；体谅的；体贴的

ex.en: She is always polite and considerate towards her employees.
ex.cn: 她对待雇员总是客客气气，关心体谅。

ex.en: It was very considerate of him to wait.
ex.cn: 他一直在等候着，真是体贴。

senses.def: the act of thinking carefully about sth

ex.en: Careful consideration should be given to issues of health and safety.
ex.cn: 健康与安全的问题应该认真予以考虑。

ex.en: The proposals are currently under consideration (= being discussed).
ex.cn: 那些提案目前正在审议中。

ex.en: After a few moments' consideration, he began to speak.
ex.cn: 他想了片刻后开始讲话。

ex.en: a consideration of the legal issues involved
ex.cn: 对有关法律问题的考虑

senses.def: something that must be thought about when you are planning or deciding sth
senses.chn: （作计划或决定时）必须考虑的事（或因素、原因）

ex.en: economic/commercial/environmental/practical considerations
ex.cn: 需要考虑的经济／商业／环境／实际因素

ex.en: Time is another important consideration.
ex.cn: 时间是另一个需要考虑的重要因素。

senses.def: the quality of being sensitive towards others and thinking about their wishes and feelings
senses.chn: （对他人的）考虑周到，体谅，顾及

ex.en: They showed no consideration whatsoever for my feelings.
ex.cn: 他们根本不体谅我的感受。

ex.en: Journalists stayed away from the funeral out of consideration for the bereaved family.
ex.cn: 出于对亡人家属的考虑，新闻记者没有到葬礼现场。

senses.def: a reward or payment for a service
as payment for sth

ex.en: a small sum in consideration of your services
ex.cn: 对你服务的微薄酬金

senses.def: to think about and include a particular thing or fact when you are forming an opinion or making a decision

ex.en: The candidates' experience and qualifications will be taken into consideration when the decision is made.
ex.cn: 作决定时要考虑候选人的经验和资格。

ex.en: Taking everything into consideration, the event was a great success.
ex.cn: 总的说来，这项活动取得了极大的成功。

senses.def: after thinking about sth carefully and for a long time
senses.chn: 经过深思熟虑；经过审慎考虑

senses.def: used to show that you are thinking about a particular fact, and are influenced by it, when you make a statement about sth

ex.en: She's very active, considering her age.
ex.cn: 就她的年龄来说，她是十分活跃的。

ex.en: Considering he's only just started, he knows quite a lot about it.
ex.cn: 鉴于他才刚刚开始，他懂得的已经不少了。

ex.en: You've done very well, considering (= in the difficult circumstances).
ex.cn: 考虑到处境的艰难，你已经做得相当不错了。

senses.def: to put sb/sth somewhere in order to get rid of them/it

ex.en: I consigned her letter to the wastebasket.
ex.cn: 我把她的信丢进了废纸篓。

ex.en: What I didn't want was to see my mother consigned to an old people's home.
ex.cn: 我所不愿意的是看到我母亲被送进养老院。

senses.def: to put sb/sth in an unpleasant situation
senses.chn: 把…置于（令人不快的境地）；打发；发落

ex.en: The decision to close the factory has consigned 6 000 people to the scrapheap.
ex.cn: 关闭那家工厂的决定使 6 000 人遭到了遗弃。

ex.en: A car accident consigned him to a wheelchair for the rest of his life.
ex.cn: 一次车祸使他落得在轮椅上度过余生。

senses.def: to give or send sth to sb
a quantity of goods that are sent or delivered somewhere

ex.en: a consignment of medicines
ex.cn: 运送的一批药物

senses.def: the act of sending or delivering sb/sth

a shop/store where people take their old clothes, etc. to be sold to sb else. The consignment shop keeps part of the money after an item is sold and gives the other part to the person who brought it in.
to have sth as the main or only part or feature

ex.en: The beauty of the city consists in its magnificent buildings.
ex.cn: 这座城市的美就在于它那些宏伟的建筑。

ex.en: True education does not consist in simply being taught facts.
ex.cn: 真正的教育并不在于仅仅讲授事实。

senses.def: to be formed from the people or things mentioned

ex.en: The committee consists of ten members.
ex.cn: 委员会由十人组成。

ex.en: Their diet consisted largely of vegetables.
ex.cn: 他们的日常饮食以蔬菜为主。

ex.en: Most of the fieldwork consisted of making tape recordings.
ex.cn: 现场工作多半为进行磁带录音。

ex.en: Their diet consists largely of vegetables.
ex.cn: 他们的日常饮食以蔬菜为主。

ex.en: The collection comprises 327 paintings.
ex.cn: 这组收藏有 327 幅画。

ex.en: Older people comprise a large proportion of those living in poverty.
ex.cn: 在那些生活贫困的人中，老年人占很大的比例。

senses.def: the quality of always behaving in the same way or of having the same opinions, standard, etc.; the quality of being consistent

ex.en: She has played with great consistency all season.
ex.cn: 她整个赛季表现相当稳定。

ex.en: We need to ensure the consistency of service to our customers.
ex.cn: 我们对客户要确保服务的连贯性。

senses.def: the consistency of a mixture or a liquid substance is how thick, smooth, etc. it is
senses.chn: 黏稠度；密实度；平滑度；坚实度

ex.en: Beat the ingredients together to a creamy consistency.
ex.cn: 把配料搅拌成乳脂状。

ex.en: The cement should have the consistency of wet sand.
ex.cn: 水泥的稠度应如湿沙。

senses.def: always behaving in the same way, or having the same opinions, standards, etc.

ex.en: She's not very consistent in the way she treats her children.
ex.cn: 她对待孩子反复无常。

ex.en: He has been Milan's most consistent (= most consistently good) player this season.
ex.cn: 他是米兰队这个赛季状态最稳定的队员。

ex.en: We must be consistent in applying the rules.
ex.cn: 我们在实施这些规则时必须保持一贯性。

ex.en: a consistent approach to the problem
ex.cn: 解决问题的一贯方法

senses.def: happening in the same way and continuing for a period of time

ex.en: the party's consistent failure to come up with any new policies
ex.cn: 这个政党长时间提不出任何新政策

ex.en: a pattern of consistent growth in the economy
ex.cn: 经济持续增长的模式

senses.def: in agreement with sth; not contradicting sth
senses.chn: 与…一致的；相符的；符合的；不矛盾的

ex.en: The results are entirely consistent with our earlier research.
ex.cn: 这些结果与我们早些时候的研究完全吻合。

ex.en: injuries consistent with a fall from an upper storey (= similar to those such a fall would have caused)
ex.cn: 和从楼上摔下来的情形相符合的伤处

senses.def: having different parts that all agree with each other

ex.en: a well-thought-out and consistent argument
ex.cn: 经过深思熟虑的、相互连贯的论点

senses.def: to have sth as the main or only part or feature

ex.en: The beauty of the city consists in its magnificent buildings.
ex.cn: 这座城市的美就在于它那些宏伟的建筑。

ex.en: True education does not consist in simply being taught facts.
ex.cn: 真正的教育并不在于仅仅讲授事实。

senses.def: a thing or person that makes you feel better when you are unhappy or disappointed
senses.chn: 使感到安慰的人（或物）；安慰；慰藉

ex.en: a few words of consolation
ex.cn: 几句安慰的话

ex.en: If it's any consolation, she didn't get the job, either.
ex.cn: 不知道这算不算得上安慰，她也没有得到那份工作。

ex.en: The children were a great consolation to him when his wife died.
ex.cn: 他妻子去世后，几个孩子就是他极大的安慰。

senses.def: a small prize given to sb who has not won a competition
intended to make sb who is unhappy or disappointed feel better
to give comfort or sympathy to sb who is unhappy or disappointed

ex.en: Nothing could console him when his wife died.
ex.cn: 他妻子去世后，什么事情也不能使他感到宽慰。

ex.en: She put a consoling arm around his shoulders.
ex.cn: 她搂住他肩膀以示安慰。

ex.en: Console yourself with the thought that you did your best.
ex.cn: 你可以安慰自己的是你已经尽了最大的努力。

ex.en: I didn't like lying but I consoled myself that it was for a good cause.
ex.cn: 我不愿意撒谎，但我安慰自己那是出于好意。

ex.en: 'Never mind,' Anne consoled her.
ex.cn: “没关系。” 安妮安慰她说。

senses.def: a flat surface which contains all the controls and switches for a machine, a piece of electronic equipment, etc.
senses.chn: （机器、电子设备等的）控制台，操纵台，仪表板

senses.def: a small electronic device for playing video games
to make a position of power or success stronger so that it is more likely to continue

ex.en: With this new movie he has consolidated his position as the country's leading director.
ex.cn: 他新执导的影片巩固了他作为全国最佳导演的地位。

ex.en: Italy consolidated their lead with a second goal.
ex.cn: 意大利队的第二个进球巩固了其领先的地位。

senses.def: to join things together into one; to be joined into one

ex.en: All the debts have been consolidated.
ex.cn: 所有债项均已合并。

ex.en: consolidated accounts
ex.cn: 合并账目

ex.en: The two companies consolidated for greater efficiency.
ex.cn: 为提高效率，这两家公司已合并。

senses.def: agreement

ex.en: a policy that is popular because of its consonance with traditional party doctrine
ex.cn: 因与传统的政党宗旨一致而受欢迎的政策

senses.def: a combination of musical notes that sound pleasing together
a speech sound made by completely or partly stopping the flow of air being breathed out through the mouth
a letter of the alphabet that represents a consonant sound, for example 'b', 'c', 'd', 'f', etc.
senses.chn: 辅音字母（如 b、c、d、f 等）

senses.def: agreeing with or being the same as sth else
senses.chn: （与…）一致的，符合的，相同的，和谐的

senses.def: relating to or consisting of a consonant or consonants
the husband or wife of a ruler

ex.en: the Prince Consort (= the queen's husband)
ex.cn: 女王的丈夫

senses.def: a group of old-fashioned musical instruments, or a group of musicians who play music from several centuries ago
senses.chn: 一组（古乐器）；（演奏几世纪前音乐的）一组乐师

senses.def: to spend time with sb that other people do not approve of

ex.en: He is known to have consorted with prostitutes.
ex.cn: 众所周知他曾与妓女厮混在一起。

senses.def: a group of people, countries, companies, etc. who are working together on a particular project
senses.chn: （合作进行某项工程的）财团，银团，联营企业

ex.en: the Anglo-French consortium that built the Channel Tunnel
ex.cn: 修建英吉利海峡隧道的英法财团

senses.def: easy to see or notice; likely to attract attention
senses.chn: 易见的；明显的；惹人注意的

ex.en: Mary's red hair always made her conspicuous at school.
ex.cn: 玛丽的红头发在学校里总是很惹眼。

ex.en: I felt very conspicuous in my new car.
ex.cn: 坐在我的新车里，我感到十分惹人注目。

ex.en: The advertisements were all posted in a conspicuous place.
ex.cn: 广告都贴在了显眼的地方。

ex.en: The event was a conspicuous success (= a very great one).
ex.cn: 这项活动至为成功。

senses.def: not present in a situation or place, when it is obvious that you should be there
senses.chn: （本应在场）因缺席而招人注意

ex.en: When it came to cleaning up afterwards, Anne was conspicuous by her absence.
ex.cn: 后来到打扫时，本应在场的安妮却因为不在而引起了注意。

senses.def: not present in a situation or place, when it is obvious that you should be there
senses.chn: （本应在场）因缺席而招人注意

ex.en: When it came to cleaning up afterwards, Anne was conspicuous by her absence.
ex.cn: 后来到打扫时，本应在场的安妮却因为不在而引起了注意。

senses.def: the buying of expensive goods in order to impress people and show them how rich you are
senses.chn: 夸耀性消费；炫耀性购买

senses.def: a secret plan by a group of people to do sth harmful or illegal

ex.en: a conspiracy to overthrow the government
ex.cn: 颠覆政府的阴谋

ex.en: conspiracies against the president
ex.cn: 反对总统的阴谋诡计

ex.en: They were charged with conspiracy to murder.
ex.cn: 他们被指控秘密策划谋杀。

ex.en: a conspiracy of silence (= an agreement not to talk publicly about sth which should be made public)
ex.cn: 保持缄默的密约（对该公开的事情不公开谈论的约定）

ex.en: a conspiracy theory (= the belief that a secret conspiracy is responsible for a particular event)
ex.cn: 阴谋论（认为某事件背后有阴谋）

senses.def: a person who is involved in a conspiracy
connected with, or like, a conspiracy
senses.chn: 阴谋的；密谋的；似阴谋的

senses.def: suggesting that a secret is being shared

ex.en: 'I know you understand,' he said and gave a conspiratorial wink.
ex.cn: “我知道你明白。” 他说道，会意地眨一眨眼。

senses.def: to secretly plan with other people to do sth illegal or harmful

ex.en: They were accused of conspiring against the king.
ex.cn: 他们被指控密谋反对国王。

ex.en: They deny conspiring together to smuggle drugs.
ex.cn: 他们否认共谋走私毒品。

ex.en: She admitted conspiring with her lover to murder her husband.
ex.cn: 她承认与情夫密谋杀害亲夫。

senses.def: to seem to work together to make sth bad happen
senses.chn: 似乎共同导致（不良后果）

ex.en: Circumstances had conspired against them.
ex.cn: 各种情况都凑在一起和他们作对。

ex.en: Everything conspired to make her life a misery.
ex.cn: 她事事不顺，生活悲惨。

senses.def: a peace officer with some of the powers of a police officer, typically in a small town
senses.chn: （通常指小城镇的）警员，治安官

senses.def: (in Britain) the police force of a particular area or town
senses.chn: （英国某地区或城镇的）警察部队

senses.def: the quality of staying the same and not changing
senses.chn: 稳定性；持久不变；始终如一

senses.def: the quality of being faithful

ex.en: He admired her courage and constancy.
ex.cn: 他钦佩她的勇气和忠贞。

senses.def: happening all the time or repeatedly
senses.chn: 连续发生的；不断的；重复的

ex.en: constant interruptions
ex.cn: 无休止的干扰

ex.en: a constant stream of visitors all day
ex.cn: 整天络绎不绝的游客

ex.en: Babies need constant attention.
ex.cn: 婴儿一刻也离不开人。

ex.en: This entrance is in constant use.
ex.cn: 此入口经常使用。

senses.def: that does not change

ex.en: travelling at a constant speed of 50 m.p.h.
ex.cn: 以每小时 50 英里的速度匀速行驶

senses.def: a number or quantity that does not vary
all the time; repeatedly

ex.en: Fashion is constantly changing.
ex.cn: 时尚总是日新月异。

ex.en: Heat the sauce, stirring constantly.
ex.cn: 加热调味汁并不停地搅动。

senses.def: stating that sth is real or true
a group of stars that forms a shape in the sky and has a name
a group of related ideas, things or people
senses.chn: 一系列（相关的想法、事物）；一群（相关的人）

ex.en: a constellation of Hollywood talent
ex.cn: 一群好莱坞天才

senses.def: a worried, sad feeling after you have received an unpleasant surprise

ex.en: The announcement of her retirement caused consternation among tennis fans.
ex.cn: 她宣布挂拍告退的消息引起了网球迷的震惊。

senses.def: unable to get rid of waste material from the bowels easily
the condition of being unable to get rid of waste material from the bowels easily (= being constipated )
a district that elects its own representative to parliament

ex.en: Unemployment is high in her constituency.
ex.cn: 她的选区的失业人数居高不下。

ex.en: He owns a house in his Darlington constituency.
ex.cn: 他在自己的选区达灵顿拥有一座房子。

senses.def: the people who live in and vote in a particular district

ex.en: constituency opinion
ex.cn: 选区选民的意见

senses.def: a particular group of people in society who are likely to support a person, an idea or a product
a person who lives, and can vote in a constituency

ex.en: She has the full support of her constituents.
ex.cn: 她得到本区选民的全力支持。

senses.def: one of the parts of sth that combine to form the whole
forming or helping to make a whole

ex.en: to break something up into its constituent parts/elements
ex.cn: 把某物分离为各个组成部分／要素

senses.def: a group of elected representatives with the power to make or change a country's constitution
senses.chn: 立宪会议（有权制定或修改国家宪法）

senses.def: to be considered to be sth

ex.en: Does such an activity constitute a criminal offence?
ex.cn: 难道这样的活动也算刑事犯罪吗？

ex.en: The increase in racial tension constitutes a threat to our society.
ex.cn: 种族间紧张状态的升级是对我们社会的一种威胁。

senses.def: to be the parts that together form sth

ex.en: Female workers constitute the majority of the labour force.
ex.cn: 女性雇员占劳动力的多数。

ex.en: Their diet consists largely of vegetables.
ex.cn: 他们的日常饮食以蔬菜为主。

ex.en: The collection comprises 327 paintings.
ex.cn: 这组收藏有 327 幅画。

ex.en: Older people comprise a large proportion of those living in poverty.
ex.cn: 在那些生活贫困的人中，老年人占很大的比例。

ex.en: Women make up 56% of the student numbers.
